creator: Yiqin Deng, Shujun Zang, Ziyang Lin, Liwen Xu, Changhong Cheng, Juan Feng
description: Hfq is a global regulator and can be involved in multiple cellular processes by assisting small regulatory RNAs (sRNAs) to target mRNAs. To gain insight into the virulence regulation of Hfq in Vibrio harveyi, the hfq null mutant, ∆hfq, was constructed in V. harveyi strain 345.

title: Using Machine Learning to Predict Genes Underlying Differentiation of Multipartite and Unipartite Traits in Bacteria
creator: Fatemah Almalki, Janak Sunuwar, Rajeev K. Azad
description: Since the discovery of the second chromosome in the Rhodobacter sphaeroides 2.4.1 by Suwanto and Kaplan in 1989 and the revelation of gene sequences, multipartite genomes have been reported in over three hundred bacterial species under nine different phyla. This phenomenon shattered the dogma of a unipartite genome (a single circular chromosome) in bacteria.

title: The nuclear magneto-electric response of a chiral molecule via molecular dynamics in a time-dependent electric field
creator: Mateusz A. Słowiński, Juha Vaara, Piotr Garbacz
description: A chiral molecule with a permanent electric dipole moment aligns partially in an external electric field, preventing antisymmetric nuclear spin interactions from averaging out. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to investigate two such interactions – antisymmetric nuclear magnetic shielding and indirect spin–spin coupling in the light fluorinated alcohol, 1,1,1-trifluoropropan-2-ol.

title: Label-free 4D holotomography with depth-adaptive segmentation for quantitative analysis of lipid droplet dynamics in hepatic organoids
creator: Jimin Cho, Hoyeon Lee, ChulMin Oh, Juyeon Park, Sujin Park, Bon-Kyoung Koo, YongKeun Park
description: .SignificanceQuantifying lipid droplet (LD) remodeling in 3D hepatic organoids is often limited to endpoint staining or phototoxic live fluorescence imaging, thereby obscuring droplet-level kinetics.AimWe aimed to develop a label-free method to track LD dynamics in living hepatic organoids under different fatty-acid loads.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Diagnostic Prediction of Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome and Rickettsiosis in the Co-Endemic Wakayama Prefecture, Japan
creator: Kan Teramoto, Shinobu Tamura, Kikuaki Yoshida, Yukari Inada, Yusuke Yamashita, Masaya Morimoto, Toshiki Mushino, Daisuke Koreeda, Kyohei Miyamoto, Nobuhiro Komiya, Yoshio Nakano, Yusaku Takagaki, Yusuke Koizumi, Iosif Marincu
description: Background and Objectives: The Wakayama prefecture is endemic for two types of tick-borne rickettsioses: Japanese spotted fever (JFS) and scrub typhus (ST). Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne hemorrhagic viral disease with a high mortality rate and is often difficult to differentiate from such rickettsioses. SFTS cases have recently increased in Wakayama prefecture.

title: A computational framework to predict the spreading of Alzheimer’s disease
creator: Ana Vazquez-Palomo, Covadonga Betegón, Johannes Weickenmeier, Emilio Martínez-Pañeda
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Alzheimer’s disease is characterised by the spreading of misfolded proteins and progressive structural changes in the brain. Despite significant clinical research, understanding how microscopic protein dynamics translate into macroscopic tissue degeneration remains a major challenge. In this work, we present a three-dimensional, finite element-based computational framework to model disease progression by combining multi-protein transport and brain tissue deformation within anatomically realistic geometries.

title: Abortion law in the Crown Dependencies: liberalisation in the UK’s small, independent neighbours
creator: Jordan A Parsons, Alexandra Mullock
description: There has been significant exploration of UK abortion law variation in recent years. However, this comparative research has not extended to the neighbouring Crown Dependencies. The Isle of Man, Guernsey, and Jersey operate in unusual constitutional contexts, with more autonomy than the UK’s devolved nations. Whilst they often match UK policy in many areas, this is not automatic.

title: Home-based transcutaneous electrical acupuncture-point stimulation for depressive symptoms in inflammatory bowel disease: a randomized feasibility study
creator: Chongwen Huang, Wladyslawa Czuber-Dochan, Christine Norton
description: BackgroundDepressive symptoms are common in individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and are associated with poor disease outcomes. Transcutaneous electrical acupuncture point stimulation (TEAS) is a noninvasive intervention with potential benefits for inflammation but remains untested in IBD. We developed a smartphone application for home-based TEAS self-administration and evaluated its feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects.

title: The Impact of Warming on Assembly Processes and Diversity Patterns of Bacterial Communities in Mesocosms
creator: Qian Yang, Yifeng Yan, Jinhe Huang, Zhaolei Wang, Mingjun Feng, Haowu Cheng, Peiyu Zhang, Huan Zhang, Jun Xu, Min Zhang
description: Bacteria in lake water bodies and sediments play crucial roles in various biogeochemical processes. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of bacterioplankton and sedimentary bacteria community composition and assembly processes across multiple seasons in 18 outdoor mesocosms exposed to three temperature scenarios.

title: Executive summary: Workshop on preterm birth, January 28–29, 2025, co‐sponsored by the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development
creator: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine (SMFM), Rupsa Boelig, Andrea Edlow, Tracy Manuck, Eva Pajkrt, Ina A Stelzer, Sarahn Wheeler, Cynthia Gyamfi‐Bannerman
description: The Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine collaborated with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development at the National Institutes of Health to co‐sponsor the annual SMFM President's Workshop on preterm birth.

title: cGAS-STING信号通路调控中枢神经炎症性疾病的分子机制及干预策略
creator: Xinyuan YU, Song YAO, Pinglong XU, Ailian WANG, 敏 沈, 方 余
description: cGAS-STING信号通路是细胞感知异常DNA并触发Ⅰ型干扰素和炎症反应的重要途径。在多种中枢神经系统疾病中，线粒体损伤释放线粒体DNA、核DNA损伤、溶酶体破裂及细胞死亡相关DNA外泄等事件，可在小胶质细胞、星形胶质细胞及部分神经元中激活cGAS-STING信号通路，从而驱动干扰素调节因子3及核因子κB等转录程序，并与自噬及细胞命运变化交联，启动并放大神经炎症，加速神经功能受损。本文围绕DNA来源、信号机制、细胞命运改变、病理结局的总体框架，归纳cGAS-STING信号通路在阿尔茨海默病、帕金森病、缺血性脑卒中及多发性硬化等病理中的机制，介绍cGAS或STING小分子抑制剂、转录轴阻断及靶向递送等干预技术，为cGAS-STING靶向的神经炎症性疾病干预提供思路。Keywords: 神经退行性变性疾病, cGAS-STING信号通路, 天然免疫, 神经炎症, 综述 神经炎症是中枢神经系统对感染、损伤等病理刺激产生的一种免疫应答 ［ 1］，作为创伤性脑损伤、脑卒中等急性损伤和阿尔茨海默病、帕金森病、肌萎缩侧索硬化等慢性退行性变性疾病的共同病理特征 ［ 2- 3］，在神经系统疾病中具有重要作用。神经炎症的典型表现包括小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞活化，以及外周免疫细胞向中枢神经系统浸润 ［ 4］。这一免疫应答本是机体的防御和修复机制，然而在慢性病程中这一过程往往失调，转变为持续存在的病理状态，进而引发血脑屏障破坏、髓鞘脱失、突触丢失等，最终导致神经元不可逆死亡 ［ 3- 4］。 十九世纪初，大脑一度被认为是“免疫豁免”器官，随着科学发展，这一观点已经修正 ［ 5］。神经炎症的主要执行者小胶质细胞是大脑天然免疫系统的主要细胞类型，且大脑中其他类型细胞如星形胶质细胞、神经元、内皮细胞等均表达模式识别受体。这些模式识别受体能特异性识别由组织损伤或蛋白质稳态失衡释放的内源性损伤相关分子模式，从而自主启动并持续驱动神经炎症反应 ［ 6］。这一由中枢神经系统常驻细胞主导的天然免疫激活不仅构成了神经炎症的初始环节，更通过复杂的信号间交互作用招募适应性免疫细胞浸润，共同形成并维持慢性促炎微环境，最终诱发神经元损伤和功能障碍。 近年研究表明，cGAS-STING信号通路与多种神经系统疾病的发生发展密切相关。作为天然免疫的关键组成部分，cGAS-STING信号通路主导了对细胞质异常dsDNA的免疫响应，诱导Ⅰ型干扰素和多种促炎性细胞因子产生并触发下游炎症通路 ［ 2- 3， 7］。当cGAS识别细胞质中异常的dsDNA后，会利用鸟苷三磷酸和腺苷三磷酸合成cGAMP；cGAMP与内质网膜上的STING二聚体结合触发STING构象改变并激活；活化的STING随后从内质网经内质网-高尔基体中间体转运至高尔基体，在此过程中发生寡聚化并招募TBK1；寡聚化的TBK1发生自磷酸化，进而磷酸化STING的羧基端尾巴，为转录因子IRF3提供锚定位点；被招募至STING-TBK1复合体的IRF3经TBK1磷酸化激活后形成二聚体入核，与核因子κB等转录因子协同调控Ⅰ/Ⅲ型干扰素、趋化因子及促炎性细胞因子等的表达，从而建立起机体的免疫防御态势。 ［ 8- 9］ 除上述cGAS-STING经典通路外，STING还具有多种非经典功能，包括在内质网促进蛋白激酶R样内质网激酶激活以调控蛋白质翻译、在内质网-高尔基体中间体及后高尔基体囊泡上介导非经典自噬的起始以及微管相关蛋白轻链3等关键自噬相关蛋白质脂化。研究发现，STING具有质子通道活性，不仅对于诱导非经典自噬具有重要作用，也有助于激活转录因子EB家族成员以促进溶酶体生成及调节高尔基体的细胞因子转运 ［ 10- 13］。 值得注意的是，DNA异常定位是多种中枢神经系统疾病的共性，线粒体或细胞核泄漏的dsDNA通过激活cGAS-STING信号通路诱发神经炎症 ［ 7］。然而，该通路在中枢神经系统中的作用复杂且具有情境依赖性，使得精确、安全有效的干预颇具挑战性。本文通过回顾cGAS-STING信号通路在中枢神经系统疾病中的最新研究进展，重点探讨其在疾病进程中调控神经炎症的多重作用机制及潜在治疗策略，以期为未来研究提供清晰的认知框架，并为临床转化提供更全面的视角。 cGAS-STING信号通路在中枢神经系统疾病中的调控机制 cGAS-STING信号通路在神经系统中具有重要的病理调控作用，其异常激活并通过诱导Ⅰ型干扰素及炎症反应驱动神经炎症和神经退行性变性。尽管不同疾病的致病因素存在差异，但它们往往通过染色体损伤、线粒体损伤、溶酶体功能异常等共同的应激途径导致细胞质dsDNA积累，从而激活cGAS-STING信号通路并放大神经炎症反应，驱动神经元死亡。 阿尔茨海默病 阿尔茨海默病是最常见的神经退行性疾病，其典型病理特征包括Aβ沉积和神经元内高度磷酸化的τ蛋白聚集形成神经原纤维缠结。长期以来，这些蛋白质聚集被认为是神经元损伤和认知障碍的核心驱动因素。然而，近年来越来越多的证据表明慢性神经炎症在阿尔茨海默病病程中发挥重要作用，而cGAS-STING信号通路可能是连接多种病理刺激与炎症反应的重要分子枢纽。 阿尔茨海默病中典型的蛋白质聚集病理能够直接或间接触发天然免疫信号。研究发现，外源性τ蛋白可被PQBP1感知，进而激活小胶质细胞中cGAS-STING信号通路以介导核因子κB入核并诱导炎症因子转录 ［ 14- 15］。PQBP1属于固有无序蛋白，具有相分离的潜能，鉴于cGAS已被证实能够发生相分离，PQBP1与cGAS的相互作用是否通过相分离介导并调控下游反应有待深入研究 ［ 16- 17］。与此同时，Aβ沉积可以激活神经元及胶质细胞中的cGAS，尤其是在小胶质细胞中引发Ⅰ型干扰素反应。遗传性敲除 Cgas或应用STING抑制剂均可显著改善5×FAD小鼠模型中的Aβ沉积及神经炎症。值得注意的是，小胶质细胞特异性缺失 Cgas不仅抑制了STING，还可减少星形胶质细胞向神经毒性A1表型转化，从而缓解寡聚Aβ诱导的神经元损伤 ［ 18］。这些研究提示，蛋白质聚集兼具神经毒性结构损伤和损伤相关分子模式介导的STING免疫激活双重病理效应。进一步研究表明，线粒体功能障碍可能是连接蛋白质聚集与cGAS-STING信号通路激活的重要中介事件：τ蛋白和Aβ均可诱导线粒体损伤和氧化应激，导致线粒体膜完整性被破坏并促进mtDNA释放至细胞质，进而激活小胶质细胞中的cGAS-STING信号通路，促进炎症、突触丢失及认知功能下降 ［ 19- 21］。此外，APP/PS1突变转基因小鼠体内重要的代谢产物烟酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸水平降低，伴随炎症、mtDNA损伤和细胞衰老增加，以及cGAS、STING蛋白质水平上升，而使用烟酰胺核苷进行补充治疗可提高脑组织中烟酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸水平，显著抑制cGAS-STING信号通路依赖的神经炎症和细胞衰老 ［ 22］。因此，mtDNA释放可能是阿尔茨海默病中cGAS-STING信号通路持续激活的重要来源之一。 除mtDNA释放增加外，细胞质DNA清除能力下降也可能维持STING慢性激活。在阿尔茨海默病小鼠胶质细胞中DNase Ⅱ下调，由于dsDNA是阿尔茨海默病中cGAS-STING信号通路激活的主要原因，DNase Ⅱ缺乏影响了细胞质dsDNA清除，通过cGAS-STING信号通路进一步加重了阿尔茨海默病中Aβ沉积、τ蛋白聚集、神经炎症及认知障碍

title: Research of Multicopper Oxidase and Its Degradation of Histamine in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LPZN19
creator: Huijie Pei, Yilun Wang, Wei He, Lin Deng, Qinjie Lan, Yue Zhang, Lamei Yang, Kaidi Hu, Jianlong Li, Aiping Liu, Xiaolin Ao, Hui Teng, Shuliang Liu, Likou Zou, Ran Li, Yong Yang
description: In order to explore the structural changes and products of histamine degradation by multicopper oxidase (MCO) in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LPZN19, a 1500 bp MCO gene in L. plantarum LPZN19 was cloned, and the recombinant MCO was expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3).

title: Comparison of Wear Resistance of Overlay Welded Layers and Thermal Sprayed Coatings in Real Conditions
creator: Michał Szymura, Grzegorz Gąsiorek, Artur Czupryński, Waldemar Kwaśny, Viktor Kvasnytskyi
description: Tribological tests in real conditions enable obtaining full data on the life of interacting machine parts. This article presents the results of operational tests on the elements of the support ring guidance system in a vertical ball-race mill. The guide and active armour operate under abrasive wear conditions with moderate-impact loads.

title: Effects of Increasing the Orthodontic Forces over Cortical and Trabecular Bone during Periodontal Breakdown—A Finite Elements Analysis
creator: Radu-Andrei Moga, Cristian Doru Olteanu, Mircea Daniel Botez, Stefan Marius Buru, Ada Gabriela Delean, Gaetano Isola
description: Background and Objectives: Herein we used numerical analysis to study different biomechanical behaviors of mandibular bone subjected to 0.6 N, 1.2 N, and 2.4 N orthodontic loads during 0–8 mm periodontal breakdown using the Tresca failure criterion. Additionally, correlations with earlier FEA reports found potential ischemic and resorptive risks.

title: Characteristics and Degradation Mechanisms under High Reverse Base–Collector Bias Stress in InGaAs/InP Double HBTs
creator: Silu Yan, Hongliang Lu, Lin Cheng, Jiantao Qiao, Wei Cheng, Yuming Zhang
description: In this paper, the reliability of InP/InGaAs DHBTs under high reverse base–collector bias stress is analyzed by experiments and simulation. The DC characteristics and S parameters of the devices under different stress times were measured, and the key parameters with high field stress were also extracted to fully understand and analyze the high-field degradation mechanism of devices.

title: Mean Diffusivity of the Left Caudal Anterior Cingulate Cortex and Past Major Depressive Disorder in Adolescents: Evidence from the ABCD Study
creator: Shervin Assari, Alexandra Donovan, Babak Najand, Golnoush Akhlaghipour, Mario F Mendez
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Adolescence is a critical developmental stage for the emergence of major depressive disorder (MDD). Structural and diffusion neuroimaging studies have highlighted the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) as a key region implicated in emotion regulation, stress reactivity, and mood processing.

title: Locally deployed large language model for real‐world lecanemab eligibility pre‐screening
creator: Carolin Miklitz, Maya Shrestha, Wegner Philipp, Nils Henk, Alois Martin Sprinkart, Wolfgang Block, Julian Alexander Luetkens, Alexander Radbruch, Nils Christian Lehnen, Sebastian Nowak
description: INTRODUCTIONThe introduction of disease‐modifying Alzheimer's therapies requires complex, labor‐intensive patient screening. Cloud‐based large language models (LLMs) could support this task but are often unsuitable for routine care due to data protection constraints.METHODSWe evaluated an on‐premises, open‐weights LLM (gpt‐oss‐120b) for automated extraction of therapy‐relevant variables for lecanemab eligibility from German memory clinic reports.

title: Lighting the Way: Anita Mahadevan-Jansen’s Journey Through Biophotonics and Beyond
creator: Darren Roblyer
description: .Anita Mahadevan-Jansen discusses her experiences of discovery and translation in biophotonics. The interview highlights her groundbreaking research as well as her impact as a mentor and leader in biomedical optics. Anita Mahdevan-Jansen (left), Orrin H. Ingram Chair in Biomedical Engineering at Vanderbilt University, discusses translation and discovery in biophotonics with Biophotonics Discovery Editor-in-Chief Darren Roblyer (right).

title: Delayed Metal Hypersensitivity from Surgical Clips Causing Progressive Neuropathy
creator: Satyamedha Bathula, Oluwasegun J. Olowe, Amanda Lalama, Krystal Virk, Alejandro Pena, Frederick Tiesenga
description: Introduction:Systemic immune reactions to surgical clips or implants remain underrecognized and pose a diagnostic challenge after minimally invasive surgeries. Although the incidence of metal hypersensitivity is increasing, these reactions are often overlooked because postoperative imaging and routine evaluations are frequently unremarkable.

title: LAYLA: development of a comprehensive and cross-sample program for detecting structural variants and its application to citrus cultivars
creator: Tomoaki Watanabe, Tomoko Endo, Yoshihiro Kawahara, Kenta Shirasawa, Keisuke Nonaka, Sachiko Isobe, Takehiko Shimada, Shingo Goto, Hiroshi Fujii
description: Structural variants (SVs) are genomic mutations that are typically 50 bp or larger. Given their larger scale compared to single nucleotide polymorphisms and small insertions and deletions, SVs are expected to be associated with various traits in several crops and fruit species. They can also be used to identify plant cultivars.

title: High-Value Oil–Water Separation Materials Prepared from Waste Polyethylene Terephthalate
creator: Changjian Zhou, Jiahao Zhang, Yuqing Fu, Maowan Wu, Heng Zhang, Qingle Shi, Yong Dai, He Zhao, Katarzyna Lewandowska
description: As one of the most common forms of waste, waste PET is a serious pollutant in natural and human living environments. There is an urgent need to recycle PET. For this study, the complete degradation of PET was realized at a low temperature.

title: Correction to: Degradation of helicase-like transcription factor (HLTF) by ß-TrCP promotes hepatocarcinogenesis via activation of the p62/mTOR axis
creator: Unknown
description: 2023, mjad012, https://doi.org/10.1093/jmcb/mjad012 Following the online publication of this article, the authors identified two figure errors within the Results section. The corrected figures are detailed below: In Figure 2E (Huh7 cell invasion assay), the siControl image partially overlaps with the siControl invasion image shown in Figure 4I. This error arose during figure assembly.

title: Electrical Characteristics of 3D Trench Electrode Germanium Detector with Nested Complementary Cathodes
creator: Mingyang Wang, Zheng Li, Bo Xiong, Yongguang Xiao
description: High-purity germanium detectors, widely employed in fields such as aerospace applications based on radiation detection principles, have garnered attention due to their broad detection range and fast response time. However, these detectors often require larger sensitive area volumes to achieve larger signals and higher detection efficiency.

title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation of Executive Function Performance Test (EFPT): ACOSMIN Systematic Review
creator: Sama Rasouli Osalo, Armin Zareiyan, Mehdi Rezaee, Monire Nobahar Ahari
description: BackgroundPsychometrics plays a crucial role in cross-cultural research, necessitating the adaptation of scales for measuring health status. As the Executive Function Performance Test measures functional cognition and can be helpful in medical, rehabilitation, and research settings, this review aims to methodologically review cross-culturally adapted versions of the Executive Function Performance Test using the COSMIN checklist.

title: Cinacalcet and Parathyroidectomy Outcomes in Symptomatic and Asymptomatic Primary Hyperparathyroidism: A Retrospective Observational Study
creator: Aditya Dutta, Praphulla Koirala, Nupoor Vaghasia, Kajal Allawadi, Ambrish Mithal
description: Introduction:Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is a common and symptomatic endocrine disorder in India. There has been a notable rise in asymptomatic PHPT (urban India), creating a dilemma in optimal treatment approach—surgery or medical management. Cinacalcet is a calcimimetic used in managing PHPT, but data regarding its use from India is limited.

title: Effects of Block Copolymer Terminal Groups on Toughening Epoxy-Based Composites: Microstructures and Toughening Mechanisms
creator: Gang Li, Wenjie Wu, Xuecheng Yu, Ruoyu Zhang, Rong Sun, Liqiang Cao, Pengli Zhu
description: Despite the considerable research attention paid to block copolymer (BCP)-toughened epoxy resins, the effects of their terminal groups on their phase structure are not thoroughly understood. This study fills this gap by closely examining the effects of amino and carboxyl groups on the fracture toughness of epoxy resins at different temperatures.

title: Study on the Internal Stress and Thermal Anisotropy in Magnesium Alloys Using a Thermal Elastic Viscoplastic Self-Consistent Model
creator: Xianyun Zhu, Huamiao Wang, Yunxin Wu
description: A thermal elastic viscoplastic self-consistent model is utilized to examine the thermal stress induced by the thermal anisotropy of single crystals during heat treatments. This model considers temperature-dependent elastic constants and critical resolved shear stress associated with thermal dilation. Simulation results demonstrate that under cooling, the elastic lattice strain increases significantly when constrained compared to unconstrained cooling.

title: Research advances in intelligent microenvironment-responsive hydrogels for myocardial infarction therapy
creator: Jian Li, Jinglin Gao, Kaiyi Zhu, Yuping Gao
description: Myocardial infarction (MI) poses a severe threat to human life and health. During acute MI, persistent myocardial ischemia and hypoxia induce pathological alterations in the microenvironment. Traditional therapeutic approaches exhibit limited capacity for targeted modulation of this infarcted microenvironment. Consequently, developing therapeutic strategies capable of precisely responding to the pathological microenvironment holds significant importance.

title: Fatty Acid-Binding Proteins Identification during the Evolution of Metabolic Syndrome: A Raman Spectroscopy-Based Approach
creator: Guadalupe Donjuán-Loredo, Ricardo Espinosa-Tanguma, Edgar Guevara, María del Carmen Rodríguez-Aranda, Fabiola León-Bejarano, Karen Hernández-Vidales, Miguel Ramírez-Elías, Ivo Piantanida
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Excess fat in abdominal deposits is a risk factor for multiple conditions, including metabolic syndrome (MetS); lipid metabolism plays an essential role in these pathologies; fatty acid-binding proteins (FABPs) are dedicated to the cytosolic transport of fat. FABP4, whose primary source is adipose tissue, is released into the circulation, acting as an adipokine, while FABP5 also accompanies the adverse effects of MetS. FABP4 and 5 are potential biomarkers of MetS, but their behavior during syndrome evolution has not been determined.

title: Efficacy of Dapagliflozin vs. Saroglitazar on Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis in Patients of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Metabolic-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)
creator: Bijay K. Das, Sambit Das, Dayanidhi Meher, Arun K. Choudhury, Sourav Padhee, Sandeep K. Sahu, Devadarshini Sahoo, Binod Prusty, Vishal Agarwal
description: Introduction:There is a rising prevalence of metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), particularly in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, which needs early detection and treatment to prevent the grave outcomes. Dapagliflozin and Saroglitazar are known to improve metabolic and liver health in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Fluorinated Polymers for Hydrovoltaic Energy Harvesting: Mechanisms and Multifunctional Integration
creator: Seungjae Lee, Changwoo Nam
description: Hydrovoltaic energy harvesting converts interactions at water–solid interfaces into electricity through capacitive discharge, streaming, and diffusion. Fluorinated polymers such as poly­(tetrafluoroethylene) (PTFE), fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP), and poly­(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) are central to these processes owing to their high electronegativity, hydrophobicity, and chemical stability. These materials facilitate charge separation and storage while offering structural versatility for device fabrication.

title: Abaloparatide Increases Distal Femur Bone Mineral Density Post-Total Knee Arthroplasty
creator: Brian Nickel, Diane Krueger, Gretta Borchardt, Samuel Mosiman, Paul A. Anderson, Neil Binkley
description: Background:Osteoporosis is common in joint replacement patients and increases adverse outcome risk. Data indicate that total knee arthroplasty (TKA) causes distal femur bone loss. We hypothesized that abaloparatide (ABL) would mitigate this loss. The study’s purpose was to evaluate the effect of ABL initiated before TKA on distal femur bone mineral density (BMD) in osteoporotic patients.

title: Optimal Number of Practice Trials for Balance and Hop Tests in Individuals with Chronic Ankle Instability
creator: Min Jun Kim, Jordan Read, Hongsuk Lee, J. Ty Hopkins, S. Jun Son
description: BackgroundStatic and dynamic balance tests and hop tests are widely used to assess lower extremity function; however, scientific evidence regarding the optimal number of practice trials remains limited.PurposeTo determine the number of practice trials necessary to achieve consistent performance on static and dynamic balance tests and hop tests in males and females.

title: Hypertonic saline versus Lactated Ringer’s Solution for neurological recovery in cats with traumatic brain injury
creator: Aiden Pang
description: PICO questionIn cats with traumatic brain injury, is hypertonic saline more effective than Lactated Ringer’s Solution (LRS), when measuring neurological recovery?In dogs diagnosed with canine transmissible venereal tumour (CTVT), does treatment with vincristine combined with ivermectin, compared to treatment with vincristine alone, lead to improved clinical outcomes?Clinical bottom lineCategory of researchTreatment.Number and type of study designs reviewedZero.Strength of evidenceZero.

title: Drip Loss During Strawberry Thawing: A Simple Method for Predicting and Improving the Colour Stability of Nectars
creator: Helen Murray, Jhoan-Sebastian Rincon-Berbeo, Kristýna Šimková, Marlene Lindner, Carine Le Bourvellec, Jerneja Jakopič, Heidrun Halbwirth, Manfred Gössinger
description: Drip loss is the liquid released from frozen strawberries during defrosting. High levels of drip loss make strawberries unsuitable for many applications that require whole fruit. This study is aimed at investigating the relationship between strawberry drip loss and the colour stability of nectars produced from these strawberries.

title: Impact of cervical lymph node dissection on accessory spinal nerve XI function: Case series and literature review
creator: Saout Arrih Badr, Bijou Walid, Oukessou Youssef, Rouadi Sami, Abada Reda, Mahtar Mohamed
description: IntroductionCervical lymph node dissection can damage the accessory spinal nerve, causing motor and pain disorders. This study evaluates the impact of these lesions and investigates the associated risk factors.MethodsProspective study of 29 patients who underwent cervical lymph node dissection. Assessment of accessory spinal nerve function was performed by clinical examination and electromyogram on day 28 and 6 months post-operatively.

title: Distinct value-modulated connectomic signatures during monetary incentive anticipation predict severity and craving in internet gaming disorder
creator: Zifeng Wang, Guangdong Zhou, Yifan Liu, Yuchen Huang, Taoyu Wu, Shiqiu Meng, Chengyao Qian, Yan Sun
description: BackgroundInternet gaming disorder (IGD) involves dysregulated incentive processing, yet precise neural substrates remain inconsistent. While the Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task assesses reward systems, traditional analyses conflate reward valence (Value) and motivational salience, masking process-specific neural alterations. This study evaluated which neural features—from localized activity to large-scale connectivity—most effectively characterize IGD clinical phenotypes.

title: The Role of miRNA in Testicular Cancer: Current Insights and Future Perspectives
creator: Francesco Ditonno, Antonio Franco, Celeste Manfredi, Daniela Fasanella, Marco Abate, Roberto La Rocca, Fabio Crocerossa, Vincenzo Iossa, Ugo Giovanni Falagario, Luigi Cirillo, Vincenzo Maria Altieri, Ernesto Di Mauro, Felice Crocetto, Biagio Barone, Simone Cilio, Savio Domenico Pandolfo, Achille Ave
description: Background and Objectives: Despite advancements in the diagnosis and treatment of testicular germ cell tumours (TGTCs), challenges persist in identifying reliable biomarkers for early detection and precise disease management. This narrative review addresses the role of microRNAs (miRNAs) as potential diagnostic tools and therapeutic targets in the treatment of TGCTs.

title: A Numerical Study of the Dynamic Crack Behavior of Brittle Material Induced by Blast Waves
creator: Haijun Yu, Ming Zou, Jinshan Sun, Yuntao Wang, Meng Wang, Oldrich Sucharda
description: Blast stress waves profoundly impact engineering structures, exciting and affecting the rupture process in brittle construction materials. A novel numerical model was introduced to investigate the initiation and propagation of cracks subjected to blast stress waves within the borehole-crack configuration. Twelve models were established with different crack lengths to simulate sandstone samples.

title: Right ventricular-protective ventilation in acute respiratory distress syndrome: phenotypes, monitoring and ventilatory management
creator: Chengchao Peng, Le Yang, Yongran Wu, You Shang, Xiaojing Zou
description: Despite the widespread implementation of lung-protective ventilation, mortality in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains substantial, underscoring the importance of extrapulmonary determinants of outcome. Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is recognised as a frequent and clinically meaningful complication of ARDS, affecting a sizeable proportion of patients and consistently associated with adverse outcomes.

title: Further Association of Germline CHEK2 Loss-of-Function Variants with Testicular Germ Cell Tumors
creator: Kira Kirchner, Christoph Seidel, Finn-Ole Paulsen, Bianca Sievers, Carsten Bokemeyer, Davor Lessel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs) represent the most frequent malignancy in young adult men and have one the highest heritability rates among all cancers. A recent multicenter case–control study identified CHEK2 as the first moderate-penetrance TGCT predisposition gene. Here, we analyzed CHEK2 in 129 TGCT cases unselected for age of onset, histology, clinical outcome, and family history of any cancer, and the frequency of identified variants was compared to findings in 27,173 ancestry-matched cancer-free men.

title: Arrhythmias in Patients with Congenital Heart Disease: An Ongoing Morbidity
creator: Despoina Ntiloudi, Spyridon Rammos, Maria Karakosta, Alkistis Kalesi, Nearchos Kasinos, George Giannakoulas
description: With the aging of congenital heart disease (CHD) patients, the burden of arrhythmias is expanding. Atrial arrhythmias, especially intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia and atrial fibrillation, are the most prevalent forms of arrhythmia. Managing comorbidities, such as obesity, using pharmacotherapy, including antiarrhythmics and anticoagulants, and ablation therapy has become the cornerstone of arrhythmia management.

title: Animal‐ and Plant‐Source Protein‐Rich Foods Differ in Their Association With Maternal Micronutrient Status and Breast Milk Composition During Lactation
creator: Sofa Rahmannia, Gina Arena, Kevin Murray, Aly Diana, Lisa Houghton, Rosalind Gibson, Siobhan Hickling
description: Micronutrient deficiencies in lactating women remain widespread and under‐addressed, compromising maternal health and breast milk quality. Although dietary guidelines promote protein‐rich foods, most do not distinguish between animal and plant sources within this food group, despite differences in nutrient profiles and bioavailability.

title: Angina and Non-Obstructive Coronary Artery (ANOCA) Patients with Coronary Vasomotor Disorders
creator: Sarena La, Rosanna Tavella, Jing Wu, Sivabaskari Pasupathy, Christopher Zeitz, Matthew Worthley, Ajay Sinhal, Margaret Arstall, John A Spertus, John F Beltrame, Panagiota Anyfanti, Theodoros Dimitroulas
description: Angina and Non-Obstructive Coronary Artery (ANOCA) patients often lack a clear explanation for their symptoms, and are frequently discharged with the label of “unspecified chest pain”, despite the availability of functional coronary angiography (provocative spasm and microvascular function testing) to identify potential underlying coronary vasomotor disorders.

title: Greater deformation and lower stiffness, but similar ultimate failure strength with fixed‐loop cortical suspensory device compared to metal interference screw for femoral fixation of bone–patellar tendon–bone grafts in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
creator: Alexander Nagel Tandberg, Marek Zegzdryn, Jan‐Egil Brattgjerd, Gilbert Moatshe, Arne Kristian Aune
description: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to compare a contemporary fixed‐loop cortical suspensory devices (CSDs) with metal interference screws (IS) for femoral bone–patellar tendon–bone (BPTB) graft fixation in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR).MethodsSeven matched pairs of fresh‐frozen human cadaveric knees underwent anatomical ACLR with BPTB grafts. Femoral fixation was randomized to a fixed‐loop CSD or metal IS.

title: Fundus Albipunctatus Associated with Biallelic LRAT Gene Mutation: A Case Report with Long-Term Follow-Up
creator: Wendy D Tan, J Vernon Odom, Monique Leys, Yoshiaki Kiuchi, Kyung Chul Yoon
description: This case report presents a 26-year-old female patient diagnosed with fundus albipunctatus (FAP), a rare form of congenital stationary night blindness. The patient’s clinical history and retinal findings spanning 23 years are consistent with FAP. The patient has profound night blindness, photophobia, and mild color vision changes with preserved best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).

title: Case Analysis of Neonatal Acute Liver Failure Presumably Caused by Gestational Alloimmune Liver Disease
creator: Qingying Wang, Jingyi Zhang, Yi Xu, Xia Chen, Fang Huang, Jingjing Wu, Yongchao Jiang, Gaoyan Chen
description: Neonatal acute liver failure is a rare, life-threatening condition. We present a 33 6/7 -week-old neonate with severe coagulopathy and hyperbilirubinemia refractory to vitamin K 1 , plasma, and platelet transfusions. The mother had a history of two previous neonatal deaths, one of whom had similar coagulopathy.

title: The Association between the Platelet to White Blood Cell Ratio and Chronic Kidney Disease in an Aging Population: A Four-Year Follow-Up Study
creator: Yang Xiong, Qian Zhong, Yangchang Zhang, Feng Qin, Jiuhong Yuan, Bernard Canaud, Sylvia Stracke
description: Introduction: The platelet to white blood cell ratio (PWR) has been reported to be a prognostic factor for some diseases, such as subarachnoid hemorrhage. However, the association between the PWR and chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unknown. To investigate the cross-sectional and longitudinal association between the PWR and CKD, this study was performed.

title: The role of gene polymorphisms in infertility, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome and recurrent miscarriage in the Iranian women population: A review study
creator: Vida Hojati
description: More than 40% of infertility causes are attributed to women. Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is one of the important and common causes of infertility in women. Recurrent miscarriage is defined as the occurrence of 2 or 3 consecutive spontaneous miscarriages before the 20 th wk of pregnancy.

title: Effect of Segmented Optical Axial Length on the Performance of New-Generation Intraocular Lens Power Calculation Formulas in Extremely Long Eyes
creator: So Goto, Naoyuki Maeda, Kota Uehara, Keiko Ogawa, Maki Matsumaru, Saori Sugiyama, Kazuhiko Ohnuma, Tjundewo Lawu, Toru Noda
description: Purpose: To evaluate the performance of traditional vergence formulas with segmented axial length (AL) compared to traditional composite AL in extremely long eyes, and to determine whether the segmented AL can be extended to the new-generation formulas, including the Barrett Universal II, Emmetropia Verifying Optical 2.0 (EVO2), Hill-RBF 3.

title: Dramatic biases in terrestrial nitrogen fixation in Earth System Models revealed by natural isotope signatures
creator: Maoyuan Feng, Shushi Peng, Philippe Ciais, Daniel S Goll, Benjamin Z Houlton, Ying-Ping Wang, Yilong Wang, Pan Liu, Joshua B Fisher, Pierre Regnier
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) is the primary input of new reactive nitrogen to natural terrestrial ecosystems. However, this flux is poorly constrained due to its unclear drivers and associated control mechanisms. Here, we extend the existing theory of nitrogen (N) isotope mass balance to estimate BNF rates and then use a Bayesian approach to constrain the BNF rates in natural terrestrial ecosystems by using measurements of natural N-isotope ratios (δ15N) in plants (δP) and soil (δS).

title: Minimally Invasive Strategy to Repair Mitral Valve after Repeated Coronary Revascularization: A Case Report and Literature Review
creator: Laura Asta, Umberto Benedetto, Fabrizio Costantino Tancredi, Gabriele Di Giammarco, Johannes Maximilian Albes, Omer Dzemali
description: Redo cardiac surgery after Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) is burdened by high morbidity and mortality, either intraoperatively and postoperatively, with the repeated sternotomy playing a crucial role as risk factor. The right minithoracotomy approach guarantees a safer control on conduits integrity and the right ventricular wall and a low impact on the respiratory mechanics.

title: Exploring a novel voice-guided artificial intelligence platform for real-time colonoscopy documentation: a pilot study
creator: Mahsa Taghiakbari, Timothy Wong, Rohini Gaikar, Azar Azad, Robert Battat, Mickael Bouin, Benoit Panzini, Roupen Djinbachian, David Armstrong, Daniel von Renteln
description: BackgroundAccurate and consistent documentation during colonoscopy is essential for optimal patient care and therapeutic decisions. Traditional manual documentation is time-consuming and subject to variability. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tools offer potential improvements by standardizing report generation in real-time. We developed a novel AI-driven, voice-guided reporting platform that uses natural language processing (NLP) and real-time image capture for endoscopy documentation.

title: Mathematical Modeling of Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Biology through the Experimental Data on Cell Composition and Growth of Patient-Derived Organoids
creator: Rushan Sulimanov, Konstantin Koshelev, Vladimir Makarov, Alexandre Mezentsev, Mikhail Durymanov, Lilian Ismail, Komal Zahid, Yegor Rumyantsev, Ilya Laskov, Qian Du
description: Mathematical models of non-small-cell lung cancer are powerful tools that use clinical and experimental data to describe various aspects of tumorigenesis. The developed algorithms capture phenotypic changes in the tumor and predict changes in tumor behavior, drug resistance, and clinical outcomes of anti-cancer therapy.

title: Evolution of a Pathogenic Microbiome
creator: Pui Yin Wong, Carmen Yip, Daniel A Lemberg, Andrew S Day, Steven T Leach, Hidekazu Suzuki
description: The process of microbiome development arguably begins before birth. Vertical transmission of bacteria from the mother to the infant is a keystone event in microbiome development. Subsequent to birth, the developing microbiome is vulnerable to influence from a wide range of factors. Additionally, the microbiome can influence the health and development of the host infant.

title: Long‐Term Subcutaneous Treprostinil in Pediatric Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension at a Latin American Referral Center: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Angelo Valencia Salazar, Ernesto León Vallejo Mondragón
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension is a progressive vasculopathy with substantial early mortality. Subcutaneous treprostinil is an established prostacyclin‐pathway therapy for higher‐risk disease, but long‐term pediatric data from Latin American referral centers remain limited. This retrospective cohort included all nine consecutive children with World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension Group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension who initiated subcutaneous treprostinil at a Colombian referral center and were followed from diagnosis until death or last known contact.

title: Solitary adrenal metastasis presenting 15 years after breast cancer: a case report
creator: Salsabil Haque, Jamil Alghanem, Suven Shankar
description: Introduction and importance:Adrenal metastasis from breast cancer is exceptionally rare and typically arises within a few years of the primary diagnosis. We report a unique case of solitary adrenal metastasis presenting 15 years after breast carcinoma, with hypercalcemia as the only symptom.

title: Tocotrienol metabolites redirect lipid mediator production in innate immune cells towards inflammation resolution
creator: Stephan Permann, Elena Brunner, Khaled Alsabil, Markus Werner, Lorenz Waltl, Guillaume Viault, Danilo D’Avino, Bill Perkowski, Anita Siller, Laura Fritsch, Sara Perna, Harald Schennach, Denis Séraphin, Solveigh C. Koeberle, Paul M. Jordan, Fiorentina Roviezzo, Pascal Richomme, Antonietta Rossi, Jean
description: Restoring homeostasis in persistent inflammation requires suppressing the inflammatory response and promoting resolution. Currently, no clinically used small molecules intentionally achieve both effects. Endogenous long-chain vitamin E metabolites (LCMs) address inflammation at multiple sites, including pro-inflammatory leukotriene production and cytokine release, thus limiting inflammation.

title: The Prevalence of Neck and Back Pain among Paramedics in Poland
creator: Aleksandra Bryndal, Sebastian Glowinski, Kazimiera Hebel, Julia Grochulska, Agnieszka Grochulska, Jacob Ablin
description: Neck Pain (NP) and low back pain (LBP) are ubiquitous musculoskeletal conditions and some of the major causes of disability worldwide. The aim of the study was to assess the incidence and risk factors of back pain among paramedics and their correlation with the nature of work, anthropometric features and the level of recreational physical activity.

title: Jointing Achievement and Performance Evaluation of Bogie Crossmember Ring Joint Welded via Inertia Friction Welding
creator: Feng Qin, Xinmeng Zhang, Chunbo Zhang, Yanquan Wu, Wu Liang, Rui Li, Jun Zhou
description: As a major load-bearing component of trains, the weld quality of the bogie beam is critical to the safety of railway operations. This study specifically investigates the inertia friction welding process of S355 bogie crosshead tubes, with the aim of improving the weld quality and achieving one-time formation of the crosshead tube and tube seat.

title: Comparative risks of mortality, cardiovascular events, and dementia with methotrexate versus hydroxychloroquine in rheumatoid arthritis: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Bal Krishna Subedi, Naveen Gautam, Rafal Ali, Anuja Upadhyay, Prakriti Sapkota, Basu Dev Subedi
description: Background:Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder primarily affecting joints. Methotrexate (MTX) and hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) are common disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, yet more comparative outcome studies are needed. This study aimed to compare associations of HCQ versus MTX initiation with mortality, cardiovascular events, and other major health outcomes in RA patients.

title: Breeding Efficiency for Salt Tolerance in Alfalfa
creator: Michael D. Peel, M. Rokebul Anower, Yajun Wu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.), one of the most extensively grown forage crops, is sensitive to saline soils. We measured the breeding efficiency for increased salt tolerance in alfalfa by comparing lines selected from BC79S, CS, and SII populations with their unselected parental means for forage mass and associated changes in stem length, leaf-to-stem ratio (LSR), number of nodes per stem, crude protein (CP) content, and neutral detergent fiber (NDF) content.

title: Pretreatment Tumor Volume and Tumor Sphericity as Prognostic Factors in Patients with Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prospective Clinical Study in 95 Patients
creator: Elisabetta Lucchi, Laura Cercenelli, Vincenzo Maiolo, Barbara Bortolani, Emanuela Marcelli, Achille Tarsitano, Omar Kujan
description: The prognostic impact of tumor volume and tumor sphericity was analyzed in 95 patients affected by oral cancer. The pre-operative computed tomography (CT) scans were used to segment the tumor mass with threshold tools, obtaining the corresponding volume and sphericity. Events of recurrence and tumor-related death were detected for each patient. The mean follow-up time was 31 months.

title: 谷胱甘肽在调控代谢相关脂肪性肝病铁死亡和铜死亡中的作用
creator: Sijia Liu, Yi Long, Lina Yang, 朴 田
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 代谢相关脂肪性肝病(metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease，MASLD)是以代谢功能障碍为核心特征的脂肪肝病，是全球肝病最常见的原因之一，可带来严重的疾病负担。异常的细胞死亡方式参与MASLD的发生与发展，铁死亡和铜死亡诱发并加重MASLD，成为新近研究热点。谷胱甘肽(glutathione，GSH)作为调节氧化还原过程最重要的还原剂，其含量下降或耗竭会促进肝脏脂质蓄积与氧化损伤，推动MASLD进展。GSH是铁死亡和铜死亡的共同枢纽：一方面，GSH作为谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶4(glutathione peroxidase 4，GPX4)的必需还原底物，通过清除有毒脂质过氧化物来抑制铁死亡；另一方面，GSH能螯合细胞内过量的亚铜离子(Cu+)，降低Cu⁺在细胞内的毒性，从而抑制铜死亡。因此，GSH是调控MASLD铁死亡与铜死亡的关键，靶向GSH代谢通路有望成为预防、诊断与治疗MASLD的潜在新策略。未来可深入解析GSH调控铁死亡与铜死亡串扰的分子网络，并结合纳米靶向递送、基因编辑等新技术，开发安全高效的GSH靶向调节剂，推动基础研究成果向临床转化。Keywords: 谷胱甘肽, 代谢相关脂肪性肝病, 铁死亡, 铜死亡, 串扰, 氧化应激, 脂质过氧化

代谢相关脂肪性肝病(metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease，MASLD)过去被称为非酒精性脂肪肝病(nonalcoholic fatty liver disease，NAFLD)，是肝脏脂肪堆积与代谢功能障碍共存的疾病，其代谢异常表现为超重或肥胖及胰岛素抵抗。MASLD的特征是肝脏脂肪堆积(进而表现为肝脂肪变性)，伴有不同程度的炎症和纤维化[1]。研究[2]显示，MASLD全球患病率为30.2%，已成为全球公共卫生负担。如不及时治疗，MASLD常发展为代谢相关脂肪性肝炎(metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis，MASH)、肝纤维化甚至肝细胞癌(hepatocellular carcinoma，HCC)[2]，严重危害患者健康。

MASLD的发病涉及多种病理机制，其中氧化应激、脂质过氧化被认为是推动疾病进展的重要机制[3]。谷胱甘肽(glutathione，GSH)是细胞内最重要的抗氧化分子之一，不仅参与清除活性氧(reactive oxygen species，ROS)，还是谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶(glutathione peroxidase，GPX)的必需辅因子，GSH将脂质过氧化物还原为无毒脂质醇，从而抑制脂质过氧化累积、减轻氧化损伤，促进内源性及外源性有害物质的解毒[4]。近年研究[5]表明，GSH缺失诱导肝细胞应激、损伤和死亡，造成肝脏纤维化，导致肝硬化和HCC。新近研究[6-7]发现，铁死亡和铜死亡均与氧化还原失衡、脂质过氧化积累及金属离子稳态异常密切相关，参与MASLD进展。GSH含量降低会增加ROS和脂质过氧化，继而促进铁死亡和铜死亡，参与MASLD的发生与发展[4, 6-7]。本文旨在总结MASLD中GSH调控铁死亡和铜死亡的进展，为探究MASLD新的治疗靶点提供证据。

GSH在MASLD中的作用

GSH由谷氨酸、半胱氨酸和甘氨酸组成，是真核细胞中最丰富的天然活性肽，也是哺乳动物细胞中最常见的非蛋白硫醇[8]。维持细胞内氧化还原平衡状态的抗氧化系统主要分为3类：还原型谷胱甘肽/氧化型谷胱甘肽(oxidized glutathione，GSSG)系统、谷氧还蛋白(glutaredoxin，Grx)系统及硫氧化蛋白(thioredoxin，Trx)/Trx还原酶系统。前2个系统均需要GSH提供电子供体，因此GSH是维持生物体内氧化还原稳态最重要的小分子活性物质[9]。

细胞内GSH的稳态依赖于一个由合成酶、再生酶、结合酶及降解酶精密调控的网络，该网络常被称为GSH抗氧化系统[10]。其核心包括2个方面：合成与再生循环。GSH的合成主要分为2步，由腺苷三磷酸(adenosine triphosphate，ATP)驱动的酶促反应：首先，谷氨酸和半胱氨酸在谷氨酸半胱氨酸连接酶(glutamate-cysteine ligase，GCL)的催化下生成γ-谷氨酰半胱氨酸，这是GSH合成的限速步骤；随后，谷胱甘肽合成酶(glutathione synthetase，GS)催化甘氨酸与γ-谷氨酰半胱氨酸结合生成GSH[11]。在发挥抗氧化作用时，GSH在GPX的催化下，将电子提供给过氧化物(如脂质过氧化物)，自身被氧化为GSSG。随后，GSSG在谷胱甘肽还原酶(glutathione reductase，GR)和还原型烟酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸磷酸(nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate hydrogen，NADPH)的作用下被还原再生为GSH，从而维持细胞内极高的GSH/GSSG比值。这一循环是维持细胞氧化还原稳态的核心机制[10]。

抗氧化系统在MASLD发病机制和疾病进展中发挥关键作用，作为抵抗氧化应激的主要防御物质，GSH主要集中在肝脏，对肝脏健康至关重要[12]。研究[13]发现，GSH能有效抑制大鼠体内抗坏血酸诱导的肝微粒体和线粒体不饱和脂肪酸发生脂质过氧化。GSH含量下调、GSH依赖性抗氧化剂活性降低是MASLD恶化的机制[14]。在MASLD早期，代谢改变限制了甘氨酸的可用性，损害了GSH的合成，从而加剧了急性肝毒性[15]。随着疾病加重，GSH/GSSG比值下降，这提示氧化应激和GSH耗竭存在于MASLD整个过程中[16]。鉴于GSH耗竭在MASLD进展中的重要作用，通过外源性物质靶向调控GSH代谢已成为潜在的干预策略。例如，黄芩苷可通过影响GSH的从头合成途径有效缓解MASLD[17]；对肝脂肪变性小鼠补充甘氨酸，可通过支持GSH的从头合成来减轻对乙酰氨基酚诱导的肝毒性[15]。肝脏GSH氧化还原系统及其在MASLD进展中的失代偿过程见图1。

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and preconception planning: bridging the gap between obesity treatment and reproductive safety, a narrative review
creator: Abdulrahman Saad Alfaiz
description: Background:Obesity and associated metabolic disorders such as type 2 diabetes mellitus and polycystic ovary syndrome are rising globally, contributing to infertility and adverse pregnancy outcomes. This review synthesizes current evidence on pharmacokinetics, safety in preconception and early pregnancy, and clinical management strategies for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) therapy in women of reproductive age.

title: Pharmacogenomics in everyday practice: realities after Bupa’s DNA-based medication screening
creator: Shahbaz Shakil, Mahira Ijaz, Aman Kumar Shah
description: he moral and practical problems that need to be solved before PGx can be safely and fairly used in everyday life. This article is compliant with the TITAN Guidelines 2025 governing the declaration and use of artificial intelligence tools in research and publication[1]. The most exciting thing about PGx is that it could change how prescriptions are written.

title: 肺复张策略联合个体化呼气末正压对高血压患者肺切除术后肺部并发症和围手术期血流动力学的影响
creator: 珂辰 施, 静雯 谷, 华 柴, 命珩 刘, 怀顺 刘, 炳鑫 陈, 继如 张
description: 目的肺复张策略(lung recruitment maneuver，LRM)联合肺动态顺应性导向的呼气末正压(positive end-expiratory pressure，PEEP)策略可降低肺切除术患者术后肺部并发症(postoperative pulmonary complications，PPCs)风险，然而该策略在高血压患者中的肺保护作用及其对血流动力学的影响尚不明确。本研究旨在评估LRM联合肺动态顺应性导向的PEEP策略对合并高血压的胸腔镜肺切除术患者PPCs和围手术期血流动力学的影响，以期为该策略在此类人群中的安全应用提供科学依据。方法选择2024年11月28日至2025年8月15日江南大学附属医院收治的合并高血压、拟在单肺通气下行胸腔镜肺切除术的100例患者，采用随机数字表法将其分为常规保护性通气组(对照组)和LRM联合个体化PEEP组(试验组)，每组50例。对照组术中PEEP设定为5 cmH2O (1 cmH2O=0.098 kPa)；试验组于单肺通气开始后实施LRM联合递减PEEP滴定法，以肺动态顺应性确定最佳PEEP。在单肺通气结束前，2组患者均进行一次LRM操作。主要结局为术后5 d内PPCs发生率。次要结局包括术中低血压发生率、血管活性药物使用、术后5 d内心律失常和低血压发生率、术后肾功能指标及术后住院时间。结果对照组和试验组术前基线资料的差异均无统计学意义(均P>0.05)。试验组的术中PEEP高于对照组，驱动压低于对照组，气道平台压(plateau pressure，Pplat)、脉搏氧饱和度(pulse oxygen saturation，SpO2)、肺动态顺应性略高于对照组(均P<0.05)。试验组术中低血压的发生率高于对照组[52%(26/50) vs 30%(15/50)，P<0.05]，术中血管活性药物使用率也高于对照组[54%(27/50) vs 20%(10/50)，P<0.05]。2组患者手术部位、手术类型、心率、平均动脉压(mean arterial pressure，MAP)、脉搏压变异度(pulse pressure variation，PPV)、术中补液量、呼吸频率、潮气量方面的差异无统计学意义(均P>0.05)。试验组的PPCs发生率较对照组降低[22%(11/50) vs 42%(21/50)，P<0.05]，2组患者的术后心律失常、术后低血压及住院时间方面的差异均无统计学意义(均P>0.05)。试验组与对照组术后1 d的血肌酐(serum creatinine，SCr)和血尿素氮(blood urea nitrogen，BUN)、术后3 d的BUN均高于术前(均P<0.05)；2组术前与术后1、3、5 d的SCr与BUN差异均无统计学意义(均P>0.05)。经多因素Logistic回归校正年龄、体重指数(body mass index，BMI)、高血压分级、美国麻醉医师协会(American Society of Anesthesiologists，ASA)分级及手术类型后，试验组术中低血压的发生风险为对照组的2.8倍 (OR=2.8，95% CI 1.2~6.9；P<0.05)。针对术中低血压的亚组分析显示，对于年龄≥65岁、BMI>24 kg/m2、高血压3级、ASA Ⅲ级或拟接受肺段切除手术的患者，在接受LRM联合个体化PEEP策略时更容易发生术中低血压。结论LRM联合个体化PEEP策略可降低PPCs发生率，虽然术中低血压发生率较高，但经及时干预后多能迅速纠正，持续时间较短，未影响术后心肾功能。高龄、高血压3级及超重患者术中发生低血压的风险可能较高，需加强术中血流动力学监测，并及时进行个体化治疗。 肺癌发病率持续攀升，且有年轻化趋势，手术量呈逐年快速增长态势[1]。胸腔镜肺切除术作为肺癌外科治疗的主要手段，尽管其具有创伤小、恢复快的优势，但术后肺部并发症(perioperative pulmonary complications，PPCs)的发生率仍高达15%~37%，严重影响患者康复进程与转归质量[2]。PPCs主要包括肺不张、肺炎、呼吸衰竭等，不仅延长住院时间、增加医疗费用，更与术后远期生存率下降密切相关[3]。因此，围手术期肺保护策略的优化始终是胸外科麻醉领域的研究热点。传统保护性肺通气策略，即采用小潮气量、限制气道平台压(plateau pressure，Pplat)以及适当的呼气末正压(positive end-expiratory pressure，PEEP)进行机械通气，虽已广泛应用，但其降低PPCs发生率的效果仍不理想[4]。近年研究[5-6]显示，肺复张策略(lung recruitment maneuver，LRM)联合肺动态顺应性导向的PEEP策略可进一步降低PPCs发生的风险。该策略的保护机制为LRM通过短时升高气道压使萎陷肺泡重新开放，个体化PEEP则维持肺泡开放状态，减少肺泡周期性塌陷与复张所致的剪切力损伤，同时降低驱动压、改善肺顺应性[7-8]。 然而，LRM联合肺动态顺应性导向的PEEP策略在实施过程中，需较高的跨肺压以复张肺泡，因此存在诱发术中血流动力学紊乱的潜在风险[9]。特别是高血压患者，其术中血流动力学紊乱风险高于普通人群[10]。鉴于中国成人高血压患病率已达27.

title: Development of Mortars That Use Recycled Aggregates from a Sodium Silicate Process and the Influence of Graphene Oxide as a Nano-Addition
creator: Jaime D. Ruiz Martinez, Héctor Cifuentes, José D. Rios, Pilar Ariza, Carlos Leiva
description: This research analyses how different cement mortars behave in terms of their physical and mechanical properties. Several components were necessary to make seven mixes of mortars, such as Portland cement, standard sand, and solid waste from a factory of sodium silicate, in addition to graphene oxide.

title: An Integrative Approach to the Current Treatment of HIV-Associated Neurocognitive Disorders and the Implementation of Leukemia Inhibitor Factor as a Mediator of Neurocognitive Preservation
creator: Andrés De Freitas-Suarez, Natalia Espinosa-Ponce, Natalia Alvarez-Roger, Arianna Iris Cabrera-Suarez, Guillermo Jiménez-Jordán, Rocio Vega-Roman, Mikhail Inyushin, Janaina M Alves, Julien Van Grevenynghe
description: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HANDs) continue to impact patients despite antiretroviral therapy. A combination of antiretroviral therapies can diminish the HIV viral load to near undetectable levels, but fails to preserve neurocognitive integrity. The cytokine leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) has shown neuroprotective properties that could mitigate neurodegeneration in HANDs. The LIF promotes neurogenesis, neural cell differentiation, and survival.

title: 内质网应激抑制剂4-苯基丁酸对脓毒症小鼠心肌损伤的保护作用
creator: 洧 熊, 金伟 戴, 文晔 许, 锐 金, 嫕婷 陈, 丽娜 张, 招昕 钱
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的内质网应激(endoplasmic reticulum stress，ERS)是脓毒症相关心肌损伤(sepsis-related myocardial injury，SRMI)发生和发展的重要病理生理机制之一。本研究旨在探讨ERS抑制剂4-苯基丁酸(4-phenylbutyric acid，4PBA)对脂多糖(lipopolysaccharides，LPS)诱导的SRMI的保护作用。方法给予C57BL/6J雄性小鼠腹腔注射LPS构建小鼠SRMI模型。在第1组实验中，将小鼠随机分为5组(n=6)：对照(control)组、LPS 6 h组、LPS 12 h组、LPS 24 h组和LPS 48 h组。在第2组实验中，将小鼠随机分为4组(n=6)：control组、LPS组、衣霉素(tunicamycin，TM)组、TM+LPS组。在第3组实验中，将小鼠随机分为4组(n=6)：control组、LPS组、4PBA组、4PBA+LPS组。在第4组实验中，将小鼠随机分为4组(n=8)：LPS组、TM组、TM+LPS组、4PBA+LPS组。在注射LPS前6 h，腹腔注射TM(0.5 mg/kg)，注射LPS前6 h及注射后6 h给予4PBA(10 mg/kg)。采用心脏超声检测评价小鼠心功能，酶联免疫吸附测定(enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay，ELISA)检测小鼠血浆中心肌肌钙蛋白I(cardiac troponin I，cTnI)和肌酸激酶同工酶(creatine kinase-MB，CK-MB)的水平及心脏组织中白细胞介素-1β(interleukin-1β，IL-1β)的含量，苏木精-伊红(hematoxylin-eosin，HE)染色观察心肌组织形态学变化，蛋白质印迹法检测心脏组织中ERS相关蛋白质肌醇需求酶1α(inositol-requiring enzyme 1α，IRE1α)、磷酸化蛋白激酶R样内质网激酶(phospho-protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase，p-PERK)、激活转录因子6的剪切形式(cleaved-activating transcription factor 6，cleaved-ATF6)、剪接型X盒结合蛋白1(spliced X-box binding protein 1，XBP1s)、CCAAT/增强子结合蛋白同源蛋白(CCAAT enhancer binding protein-homologous protein，CHOP)、葡萄糖调节蛋白78(glucose regulated protein 78，GRP78)，以及炎症因子肿瘤坏死因子α(tumor necrosis factor-α，TNF-α)的表达情况。采用LPS处理HL-1小鼠心肌细胞系构建脓毒症细胞模型。分别采用原位末端转移酶标记法(terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase-mediated dUTP-biotin nick end labeling，TUNEL)、线粒体膜电位染色评估心肌细胞凋亡及线粒体膜电位的变化。结果与control组比较，LPS 6 h组、LPS 12 h组、LPS 24 h组和LPS 48 h组小鼠左室射血分数(ejection fraction，EF)、短轴缩短率(fractional shortening，FS)随时间推移先降低后恢复，血浆cTnI、CK-MB水平和心肌组织IL-1β水平先升高后下降，心脏组织ERS相关蛋白质IRE1α、XBP1s、p-PERK、CHOP、cleaved-ATF6、GRP78均显著升高(均P<0.05)，心肌组织出现明显水肿、肌纤维断裂及血管间隙消失。与LPS组相比，4PBA+LPS组小鼠EF、短轴FS均显著回升，血浆cTnI、CK-MB水平及心肌组织IL-1β水平均显著下降，心肌组织中ERS相关蛋白质及炎症因子TNF-α表达水平均显著下调(均P<0.05)；心肌组织病理损伤明显改善，小鼠的5 d生存率有升高趋势。TM+LPS组则呈现与4PBA+LPS组相反的变化。在LPS处理HL-1小鼠心肌细胞系构建的脓毒症细胞模型中，线粒体膜电位检测结果显示，与LPS组比较，4PBA+LPS组线粒体膜电位改善(均P<0.05)；TUNEL凋亡检测结果显示，与LPS组比较，4PBA+LPS组TUNEL阳性细胞比率显著降低(均P<0.05)。结论激活ERS可加重LPS诱导的SRMI，4PBA通过抑制ERS的过度激活，减轻炎症反应，减少心肌细胞凋亡，改善心功能并降低病死率。靶向ERS可能成为脓毒症心肌损伤的潜在治疗策略。 脓毒症相关心肌损伤(sepsis-related myocardial injury，SRMI)是脓毒症患者常见的并发症之一，在全球范围内，脓毒症患者的SRMI发生率为10%~70%，且合并心肌损伤的脓毒症患者通常预后不良[1]。内质网应激(endoplasmic reticulum stress，ERS)是未折叠蛋白、错误蛋白过度累积所导致的内质网功能紊乱。持续的ERS将导致细胞内钙离子代谢障碍、氧化应激损伤、线粒体功能失衡，最终诱发各种类型的细胞死亡。ERS是SRMI发生和发展的重要病理生理机制之一[2]。 ERS由3种内质网跨膜传感器介导，即肌醇需求酶1(inositol-requiring enzyme 1，IRE1)、磷酸化蛋白激酶R样内质网激酶(phospho-protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase，p-PERK)、激活转录因子6(activating transcription factor 6，ATF6)[3]。这3种信号蛋白质识别氧化应激损伤、细胞内未折叠蛋白质及错误蛋白质持续累积、钙离子失衡等刺激信号后，相继被激活，进而启动下游的未折叠蛋白质应答(unfolded protein response，UPR)[4]。在适应性阶段，UPR通过抑制蛋白质翻译和减少蛋白质进入内质网以减轻负荷；但若ERS持续存在，UPR则转而加速内质网功能崩溃，最终诱导凋亡等多种细胞死亡途径[5]。

title: Plant Production Protocols from Seeds of Threatened Atropa baetica and Widespread A. belladonna, Both Rich in Alkaloids
creator: Elena Copete, Miguel A. Copete, Esmeralda Martínez-Duro, Alejandro Santiago, Pablo Ferrandis, José M. Herranz
description: Members of the genus Atropa contain various tropane alkaloids, including atropine ((±)-hyoscyamine) and scopolamine, which possess medicinal properties. Preserving the diverse genetic background of wild populations via optimal plant production from seeds could be essential for avoiding the loss of potential uses. We analyzed the germination ecology of two Atropa species comprising the threatened A. baetica and widespread A.

title: Tailored management of chronic bacterial prostatitis with sequential fluoroquinolones and adverse effect mitigation strategies: A case report
creator: Thao D Nguyen
description: Chronic bacterial prostatitis (CBP) presents diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly in patients with drug allergies and atypical symptom profiles. This case describes a retired male healthcare professional with exclusive penile pain and urinary symptoms, diagnosed with CBP. Management involved sequential fluoroquinolone therapy—ciprofloxacin followed by moxifloxacin—over 6.5 weeks, guided by clinical condition and pharmacokinetic/ pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) considerations.

title: Anticoagulation Following Surgery for Glioblastoma: Case Report and Review of the Literature
creator: Zade Akras, David I. Nawabi, Noah L. A. Nawabi, Adam Glaser, Lennard Spanehl, Florian A. Gessler, Pablo Valdes, Pierpaolo Peruzzi, Omar Arnaout, E. Antonio Chiocca, Timothy R. Smith, Joshua D. Bernstock
description: Patients with glioblastoma (GBM) have a high risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), particularly after surgery, but a competing high risk of intracranial hemorrhage complicates the need for anticoagulation. We present a case of a 70-year-old male on dabigatran with a history of VTE who underwent GBM resection.

title: Follow-Up of Men Who Have Undergone Focal Therapy for Prostate Cancer with HIFU—A Real-World Experience
creator: Katharina Sophie Mala, Henning Plage, Lukas Mödl, Sebastian Hofbauer, Frank Friedersdorff, Martin Schostak, Kurt Miller, Thorsten Schlomm, Hannes Cash
description: Purpose: To determine oncological and functional outcomes and side effects after focal therapy of prostate cancer (PCa) with high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU). Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 57 consecutive patients with localised PCa. Aged 18–80 with ≤2 suspicious lesions on mpMRI (PIRADS ≥ 3), PSA of ≤15 ng/mL, and an ISUP GG of ≤2.

title: Parenting style profiles in families of children with ADHD using a person-centred approach
creator: Marisol Cueli, Natalia Martín, Nerea Quiroga, Ada Mesa-Prado, Paloma González-Castro
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has been linked to problematic parent-child interactions in the family setting, which can influence the development of the disorder in terms of how it progresses and the types and severity of symptoms. The present study aims to determine parenting style profiles in a sample of families of children with ADHD and the relationship between those profiles and ADHD-severity and type of presentation (both reported by parents).

title: Atherosclerosis in Patients with Congenital Hemophilia: A Focus on Peripheral Artery Disease
creator: Minerva Codruta Badescu, Oana Viola Badulescu, Alexandru Dan Costache, Ovidiu Mitu, Vasile Valeriu Lupu, Bianca-Ana Dmour, Ancuta Lupu, Liliana Georgeta Foia, Irina-Iuliana Costache, Ciprian Rezus, Eleni Gavriilaki
description: Advances in the treatment of hemophilia have increased the life expectancy of this population and we are currently facing diseases associated with aging, including cardiovascular ones. Coronary atherosclerosis, with acute myocardial infarction as the most severe form of manifestation, has been recognized as part of the comorbidities of hemophiliacs. However, little is known about peripheral artery disease.

title: What is new in delirium: A vascular etiology outlook
creator: Niccolò Terrando, Mervyn Maze, Ting Yang
description: Emerging studies have highlighted the vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID), especially in the context of neurodegenerative disorders that cause cognitive decline (i.e., Alzheimer's disease and related dementias [ADRD]). More recent research on perioperative neurocognitive disorders, including postoperative delirium, is describing a potential role of neurovascular dysfunction in the pathogenesis of these common complications for many older adults.

title: Fosl1 is a transcriptional effector of BRAFV600E-driven intestinal tumorigenesis
creator: Zakia Alam, Rebecca Nightingale, Analia Lesmana, Cheng Liu, Laura J Jenkins, Mark F Richardson, Lawrence Croft, Ian Y Luk, Camilla M Reehorst, Fiona Chionh, Natalia Vukelic, Faiza Basheer, Eugene Tulchinsky, Joshua Badshah, Troy Dumenil, Latifa Bakiri, Erwin F Wagner, Niall C Tebbutt, Vicki Whitehal
description: SummaryThe serrated neoplasia pathway is an alternate route to colorectal cancer (CRC) development where BRAFV600E is the most common initiating genetic alteration. BRAFV600E-driven tumorigenesis requires gene expression changes mediated by activation of the ERK MAPK signaling pathway. However, the key effectors of this process are elusive. Here, we identify the ERK-regulated transcription factor Fosl1, one such effector.

title: Using Multistage Energy Barrier of Heterojunctions in Improving Cr(VI) Detection
creator: Minggang Zhao, Yichang He, Xiaotong Dong, Kun Pang, Qian He, Ye Ma, Hongzhi Cui, Marina N Rumyantseva
description: Detecting heavy metals in seawater is challenging due to the high salinity and complex composition, which cause strong interference. To address this issue, we propose using a multistage energy barrier as an electrochemical driver to generate electrochemical responses that can resist interference.

title: EUS-guided hepatico-gastrostomy followed by antegrade digital cholangioscopy and laser lithotripsy for a large biliary stone in surgically altered anatomy (with video)
creator: Amine Achemlal, Shrikant Mukewar, Bhushan Bhaware, Shubankar Godbole, Saurabh Mukewar
description: ered anatomy (Roux-En-Y Hepatico-jejunostomy) who was referred for symptomatic biliary obstruction caused by a large impacted stone located at the hepatic duct confluence. Enteroscopy-assisted endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography was attempted but failed due to inability to reach the biliary anastomosis. Given the high morbidity associated with alternative surgical or percutaneous options, an EUS–guided approach was selected.

title: FDTransformer: A firn density prediction framework combining a self-attention transformer network with firn densification physics
creator: Xueyu Zhang, Lin Liu, Houjun Jiang, Zhicai Luo
description: SummaryAccurate firn density estimation is essential for assessing glacier mass balance. However, the accuracy of existing firn densification models (FDMs) is limited by an incomplete understanding of firn compaction dynamics, particularly as firn structure alters in warming conditions. This study proposes the firn density prediction transformer (FDTransformer), a deep learning framework that combines firn densification physics to improve density estimation.

title: Oral Health-Related Quality of Life in Adult Patients with Depression or Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
creator: Stephan Gemp, Dirk Ziebolz, Rainer Haak, Nicole Mauche, Madlen Prase, Ezgi Dogan-Sander, Frauke Görges, Maria Strauß, Gerhard Schmalz, Irina Esterlis
description: The aim of this cross-sectional study was the evaluation of the oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) in patients with depression or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in comparison with a group of mentally healthy individuals. Patients from the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, University of Leipzig, Germany, were recruited.

title: Manufacturing of Aluminum Nano-Composites Reinforced with Nano-Copper and High Graphene Ratios Using Hot Pressing Technique
creator: Hossam M. Yehia, Reham A. H. Elmetwally, Abdelhalim M. Elhabak, Omayma A. El-Kady, Ahmed Yehia Shash
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this study, the nano-aluminum powder was reinforced with a hybrid of copper and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs). The ratios of GNPs were 0 wt%, 0.4 wt%, 0.6 wt%, 1.2 wt% and 1.8 wt%. To avoid the reaction between aluminum and graphene and, consequently, the formation of aluminum carbide, the GNP was first metalized with 5 wt% Ag and then coated with the predetermined 15 wt% Cu by the electroless coating process.

title: Differences in Performance and Conductivity Persistence of New Reduced Graphene Oxide Air Filter Materials before and after Eliminating Static Electricity
creator: Yun Gao, Huixin Shi, Xin Zhang, Jingyao Ma, Tao Yu, Victor M García-Suárez
description: Improving the filtration efficiency of air filter materials is an ongoing research goal. This study conducted in-depth research on a new reduced graphene oxide air filter material, and the differences in its performance and conductivity durability before and after eliminating static electricity were tested and analyzed.

title: Geospatial Analysis of Orthopedic Workforce Distribution Across Georgia
creator: Dev Shah, William E Long, Shervin Eskandari, Anna Bozzone, Stephen A Parada
description: Introduction: Healthcare disparities between rural and urban populations have been well documented; however, orthopedic surgery-specific care remains under-characterized in rural communities. The purpose of this study was to assess rural-urban disparities in access to orthopedic care in Georgia.Study type: This is a cross-sectional study.

title: Investigating Neotongue Atrophy and Postoperative Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Glossectomy With Free Flap Tongue Reconstruction
creator: Audrey Abend, Sophia Salingaros, Adrienne Biskaduros, Matthew Spano, Matthew Wright, Sara Strauss, Jason A. Spector, David I. Kutler
description: ObjectiveFollowing glossectomy, tongue reconstruction via autologous free flap can reapproximate native form and function, significantly improving postoperative quality of life. Various studies have examined functional outcomes between the commonly employed radial forearm free flap (RFFF) and the anterolateral thigh free flap (ALTFF); however, changes in neotongue volumetric bulk are less clearly understood.

title: Shoulder Calcific Tendinitis Presenting as Septic Arthritis: A Case Report
creator: Ibrahim M Aljumaan, Abdullah S Alzahrani, Hayat A Khan, Asail Ahmed A Alammar, Anwar Alnakhli
description: Calcific tendinitis of the shoulder is a common condition in which calcium hydroxyapatite crystals form within the rotator cuff tendons, most often the supraspinatus. As a sequela of this condition, long-term discomfort may develop with intermittent acute flares. Symptoms can also arise suddenly, causing intense pain and limited shoulder motion.

title: The Effectiveness of Autologous Platelet Concentrates in the Clinical and Radiographic Healing after Endodontic Surgery: A Systematic Review
creator: Alessandro Espedito di Lauro, Alessandra Valletta, Angelo Aliberti, Mario Cangiano, Pasquale Dolce, Gilberto Sammartino, Roberta Gasparro, Edgar Schäfer
description: Regenerative techniques are increasingly applied in endodontic surgery, but different materials may have varying impacts on soft and hard tissue healing. This systematic review aims to evaluate the effectiveness of autologous platelet concentrates (APCs) in clinical and radiographic healing after endodontic surgery.

title: Safety and efficacy of Shatavari in women with low libido: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
creator: Madhuchander Satla, Mounika Mudhigonda, Gurunath Surampalli
description: Women with low libido commonly report reduced desire and diminished arousal, along with negative feelings about their physical and emotional satisfaction and overall wellbeing. In line with this evidence, the present study evaluated the potential of Shatavari root extract (300 mg daily) to support healthy sexual function in women experiencing lifestyle-related reductions in sexual desire.

title: Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt Placement: Effects on Nutritional Status in Cirrhotic Patients
creator: Ilaria de Felice, Lorenzo Ridola, Oliviero Riggio, Jessica Faccioli, Silvia Nardelli, Stefania Gioia, José A Carrión, David E Kaplan
description: Malnutrition is a tangible complication of cirrhosis with portal hypertension with a prevalence of up to 50%. In particular, sarcopenia and myosteatosis, defined as the alteration in muscle quantity and quality, have a negative impact on the main complications of liver disease and are associated with higher mortality in patients with cirrhosis.

title: Prevalence of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Microvascular Complications in Sri Lanka: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Harahana Munasinghe, Sithara Wijekoon, Pansujee Dissanayaka, DDM Jayasundara, Mapa Prabhath Piyasena, Sobha Sivaprasad, M D Nugawela
description: The burden of type II diabetes and microvascular complications is increasing around the globe, especially in low- and middle-income countries. We conducted a systematic review and a meta-analysis to estimate the prevalence of type II diabetes and its microvascular complications to determine the nature of diabetes and its complications in Sri Lanka.

title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence for the Classification of Craniofacial Deformities
creator: Reinald Kuehle, Friedemann Ringwald, Frederic Bouffleur, Niclas Hagen, Matthias Schaufelberger, Werner Nahm, Jürgen Hoffmann, Christian Freudlsperger, Michael Engel, Urs Eisenmann
description: Positional cranial deformities are a common finding in toddlers, yet differentiation from craniosynostosis can be challenging. The aim of this study was to train convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify craniofacial deformities based on 2D images generated using photogrammetry as a radiation-free imaging technique.

title: Machine Learning Model as a Useful Tool for Prediction of Thyroid Nodules Histology, Aggressiveness and Treatment-Related Complications
creator: Valeria Dell’Era, Alan Perotti, Michele Starnini, Massimo Campagnoli, Maria Silvia Rosa, Irene Saino, Paolo Aluffi Valletti, Massimiliano Garzaro
description: Thyroid nodules are very common, 5–15% of which are malignant. Despite the low mortality rate of well-differentiated thyroid cancer, some variants may behave aggressively, making nodule differentiation mandatory. Ultrasound and fine-needle aspiration biopsy are simple, safe, cost-effective and accurate diagnostic tools, but have some potential limits.

title: Comparative performance of single-use flexible ureteroscopes with and without direct in-scope suction: a retrospective analysis
creator: Petrisor Geavlete, Razvan Multescu, Cristian Mares, Cosmin Ene, Catalin Bulai, Bogdan Geavlete
description: Ureteroscopy represents the primary therapeutic approach for a broad spectrum of upper urinary tract stones. The aim of this study was to compare the efficiency of various models of single-use flexible ureteroscopes, some of them with direct in-scope suction (DISS) capabilities.

title: The role of the respiratory physiotherapist in the management of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
creator: Claire Egan
description: Shareable abstractRespiratory physiotherapy plays an important role in cough augmentation in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Early intervention is crucial in slowing the decline of pulmonary function and improving quality of life in this patient cohort. https://bit.ly/4i5yRug Educational aims To help healthcare professionals understand the effect DMD has on the respiratory system.

title: Thermal Regeneration of Spent Sand with Furfuryl Binder from an Ecological and Economic Point of View
creator: Mariusz Łucarz, Michał Dereń, Rodrigo Moreno
description: The recovery of the grain matrix from spent moulding sand is a constant challenge in making the best possible use of the deposits of quartz sand material, as well as in protecting them. In the case of spent sand with organic binders, the best method to recover the grain matrix is thermal regeneration.

title: DYRK kinases phosphorylate IL-17RA at S801
creator: Sayed Ala Moududee, Andrew A Herppich, Mary Kay H Pflum, Dongxia Ge, Zongbing You
description: Interleukin-17 (IL-17) receptor A (IL-17RA) promotes inflammatory reactions by activating kinases and transcription regulators. Our previous studies have demonstrated that glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK3) phosphorylates IL-17RA at T780. It is not known whether other kinases also phosphorylate IL-17RA. Here, we identified an association between dual-specificity tyrosine-regulated kinases (DYRKs) and IL-17RA.

title: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Harboring a Novel Four-Way Variant Translocation t(7;22;9;15)(p15;q11.2;q34.1;q22) With Cryptic Double Philadelphia Chromosomes
creator: Shogo Kamigaki, Makoto Ito, Satsuki Nakano, Norio Takagi
description: Variant Philadelphia chromosomes are occasionally observed in chronic myeloid leukemia. Among them, four-way variant Philadelphia translocations are particularly rare. Double Philadelphia chromosomes, representing an additional Philadelphia chromosome, are also uncommon and have been reported to be associated with disease progression and therapeutic challenges. We report a case of chronic myeloid leukemia with a novel four-way variant translocation t(7;22;9;15)(p15;q11.2;q34.

title: The Management of Coronary Artery Disease in TAVR Patients
creator: Laurent Faroux, Aurélien Villecourt, Damien Metz, Michel Noutsias, Emmanuel Andrès
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). About half of the transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) recipients exhibit some degree of coronary artery disease (CAD), and controversial results have been reported regarding the impact of the presence and severity of CAD on clinical outcomes post-TAVR. In addition to coronary angiography, promising data has been recently reported on the use of both cardiac computed tomography angiography and the functional invasive assessment of coronary lesions whether by FFR or iFR in the work-up pre-TAVR.

title: Evolution of the Therapeutic Management of Giant Cell Arteritis: Analysis of Real-Life Practices over Two Timeframes (2014–2017 and 2018–2020)
creator: Hubert de Boysson, Anael Dumont, Paul Castan, Sophie Gallou, Jonathan Boutemy, Gwénola Maigné, Nicolas Martin Silva, Alexandre Nguyen, Samuel Deshayes, Achille Aouba, Santos Castañeda
description: Objectives: To determine how therapeutic strategies for giant cell arteritis (GCA), especially glucocorticoid (GC) management, evolved between 2014 and 2020. Patients and Methods: Consecutive GCA patients followed for at least 24 months in a single tertiary center were enrolled and separated into two groups: those diagnosed from 2014 to 2017 and those diagnosed from 2018 to 2020.

title: Association Between Serum Uric Acid and Pulmonary Hypertension in Takayasu Arteritis With Pulmonary Artery Involvement: A Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Jinzhi Wang, Shuwen Zheng, Ruzetuoheti Yiminniyaze, Hanyu Zheng, Shuai Zhang, Han Tian, Yanhua Kong, Wanmu Xie, Qiang Huang, Zhenguo Zhai
description: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a severe complication of Takayasu arteritis (TAK) with pulmonary artery involvement (PAI), associated with poor prognosis. Serum uric acid (UA) has been linked to both TAK severity and PH in other settings, but its role specifically in TAK‐PAI‐associated PH remains unclear.

title: Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Risk of Cardiovascular Events and Mortality in Middle Age Patients without Known Cardiovascular Disease
creator: Amir Aker, Walid Saliba, Fadel Bahouth, Ibrahim Naoum, Barak Zafrir, Birna Bjarnason-Wehrens
description: Background: Low cardiorespiratory fitness is an established risk predictor for chronic non-communicable diseases. We aimed to investigate the prognostic significance of fitness level on the risk of major adverse cardiac events (MACE, the composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or all-cause death), in a contemporary cohort of middle-aged subjects without cardiovascular disease.

title: Endovascular Treatment of Type A Aortic Dissection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Using Reconstructed Time-to-Event Data
creator: Konstantinos S. Mylonas, Ioannis Zoupas, Panagiotis T. Tasoudis, Evangelos Vitkos, George T. Stavridis, Dimitrios V. Avgerinos
description: Objective: The undisputed gold standard of treatment for type A aortic dissections (TAAD) is open surgery. Anecdotal reports have assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) as a last resort for highly selected candidates. The present study aims to evaluate endovascular outcomes in TAAD patients who are unsuitable for open surgery whilst having TEVAR-compatible aortic anatomy.

title: A Pilot Test of an AI Voice-Driven Simulation With Feedback for Medical Students to Practice Discussing Diagnostic Mammogram Results With Patients
creator: Warren S Comulada, Patricia A Ganz, Yue Ming Huang, Dan Weisman, Alanna Sugarman, Daniel Lee, Saachi Shah, Lillian Gelberg
description: IntroductionEffective communication when delivering sensitive results or bad news to patients is necessary for medical professionals, warranting greater attention in medical education. The opportunity to practice communication skills with human standardized patients has limitations, including not being readily available, prompting researchers to develop virtual patients (VPs) to supplement training with a focus on routine tasks.

title: Pyramid attention network for indoor scene segmentation
creator: Rui Cao, Xiang Chen, Yiqin Wang, Feng Jiang, Meng Wang
description: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, indoor scene segmentation is more and more widely used in robot vision, security monitoring, firefighting, and other fields. Usually, indoor objects have problems such as easy mutual occlusion and dense layout, thus requiring high accuracy of network segmentation.

title: Shear Testing of Topologically Optimised Web Cover Plates in Splice Connections—Experiment Design and Results
creator: Tiago Ribeiro, Luís Bernardo, Miguel C. S. Nepomuceno, Natale Antonio Maugeri, Paolo Longo, Dario De Domenico
description: Testing shear-resisting plates in steel connections is one of the most challenging laboratory undertakings in steel construction, as the most common experimental layout design includes simulating the connection with its adjoining members. This significant hindrance gained particular magnitude as the need to test prototypes of topologically optimised shear cover plates became more pressing.

title: Applications of Silk Fibroin in Human and Veterinary Medicine
creator: Piotr Koczoń, Alicja Dąbrowska, Ewa Laskowska, Małgorzata Łabuz, Katarzyna Maj, Jakub Masztakowski, Bartłomiej J Bartyzel, Andrzej Bryś, Joanna Bryś, Eliza Gruczyńska-Sękowska, George Eliades
description: The properties of silk make it a promising material for medical applications, both in human and veterinary medicine. Its predominant amino acids, glycine and alanine, exhibit low chemical reactivity, reducing the risk of graft rejection, a notable advantage over most synthetic polymers. Hence, silk is increasingly used as a material for 3D printing in biomedicine.

title: Racial‐Ethnic Differences of Community Vulnerability Impact on Pediatric Thyroid Cancer Diagnosis and Surveillance
creator: David Fei‐Zhang, Meredith Osmulski, Christopher Puchi, Abhinav Talwar, Jorge Gutierrez, John Maddalozzo, Jill D'Souza, Anthony Sheyn, Daniel Chelius, Jeffrey Rastatter
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo assess racial‐ethnic differences of community‐level social vulnerability impact on pediatric thyroid cancer diagnosis and surveillance.Study DesignRetrospective cohort.SettingUnited States.MethodsThis retrospective analysis of 4324 pediatric thyroid cancer patients diagnosed between 1975 and 2017 from the Surveillance‐Epidemiology‐End Results (SEER) data set assessed overall social vulnerability aggregated from 15 different social vulnerabilities of health of socioeconomic status, minority‐language status, household composition, and housing‐transportation from the social vulnerability index (SVI). Social vulnerability scores of each category were matched to patients across US counties.

title: The future seen: Does episodic future thinking influence health decision-making in adolescents?
creator: Haide Chen, Zixuan Liu, Enjin Zheng, Yu Liu
description: Although prior research has clearly demonstrated the general impact of episodic future thinking (EFT) on behavioral decision-making, there has been a scarcity of studies investigating how different features of EFT might variably affect health-related intertemporal choices in adolescents. This lack of research hinders our comprehension of the functional specificity of EFT.

title: Enhancing Sumoylation Site Prediction: A Deep Neural Network with Discriminative Features
creator: Salman Khan, Mukhtaj Khan, Nadeem Iqbal, Naqqash Dilshad, Maram Fahaad Almufareh, Najah Alsubaie, Yudong Cai
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Sumoylation is a post-translation modification (PTM) mechanism that involves many critical biological processes, such as gene expression, localizing and stabilizing proteins, and replicating the genome. Moreover, sumoylation sites are associated with different diseases, including Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s. Due to its vital role in the biological process, identifying sumoylation sites in proteins is significant for monitoring protein functions and discovering multiple diseases. Therefore, in the literature, several computational models utilizing conventional ML methods have been introduced to classify sumoylation sites.
