title: 系统性红斑狼疮继发真菌感染影响因素分析
creator: Chunlin Li, Qiuyu Fan, Yu Xiao, Ting Song, Ziye Zong, Wei Yang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的探讨系统性红斑狼疮（systemic lupus erythematosus，SLE）患者继发真菌感染的影响因素。方法回顾性选取2021年6月—2025年1月我院收治的310例SLE患者作为研究对象，根据有无继发真菌感染分为未感染组和感染组，经倾向性评分法（propensity score matching，PSM）进行5：1匹配后，未感染组和感染组分别纳入患者230例、46例。分析SLE患者继发真菌感染现状，通过Logistic回归分析SLE患者继发真菌感染的影响因素，并采用受试者工作特征（receiver operating characteristic，ROC）曲线评估模型预测效能，构建预测SLE患者继发真菌感染的列线图模型。结果在纳入的310例SLE患者中真菌感染46例（14.84%），以肺部感染（50.0%）和胃肠道感染（23.9%）为主。匹配分组后，二元Logistic回归分析结果显示，狼疮活动度（OR=10.734，95%CI=2.015～57.184）、抗菌药物应用时间（OR=13.826，95%CI=2.995～63.822）、CRP（OR=9.927，95%CI=1.024～96.188）、白细胞计数（OR=11.784，95%CI=1.568～88.553）、补体C4（OR=16.392，95%CI=3.899～68.909）、24 h Pro（OR=9.391，95%CI=1.195～73.813）均为SLE患者继发真菌感染的独立危险因素（P<0.05）。ROC曲线评估显示，狼疮活动度、抗菌药物应用时间、C反应蛋白、白细胞计数、补体C4、24 h尿蛋白对SLE患者继发真菌感染均有一定的预测能力，六者联合预测的曲线下面积（area under the curve，AUC）为0.821，95%CI为0.720～0.922，优于单一指标（AUC 0.593~0.672）。此六者联合纳入构建列线图模型。结论狼疮活动度、抗菌药物应用时间、CRP、WBC、补体C4、24 h Pro是SLE患者继发真菌感染的影响因素。Keywords: 系统性红斑狼疮, 真菌感染, 影响因素, 倾向性评分法 系统性红斑狼疮（systemic lupus erythematosus, SLE）属于累及全身多脏器的慢性自身免疫病，最新流行病学调查报告显示[1]，SLE的全球患病率约为30/10万～150/10万，年发病率约2.2/10万～23.1/10万，我国发病率为30.13/10万～70.41/10万左右，且高发于育龄期女性群体。 在SLE的临床管理实践中，伴随着疾病治疗手段的不断发展与广泛应用，一系列新的临床问题也逐渐显现出来。具体而言，由于糖皮质激素在临床中长期应用、广谱抗菌药物广泛使用以及免疫抑制剂对机体免疫功能的损害，复杂感染已成为影响SLE预后的关键因素；其中真菌感染因其起病隐匿、诊断困难、治疗棘手等特点，更是当前危重症患者死亡的主要诱因之一[2]。真菌感染不仅可诱发并加剧SLE，更贯穿疾病全程[3]；相关研究表明[4]，近5年真菌感染发生率已达20世纪90年代的2倍，且发病率持续攀升，显著增加了临床诊疗难度和患者死亡风险，应引起临床的高度重视。鉴于上述严峻形势，预防SLE患者继发真菌感染已成为临床防控重点，而要实现有效的预防，早期识别相关危险因素是制定精准防治策略的关键前提。 倾向性评分法（propensity score matching, PSM）是对观察研究中偏差问题进行处理的一种统计学方法，目的是对随机分配效果进行模拟，减少非随机分配所引起的选择偏差，提高因果推断的准确性[5]。本研究即根据PSM采用单因素和多因素Logistic回归模型探究SLE患者继发真菌感染的影响因素，并建立风险预测模型，为临床早期防治提供科学参考。 资料与方法 样本量和分组 本研究为回顾性研究，经武汉市中西医结合医院伦理委员会批准，伦理批号：科伦预审[2024]54号，严格遵循《赫尔辛基宣言》伦理准则。 参考文献[6]计算样本量，采用统计学标准公式：N=Z2×[P(1－P)]/E2，其中各参数定义为：N代表所需最小样本量，Z对应标准正态分布临界值，P表示预期总体率，E为允许的最大抽样误差范围，该公式通过控制Ⅰ类错误概率和估计精度，确保研究具有足够的统计检验效能，当置信度为95%时，Z=1.96，P=0.2，E=5%，向上取整N为246例，即最低需纳入246例患者，考虑到10%～20%样本脱落率，最低需纳入296例患者。 本研究选取2021年6月—2025年1月我院收治的310例SLE患者作为研究对象，根据有无继发真菌感染，将研究对象分为未感染组264例和感染组46例。采用PSM对两组患者进行5∶1匹配，卡钳值为0.02。协变量包括性别、年龄、身体质量指数（body mass index，BMI）、吸烟、饮酒。匹配完成后，通过统计学方法验证协变量的均衡性，P>0.05即为分布均衡。最终未感染组和感染组分别纳入患者230例、46例。匹配前，未感染组与感染组在性别、年龄方面差异有统计学意义（P<0.05）。匹配后，两组基线资料均衡（P>0.05），见表1。 表 1Comparison of baseline data before and after title: Implementing a Standard Operating Procedure Is Associated with Improved Vancomycin Target Attainment in Bone and Joint Infections: A Pre-Post Study
creator: Moritz Diers, Juliane Beschauner, Maria Felsberg, Laura Isabell Kossack, Alexander Zeh, Karl-Stefan Delank, Natalia Gutteck, Felix Werneburg
description: Background: Intravenous vancomycin is a mainstay for prosthetic joint infections, osteomyelitis, and implant-associated infections, yet real-world dosing frequently misses PK/PD targets. We assessed whether a ward-embedded standard operating procedure (SOP) improves target attainment and dosing efficiency. Methods: Single-centre, non-randomized pre-post study in an orthopedic service.

title: Oral pathogens reprogram endothelial barrier and angiotensin-converting enzyme2/endothelial nitric oxide synthase-nitric oxide signaling to promote blood pressure dysregulation
creator: Ming-Shou Hsieh, Tung-Nien Hsu, Chin-Sheng Huang, Ting-Yi Renn, Kuang-Tai Kuo, Kuo-Yao Lin, Wei Jen Chang
description: Background/purposeAlthough periodontal disease is associated with an increased risk of hypertension, the endothelial mechanisms linking oral inflammation to vascular dysfunction remain unclear. We investigated whether Porphyromonas gingivalis lipopolysaccharide (Pg-LPS) can directly disturb endothelial homeostasis and whether macrophage –endothelial crosstalk further worsens endothelial injury.

title: 沙参麦冬汤通过抑制cGAS-STING-NF-κB介导的炎性衰老改善老年COPD小鼠肺功能
creator: Xiangnan Kuang, Xingran Liu, Xinyao Zhao, Xuexiao Chen, Shiqiao Liu
description: 目的观察沙参麦冬汤对慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）模型小鼠炎性衰老的影响，明确其是否通过调控环鸟苷酸-腺苷酸合成酶（cGAS）-干扰素基因刺激因子（STING）-核因子-κB（NF-κB）通路起效。方法选用18～20月龄雌雄各半C57BL/6JNifdc小鼠，以香烟烟雾暴露联合鼻滴脂多糖构建COPD模型，随机分6组：正常组、模型组、沙参麦冬汤低/中/高剂量组（8.3、16.5、33.0 g/kg）、地塞米松组（3 mg/kg），每组8只（雌雄各4只）。造模次日起每日灌胃（正常/模型组灌羧甲基纤维素钠，0.15 mL/10 g），周期12周。检测各组小鼠肺功能〔气道阻力（Rrs）、肺弹性阻力（Ers）、0.2 s用力呼气量与用力肺活量比值（FEV0.2/FVC）、50%肺活量时的用力呼气流量（FEF50%）〕、肺组织病理（HE 染色、Masson染色）、血清炎症因子〔白细胞介素-6（IL-6）、单核细胞趋化蛋白-1（MCP-1）、肿瘤坏死因子-α（TNF-α）〕、氧化应激指标〔超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）、丙二醛（MDA）〕，以及肺组织衰老蛋白（p16、p21）、cGAS-STING-NF-κB通路分子的mRNA与蛋白表达。结果与正常组相比，模型组小鼠肺功能受损，表现为Rrs升高，Ers、FEV0.2/FVC及FEF50%降低；肺组织出现大量炎症细胞浸润、细支气管壁增厚以及肺泡结构破坏；血清炎症因子及MDA升高、SOD降低，差异均有统计学意义（P<0.01）；肺组织衰老蛋白与cGAS-STING-NF-κB通路分子的mRNA及蛋白表达量亦升高（P<0.01）。与模型组相比，沙参麦冬汤中、高剂量组上述肺功能指标得到改善；血清炎症因子与MDA水平下降、SOD活性升高（P<0.05）；同时，肺组织衰老蛋白与通路分子的表达下调（P<0.05）。结论沙参麦冬汤可改善COPD小鼠以FEV0.2/FVC为核心的肺功能受损，其潜在机制可能为抑制cGAS-STING-NF-κB通路介导的炎性衰老。Keywords: 肺疾病，慢性阻塞性, 沙参麦冬汤, 衰老, 炎症, NF-κB 慢性阻塞性肺疾病（chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, COPD）以持续气流受限为特征，长期暴露于刺激性颗粒引发的慢性炎症是其主要诱因[1]。作为全球第三大死因，COPD在65岁以上人群中患病率极高[2]。然而，与年龄相关的变化在加速COPD发病机制中的作用尚不清楚[3]。现有常规治疗无法有效阻止老年患者肺功能的进行性下降，且长期使用糖皮质激素不良反应较多[4]。 传统中医学将COPD归属于“肺胀”“喘证”等范畴，老年患者多属肺肾阴虚、气阴两虚证[5-6]。沙参麦冬汤源于清代吴鞠通《温病条辨》，是养阴润肺的经典方剂[7]。临床证实其可有效缓解COPD症状、延缓肺功能衰退并减少急性加重频率[8]。 炎性衰老（inflammaging）是指增龄伴随的慢性低度炎症状态，是连接衰老与多种老年疾病的关键[9-10]。研究发现，老年COPD患者外周血中白细胞介素（interleukin, IL）-6、肿瘤坏死因子-α（tumor necrosis factor-α, TNF-α）等炎症因子水平升高且伴随肺功能下降[11]。该慢性炎症可促发衰老相关分泌表型（senescence-associated secretory phenotype, SASP），形成“炎症-衰老”恶性循环[12]。近年来发现，氧化应激等损伤可导致线粒体DNA泄漏，被胞质环鸟苷酸-腺苷酸合成酶（cyclic GMP-AMP synthase, cGAS）识别并激活干扰素基因刺激因子（timulator of interferon genes, STING），进而磷酸化核因子-κB（nuclear factor kappa-B, NF-κB）以诱导促炎因子表达[13-14]。这提示cGAS-STING-NF-κB通路可能是介导炎性衰老参与老年COPD发病的重要机制。 因此，本研究以炎性衰老为切入点，探讨沙参麦冬汤通过调控cGAS-STING-NF-κB通路改善老年COPD小鼠肺功能的分子机制，为中医药防治老年COPD提供新的理论依据和实验证据。 材料与方法 实验动物 研究使用老年C57BL/6JNifdc小鼠（18～20月龄，体质量20～25 g），雌雄各半〔北京维通利华实验动物技术有限公司，许可证号SCXK（京）2021-0006〕。小鼠饲养在河北中医药大学实验动物中心，饲养条件为温度20～24 ℃，湿度40%～60%，并采用12 h光照与12 h黑暗交替的周期，提供自由饮食和饮水。饲养期间记录小鼠体质量变化，保障各组基础生理状态均衡。本实验纳入标准为：健康且适应性饲养期间体质量变化正常、无异常行为的小鼠；排除标准为：造模期间非预期死亡、状态极度萎靡无法耐受后续实验的小鼠。本实验经河北中医药大学实验动物管理和伦理委员会批准（编号DWLL202403108），实验方案已明确雌雄动物饲养、造模及检测全流程，符合动物实验性别因素控制规范。 实验药物 本研究所用沙参麦冬汤（以下简称SMD）由沙参、麦冬、玉竹、甘草、生扁豆、冬桑叶、天花粉7味中药组成，各饮片具体信息如下：沙参9 g（批号：20200915）、麦冬9 g（批号：20201022）、玉竹6 g（批号：20200817）、甘草3 g（批号：20201103）、生扁豆4.5 g（批号：20200928）、冬桑叶4.5 g（批号：20201012）、天花粉4.5 g（批号：20200830），均购自河北省中医院中药房，并经鉴定为正品，符合《中华人民共和国药典》（2020 年版）要求。水煎剂制备：将上述饮片置于砂锅中，加入8倍量蒸馏水浸泡30 min，武火煮沸后改文火保持微沸30 min，滤取药液；药渣再加6倍量蒸馏水同法煎煮20 min，合并两次煎液，经100目筛网过滤后浓缩，4 ℃冷藏备用。根据小鼠与人（70 kg）体质量的剂量换算法，确定小鼠的灌胃剂量，以临床等效剂量作为沙参麦冬汤的中剂量，低剂量和高剂量分别为等效剂量的0.5倍和2倍。最终，沙参麦冬汤低、中、高剂量组的给药量分别为8.3 g/kg、16.

title: 口腔菌群的增龄性变化
creator: 靖芝 周, 星辰 叶, 静 邹, 玲 邹, 磊 程, 卓立 朱, 玍 廖, 学东 周, 彪 任
description: 人体微生物组由寄居于人体不同部位的微生物群落及其遗传信息共同构成，在维持宿主健康方面发挥重要作用。作为人体微生物组的重要组成部分，口腔菌群在维持口腔微生态稳态、调节局部免疫反应、参与营养代谢及影响全身健康中发挥关键作用。生命早期的口腔微生物初始定植为后续菌群发展和终身口腔健康奠定基础，同时其菌群变化与多种口腔及全身疾病密切相关。本文系统综述口腔菌群在婴幼儿期、儿童及青少年期、成年期和老年期的增龄性演替规律，分析各年龄段与菌群失调相关的口腔疾病，探讨影响口腔菌群增龄性变化的宿主、微环境和外源性等因素，并总结基于微生态调节的干预策略，以期为理解口腔菌群增龄性变化及构建全生命周期口腔微生态健康管理模式提供参考。 在人体生态系统中，微生物作为关键的共生组分发挥着不可或缺的作用[1]。口腔作为人体与外界环境交互的重要门户，是人体内微生物多样性、复杂性最高的微生态之一。健康状态下，宿主与微生物之间维持动态平衡；而当这种平衡被打破时，微生态失衡可引发或加重局部及全身多种疾病，成为慢性炎症、感染性疾病和代谢异常的重要影响因素。口腔菌群不仅在维持口腔局部健康中扮演核心角色，更与机体的免疫调节、代谢平衡及多种生理病理过程紧密相连[2-4]。随着生命历程的推进，口腔菌群并非静止不变，而是经历着一系列动态、有序的演替过程。从生命最初的口腔定植开始，历经婴幼儿期、儿童期、青少年期、成年期直至老年期，其菌群结构与宿主的生理变化、免疫状态及外部环境等多种因素相互交织、共同演替。理解这一伴随年龄增长而发生的菌群变迁规律，不仅有助于揭示口腔疾病乃至全身性疾病发生发展的微生物学基础，也为通过干预微生态促进全生命周期健康提供了潜在的可能性。因此，本文旨在系统梳理口腔菌群随年龄变化的动态轨迹，探讨其背后的驱动机制与健康影响，并对相关微生态调控策略进行展望。 生命各阶段口腔菌群及增龄性变化特征 口腔菌群的增龄性变化是指口腔菌群在个体全生命周期中，伴随宿主生长发育、成熟和衰老而发生的相对规律性演替过程。为系统阐述口腔菌群在整个生命历程中的动态演变规律，本文依据个体生理发育与增龄性变化的核心特征，并参考世界卫生组织的相关年龄分期标准[5-7]，将全生命周期划分为婴幼儿期（0～3岁）、儿童及青少年期（3～18岁）、成年期（18～65岁）和老年期（≥65岁）四个阶段进行论述。 婴幼儿时期：初始定植与群落建立 生命早期是口腔菌群建立和发育的关键时期，这一过程可追溯至出生前[8]。已有研究表明婴儿口腔菌群的初始定植受多种因素影响，包括分娩方式及产后母婴间的微生物交换[9]。经阴道分娩的婴儿口腔微生物主要来源于母亲产道和肠道微生物，而以剖宫产方式出生的婴儿则更多地接触母亲皮肤和医院环境中的微生物，导致其口腔微生物组成存在差异[10]。 婴幼儿时期口腔菌群的组成是动态演替的过程，有研究表明[11]：出生后的早期阶段以链球菌属（Streptococcus）为主导，韦荣球菌属（Veillonella）和乳杆菌属（Lactobacillus）伴随定植。链球菌作为先锋菌，不仅可通过母乳传递，还可依靠黏膜粘附能力占据生态位，其代谢产物更为后续菌群的定植奠定了基础。随着乳牙的萌出，孪生球菌属（Gemella）、颗粒链菌属（Granulicatella）、罗氏菌属（Rothia）和嗜血杆菌属（Haemophilus）等菌群丰度开始增加，口腔微生物多样性显著提升。至1岁以后，放线菌属（Actinomyces）和奈瑟菌属（Neisseria）等晚期定植菌开始显著增多，标志着口腔菌群向更复杂、更成熟的成人化结构发展。以上研究结论也说明，婴幼儿口腔菌群的初始多样性相对较低，随着乳牙萌出和饮食多样化，多样性逐渐增加。 儿童与青少年时期：群落多样化与发展 儿童及青少年期是口腔微生态走向成熟和稳定的关键时期，随着乳牙列和恒牙列的相继建立，儿童口腔菌群经历显著变化[12]。这一时期，口腔内不同生态位的微生物组成差异变得更加明显，牙齿的萌出为微生物提供了新的附着表面，包括牙体组织的平滑面、窝沟点隙和邻接区域，以及龈下含氧量低的生态位点，这些微环境的差异支持了不同需求的微生物的定植和发展[13]。 在此期间，与婴幼儿时期相似，链球菌属仍然是口腔中的优势菌属之一，但儿童及青少年时期口腔菌群的整体多样性和复杂性显著增加。有研究表明在唾液样本中，晚期定植菌属的丰度持续上升，例如普雷沃菌属（Prevotella）、韦荣球菌、奈瑟菌属、放线菌属、嗜血杆菌属及梭杆菌属（Fusobacterium）等需氧和厌氧菌逐渐占据口腔菌群的优势地位[14-15]。在混合牙列期，卟啉单胞菌属和二氧化碳噬纤维菌属（Capnocytophaga）的丰度开始出现较明显的增长，预示着菌群向成人化模式的过渡[16]。同时，放线菌属和罗氏菌属等在健康牙面菌斑中的比例也趋于稳定，而普雷沃菌属的某些菌种则被发现与青春期的牙龈健康状况变化存在关联[17]。这些研究共同表明，儿童及青少年期的口腔核心菌群从以链球菌为主导的简单结构，向一个由多种严格厌氧菌和兼性厌氧菌共同构成的、功能更为复杂的成熟微生态系统转变。 成年期：群落稳定与生态平衡 健康成年人的口腔微生态是一个高度复杂、多样化且相对稳定的生态系统[1]。在人类微生物组计划中即对健康成人口腔各种不同生态位点的样本进行了测序，结果表明健康成年人的口腔微生物在门水平上表现出高度的保守性，主要由厚壁菌门（Firmicutes）、放线菌门（Actinobacteria）、拟杆菌门（Bacteroidetes）、变形菌门（Proteobacteria）和梭杆菌门（Fusobacteria）主导[18]。这些在健康口腔生态系统中，跨个体、跨样本稳定存在，并在维持微生态平衡中发挥基础作用的微生物是口腔核心菌群。在属水平上，链球菌属是遍布所有口腔生态位（如唾液、牙菌斑、舌背、黏膜）的优势菌属，与之共生的韦荣球菌属、放线菌属、普雷沃菌属、嗜血杆菌属、奈瑟菌属和罗氏菌属等共同构成了健康成人口腔的核心菌群[19]。值得注意的是，不同生态位有其特异性：龈上菌斑富含放线菌和链球菌，而龈下菌斑则由于严格的厌氧环境，成为普雷沃菌属、梭杆菌属、卟啉单胞菌属和坦氏菌属等牙周相关病原菌的主要栖息地。 老年期：生态简化与疾病易感 老年时期由于生理性衰老和多种病理因素，口腔环境发生改变，包括唾液分泌减少、牙龈退缩、牙周袋形成、牙列缺损和牙列缺失等，这些变化共同导致口腔微生态的重构。大规模横断面研究揭示，与健康成年人相比，老年人口腔菌群的核心结构虽得以保留，但其组成与功能已发生显著改变[20]。老年人口腔微生物α-多样性显著降低，普雷沃菌属和韦荣球菌属相对丰度则显著上升，这种菌群构成的失调与老年人龋病、牙周病的高发密切相关[21]。这一趋势在中国高龄老人的研究中也得到了印证，有研究通过16S rRNA测序技术发现，尽管链球菌属依然是中国老人唾液中的优势菌属，但其微生物群落的多样性同样呈现下降态势，且普雷沃菌属等条件致病菌的比例普遍增高[22]。除细菌外，老年人口腔真菌也呈现出显著的增龄性失调。白色念珠菌（Candida albicans）是其中最主要的条件致病真菌，其在老年人群中的定植率、载量与多样性均显著高于健康成年人[23]。这种变化与老年期常见的唾液分泌减少、黏膜萎缩、免疫衰老以及佩戴义齿等因素密切相关。尤其值得注意的是，白色念珠菌与口腔细菌之间存在复杂的相互作用，它能与链球菌等共聚，形成更具致病性和耐药性的混合生物膜，共同加剧根面龋、义齿性口炎等老年常见口腔感染的发生与发展[24-28]。因此，老年口腔菌群的失衡是一个涉及多种微生物相互影响的综合性过程，该过程导致的生态简化，会提高多种口腔疾病的易感性。 增龄性变化的总体特征 口腔菌群的增龄性变化呈现出一定的规律性和连续性。从婴幼儿期到老年期，口腔细菌菌群经历了初始定植、多样性增加、相对稳定和生态简化的过程。除细菌外，口腔真菌的定植呈现两端高、中间低的模式，白色念珠菌等真菌在免疫系统尚未健全的婴幼儿期和免疫功能逐渐衰退的老年期定植率与丰度均较高；而在免疫系统处于巅峰的成年期，其水平则相对较低并保持稳定[29]。这一真菌的动态变化，与前述细菌菌群从简单到复杂再重构简化的过程相互交织，共同构成了口腔菌群的完整增龄性图谱（图1）。该演变过程受宿主生理状态、生活方式和环境等多种因素共同调控，而该过程塑造的菌群稳态，关系到宿主终身的口腔与全身健康[30]。 Aging-associated atlas of oral core microbiota, disease, and host immunity 口腔核心菌群-疾病-免疫的增龄化图谱 The central region represents the core microbiota shared across all age groups; the inner ring illustrates age-specific core microbial members and their age-related successional changes.

title: 癫痫临床文本信息的结构化标注与抽取研究
creator: Ling Jin, Mengqiao He, Basangsijia, Duanyu Feng, Wenqiang Lei, Lei Chen
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的面向癫痫专科临床及科研需求，构建一套细粒度、高覆盖的中文临床文本命名实体标注体系，并验证其在命名实体识别（named entity recognition，NER）任务中的有效性。方法从疾病、病程时间、临床表现、医疗检查、非药物治疗、用药及影响因素等7大维度设计3级标注体系，共制定25类标签，明确标签边界与特殊表达处理规则。以四川大学华西医院2009～2023年癫痫住院患者脱敏病历为数据来源，由3名具有癫痫临床背景的标注员完成804例高质量语料标注，采用双人复标、专家仲裁与实体级标注者一致性（inter-annotator agreement，IAA）评估保障标注质量。以五种中文医学预训练语言模型（Base-BERT、chinese-bert、chinese-Roberta、MC-BERT、MedBERT）分别结合BiLSTM-CRF与GlobalPointer两种序列标注框架，共10种组合方案进行NER性能验证，并在外部文献病例集上开展跨域泛化评估。结果最终语料库涵盖25类癫痫相关实体，标注实例804条，实体总数28 400个；三位标注员IAA为0.86～0.88，标注一致性达到计算语言学通行标准。NER验证中，GlobalPointer框架表现优于BiLSTM-CRF，整体Micro-F1为0.906、Macro-F1为0.760；高频核心实体（如发作症状、药物名称、时间信息）F1值均超过0.90；跨域文献病例验证中高频标签F1值维持在0.80以上，低频标签（如fac-inc-amb、trt、dru-adv）F1值为0.31～0.57，主要受样本量有限与表达多样性影响。结论本研究构建的癫痫专科中文临床标注体系覆盖范围广、粒度细、一致性高，可有效支持NER模型的训练与评估，为癫痫病历结构化分析及下游智能诊疗工具的开发提供了可复用的语料基础。Keywords: 癫痫, 电子健康档案, 自然语言处理, 命名实体识别, 语料库

癫痫是最常见的神经系统慢性疾病之一，全球约有7 000万例癫痫患者[1]，其中我国癫痫患者总数达900万，年新增病例约40万[2]。该疾病的病理特征为大脑神经元异常放电导致的反复性、发作性症状，其临床表现具有高度异质性[3]。准确的发作症状描述（包括症状特征、发作频率等）及发作环境信息（如时间、场所等）是癫痫诊断分型的关键依据[4]。电子健康记录中积累了海量癫痫患者的临床诊疗文本，这些真实世界的医疗记录为癫痫疾病研究提供了宝贵的数据资源。然而，由于不同医师的表述习惯和临床经验存在差异，癫痫病历文本中症状描述存在显著的术语不一致、表达非标准化等问题，为数据结构化提取带来巨大挑战。

本研究针对以上问题，制定了癫痫临床文本的细粒度实体标注规则体系，涵盖症状、诱因、治疗等关键医学实体，并在医院脱敏病历数据上通过命名实体识别任务（named entity recognition, NER）验证了标注方案的有效性。该标注规范可为癫痫健康咨询、智能辅助诊断等应用提供标准化信息提取框架，并为癫痫文本语料库的批量化建设奠定方法论基础。

资料与方法

为系统推进癫痫临床文本的结构化信息抽取研究，本研究设计并实施了包含三个阶段的整体工作流程，如图1所示。首先基于国际标准与临床实际制定细粒度标注体系与规范；其次通过人工标注与规范调试构建高质量语料库；最后以多种主流命名实体识别模型进行性能验证，以评估语料的可行性与模型适配性。

Overall research workflow

研究总体流程

ILAE: International League Against Epilepsy; UMLS: Unified Medical Language System; EHR: electronic health record; IAA: inter-annotator agreement; NER: named entity recognition; P: precision; R: recall; F1: F1-score; CCKS: China Conference on Knowledge Graph and Semantic Computing; CMCR: Chinese Medical Case Reports; CNKI: China National Knowledge Infrastructure.

title: 老年患者外周静脉留置针中重度并发症风险预测模型构建
creator: Xiao Chen, Yuchen Guo, Zhimin Liang, Lingli Li
description: 目的构建并验证老年患者外周静脉留置针（peripheral venous catheter, PVC）中重度并发症的风险预测模型，为临床精准防控提供依据。方法采用前瞻性队列研究，收集2023年11月—2024年9月期间收治的750例接受PVC治疗的老年患者的临床资料。按7∶3将患者分层随机分为训练集（n=526）与测试集（n=224）。通过单因素与多因素logistic回归分析筛选PVC中重度并发症的独立影响因素，分别构建二元logistic回归（binary logistic regression, BLR）、支持向量机（support vector machine, SVM）、随机森林（random forest, RF）、朴素贝叶斯（naive Bayes, NB）四种预测模型。采用受试者工作特征曲线下面积（area under the curve, AUC）结合DeLong检验评估模型区分度，使用校准曲线评估校准度，并利用决策曲线分析（decision curve analysis, DCA）评价其临床净获益，同时通过沙普利可加性模型解释算法（Shapley additive explanations，SHAP）可视化分析阐释模型的特征重要性。结果多因素logistic回归分析确定自理能力〔轻度依赖：比值比（odds ratio, OR）=1.361，95%置信区间（confidence interval, CI）：1.031～1.802；中度依赖：OR=1.992，95%CI：1.291～3.061；重度依赖：OR=3.060，95%CI：1.700～5.512〕、渗液（OR=8.998，95%CI：4.286～18.887）、临床科室〔胃肠外科：OR=28.396，95%CI：7.537～106.990；胰腺外科：OR=5.258，95%CI：1.177～23.499；胰腺炎中心：OR=5.974，95%CI：1.287～27.725〕、患者小学及以下文化程度（OR=2.525，95%CI：1.158～5.506）、饮酒（OR=1.970，95%CI：1.011～3.838）、敷料卷边（OR=1.458，95%CI：1.150～1.848）及合并症数量（OR=0.893，95%CI：0.821～0.972）为老年患者PVC中重度并发症的独立危险因素，16G～22G导管为独立保护因素（P<0.05）。测试集验证显示，RF模型AUC最高（0.891，95%CI：0.840～0.942），经DeLong检验，其区分度与BLR（0.808，95%CI：0.738～0.879）和SVM（0.842，95%CI：0.774～0.909）模型相比，差异有统计学意义（P<0.05）；SHAP分析提示渗液、自理能力、不同临床科室为RF模型的核心影响因素；DCA表明RF模型在0～0.8的阈值概率范围内具有显著的临床净获益。结论本研究成功构建并验证了老年患者PVC中重度并发症的RF预测模型，该模型区分度优异、临床应用价值突出，可有效早期识别高危人群，为临床精准干预提供科学依据。Keywords: 老年人, 导管，留置, 并发症, 比例危险度模型 随着人口老龄化，住院患者中老年群体占比持续升高[1]，外周静脉留置针（peripheral venous catheter, PVC）是老年住院患者静脉治疗的核心通路，使用率居高不下[2]，受生理机能减退、血管条件不佳及多重慢病共存等因素影响[3]，该群体PVC并发症发生率更高、损伤程度更重，已成为临床静脉治疗安全管理的突出难题。中重度PVC并发症可引发局部肿胀、治疗中断、住院周期延长，显著增加医疗成本并加重护理负荷，亟须精准化风险预警与分级防控策略[4]。 当前研究多聚焦于PVC并发症危险因素分析与现况调查[5-6]，能够量化并发症严重程度的预测模型仍较为匮乏。机器学习凭借强大的数据挖掘与特征拟合优势，为构建高精度、个体化的并发症严重度预测模型提供了关键技术支撑[7-8]。基于此，本研究拟构建老年患者PVC中重度并发症风险预测模型，为临床早期识别高危人群、实施精准干预提供循证依据与智能化工具。 资料与方法 研究对象 本研究为前瞻性队列研究，通过系统文献回顾与两轮德尔菲专家函询（11位静脉治疗专家，权威系数Cr=0.85），构建了包含患者基础资料、实验室指标与风险评估、操作者信息、留置针及治疗特征四个维度的初始预测指标库，并据此制定《住院老年患者外周静脉留置针并发症风险因素收集表》开展数据采集。基础资料与临床特征来源于病历系统；实验室指标与风险评估数据提取自检验记录与评估量表；操作者信息通过上述收集表收集；留置针及治疗相关数据（如型号、部位、留置时间、输液参数、敷料状况、药物性质等）则通过每日床旁观察与记录获取，确保数据的全面性与前瞻性。 INS）颁布的《输液治疗实践标准》[11]：①静脉炎：静脉血管的无菌性炎症；②渗出与外渗：非腐蚀性/腐蚀性药液进入静脉管腔以外的周围组织；③堵管：无法回抽血液或血液回流缓慢、无法推注冲管液或阻力大、液体无法输注；④意外脱管：患者或医务人员非故意将PVC导管拔出血管。 严重程度分级 严重度评估矩阵（severity assessment code, title: KELIM及BRCA突变状态对晚期高级别浆液性卵巢癌中间型肿瘤细胞减灭术预后的影响
creator: Yuebo Li, Mengru Li, Xiuyun Zhang, Hanjie Xu, Jie Li, Hanyuan Liu, Cheng Peng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的探讨CA125消除速率常数（CA125 elimination rate constant k, KELIM）对接受新辅助化疗联合中间型肿瘤细胞减灭术（neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery，NACT-IDS）的晚期高级别浆液性卵巢癌（high-grade serous ovarian cancer, HGSOC）患者疗效及预后的预测价值，并分析其与乳腺癌易感基因（breast cancer susceptibility gene，BRCA）突变状态的联合预后意义。方法回顾性纳入106例接受NACT-IDS治疗的晚期HGSOC患者。计算NACT期间的KELIM，以1.0为界分为高、低两组。比较两组临床病理特征、R0切除率及铂敏感率。采用Logistic回归分析R0切除的预测因素，采用Kaplan-Meier法和Cox回归分析无进展生存期（progression free survival，PFS）的影响因素。进一步根据KELIM与BRCA状态进行联合分层，分析各亚组的铂耐药复发风险。结果KELIM≥1组R0切除率高于KELIM<1组（77.1% vs 55.2%），差异有统计学意义（P=0.024）。多因素Logistic分析显示，KELIM是R0切除的独立预测因子（OR = 2.922，95% CI: 1.112～7.678）。生存分析显示，KELIM≥1组的PFS长于KELIM<1组（33.0个月 vs 18.0个月），差异具有统计学意义（P<0.001）。多因素Cox回归显示，KELIM≥1与PFS进展风险降低相关（HR = 0.481，95% CI: 0.280～0.826）；联合分层分析显示，“KELIM≥1且BRCA阳性”亚组未观察到铂耐药复发（0/21），与KELIM<1且BRCA阴性组相比较，其铂耐药复发风险较低（OR = 0.053，95% CI: 0.003～0.932，P = 0.006）。结论KELIM是预测NACT-IDS患者手术结局和PFS的有效动态标志物。KELIM与BRCA状态联合分层能更精准地识别铂耐药复发风险极低的“双重有利”人群，为晚期HGSOC的个体化治疗与风险分层管理提供重要依据。Keywords: 高级别浆液性卵巢癌, 中间型肿瘤细胞减灭术, 新辅助化疗, CA125消除速率常数K, BRCA基因 卵巢癌是病死率最高的妇科恶性肿瘤，其中晚期高级别浆液性卵巢癌（high-grade serous ovarian cancer, HGSOC）是最常见的亚型。因其早期症状隐匿，超过70%的患者确诊时已属晚期。对于肿瘤负荷大、伴有大量腹水或一般状况无法耐受初次肿瘤细胞减灭术（primary debulking surgery, PDS）的患者，新辅助化疗联合中间型肿瘤细胞减灭术（neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery，NACT-IDS）已成为标准治疗模式之一[1]。然而，患者对NACT的反应存在异质性，部分患者即使完成治疗，仍面临快速复发与铂类耐药的问题，导致预后不良。研究显示，尽管乳腺癌易感基因（breast cancer susceptibility gene，BRCA）突变患者通常对铂类药物更为敏感且生存期较长，但仍有部分患者出现耐药与早期复发[2-3]。因此，如何在治疗前或治疗早期准确评估患者对铂类药物的敏感性，成为指导临床决策、改善疗效的关键。 目前，肿瘤标志物 CA125是广泛应用的血清标志物，但其单点测定特异性有限[4-5]。You等[6]提出的KELIM，通过动力学模型定量评估化疗中肿瘤标志物CA125的清除速率，为预测疗效提供了新思路。尽管KELIM在PDS患者中的预后价值已得到验证，但针对NACT-IDS人群的研究仍有限，且较少将其与BRCA基因状态结合分析[7-12]。为此，本研究旨在通过回顾性分析106例接受NACT-IDS治疗的HGSOC患者的CA125动力学数据，评估KELIM对IDS后R0切除率、无铂间期（platinum free interval，PFI）、PFS及总生存期（overall survival, OS）的预测能力，并探讨其与BRCA状态的联合预后意义，为晚期HGSOC的风险分层与个体化治疗提供依据。 资料与方法 研究对象 本研究为一项单中心回顾性分析。选择2019年1月—2024年12月期间于本院妇产科接受治疗的晚期HGSOC患者106例。共筛查171例，按排除标准排除65例，最终纳入106例（图1）。所有患者均接受NACT后行IDS。NACT方案以铂类联合紫杉类为主，每3周为1个周期，通常完成3～4个周期后评估是否进入IDS，术后按残余病灶评估减瘤效果，定义R0为无肉眼残余，R1/R2为存在肉眼残余。BRCA 1/2检测来源于胚系和/或体细胞检测，将致病或可能致病变异定义为BRCA阳性（BRCA+），未检出致病或意义未明变异定义为BRCA阴性（BRCA－）。IDS后患者接受标准辅助化疗完成一线治疗；复发后按临床实践给予二线及后续治疗方案。 Study cohort enrollment criteria and data processing flowchart for advanced HGSOC

Recent studies show lower rates of ACL graft failure and rotatory laxity when LET is combined with ACL reconstruction.

title: Automated Planning for Bias-Free Validation of Discrete Proton Arc Therapy for Oropharyngeal Cancer
creator: Wens Kong, Merle Huiskes, Steven JM Habraken, Eleftheria Astreinidou, Coen RN Rasch, Ben JM Heijmen, Sebastiaan Breedveld
description: PurposeTo systematically compare fully automated planning for 36-field discrete proton arc therapy (36PAT) with: (1) intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) with 4- and 6-field clinical beam-angle class solutions (4CS, 6CS), (2) IMPT with patient-specific, computer-optimized beam-angle configurations with 6, 8 or 10 fields (6BAO, 8BAO, 10BAO), and (3) 36-field equiangular ‘‘Utopia’’ IMPT (36Utopia; total focus on dosimetric quality, no delivery time

title: Addressing challenges and leveraging opportunities for capacity building and the sustainable development of animal production in the south
creator: Youssef A Attia, Khalid A Asiry, Sameer A Nagadi, Asmaa F Khafaga, Rashed A Alhotan, Serena Calabrò, Bossima Ivan Koura, Manal E Shafi, Salem R Alyileili, Ahmed Galal, Samuel E Aggrey, Romdhane Rekaya
description: nd social dimensions. Livestock production in South and Africa faces interconnected challenges spanning the environmental, health, economic, and social dimensions. South and African animal scientists can lead this transformation by tapping into genetic innovations, adopting advanced technologies, and improving feeding systems.

title: Queer-religious symbol analysis (QRSA): A semiotic method for reframing Hindu iconography
creator: Preethika Shree AC, Chithra GK
description: As sacred traditions face renewed scrutiny, there's a pressing need for methods that read religious iconography as fluid, resistant, and open to new meanings. This article presents the Queer-Religious Symbol Analysis (QRSA) method, a visual-semiotic analytical framework for the reinterpretation of Hindu religious iconography.

title: Pulsed field ablation for pulmonary vein and left atrial posterior wall isolation in persistent atrial fibrillation: a narrative review
creator: Tochukwu R. Nzeako, Chukwuka Elendu, Ebubechukwu Ezeh, Daniel E. Otobrise, Olayemi Adeniran, Samuel B. Governor, Ike Ifedili, Shoshanah Kahn
description: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is an emerging technique for managing atrial fibrillation (AF). Still, its role in persistent AF (PeAF) with left atrial posterior wall isolation (LAPWI) remains to be defined. The ATHENA registry evaluated 249 PeAF patients across 9 Italian centers using the FARAPULSE PFA system, with 57.6% undergoing LAPWI.

title: Willingness to participate in a randomized trial of surgical vs. nonoperative care among patients with meniscal tear and knee pain after a course physical therapy
creator: Katharine B Fox, Kyna Long, Jon Dhani, Faith Selzer, Andrea L Carland, Paul M Oh, Nomi S Weiss-Laxer, Jeffrey N Katz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveRandomized controlled trials (RCTs) frequently fail to meet sample size requirements within their proposed timeline. Prospective preference assessments (PPAs) estimate the number of eligible individuals likely to enroll. The COSMIC Trial (Conservative care or Surgery for Meniscal tear after IneffeCtive physical therapy), currently in planning stages, will compare arthroscopic partial meniscectomy (APM) to non-operative treatment among those with meniscal tear who experience knee pain following a course of physical therapy (PT).

title: Global trends and inequalities in hypertensive and ischemic heart disease attributable to high body mass index: A systematic analysis from 1990 to 2021 with projections to 2035
creator: Xinyu Liu, Xu Zhang, Cheng Li
description: BackgroundHypertensive heart disease (HHD) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) are major global burdens. High body mass index (BMI) is a key modifiable risk factor, but the global burden, trends, and inequalities of HHD and IHD attributable to high BMI remain poorly defined.

title: Safe and Effective Analgesia Using Ultrasound-Guided Brachial Plexus Block for Upper Limb Compartment Syndrome: A Case Report
creator: Danny Alexander Utreras Freire, Paola Vanessa Astudillo Ochoa, Néxar Fernando Ron Valarezo, Wilson Andrés Saraguro Armijos, Angélica María Picón Montero, Luis Arnaldo Meza Guerrero
description: Upper limb compartment syndrome (ULCS) is a life-threatening and uncommon medical disorder that develops when the pressure within one or more muscle compartments of the upper limb increases. Consequently, it limits blood flow and leads to ischemia of the muscles and nerves.

title: A Case of Paget-Schroetter Syndrome Successfully Treated With Endovascular Treatment
creator: Tomohide Sato, Tomokazu Ikemoto, Ryusuke Tsunoda, Jyunjiro Koyama
description: A 16-year-old male presented with a five-day history of numbness in the left upper limb. Physical examination revealed asymmetry in upper arm circumference: the circumference of the right upper arm was 25.5 cm, whereas that of the left was 28.5 cm.

title: Classifying Hyponatremias According to Tonicity Disorder: Hypotonic Hyponatremia, Hypertonic Hyponatremia, and Pseudohyponatremia as Distinct Entities
creator: Todd S Ing, Raymond E Garrett, Ramin Sam, Christos Argyropoulos, Susie Q Lew, Maria-Eleni Roumelioti, Mark Unruh, Darlene Vigil, Mark Rohrscheib, Brent Wagner, Antonios H Tzamaloukas
description: Tonicity of a solution refers to its ability to cause cells in it to either swell or shrink through osmotic fluid flux across the cell membranes due to a difference in the total concentrations of osmoles in the solution and in the intracellular space. For serum, the sodium concentration ([Na]S) constitutes the major determinant of tonicity.

title: Surgical Approaches for Residual Secondary Gaze Diplopia After Strabismus Surgery: A Case Series
creator: Juan Lorenzo Simpao, Toshiaki Goseki, Hiromi Onouchi
description: This case series describes three patients who experienced residual diplopia in secondary gaze positions despite successful strabismus surgery and satisfactory alignment in primary gaze. While initial procedures effectively resolved diplopia in the primary position, symptoms remained in secondary gaze and interfered with daily activities.

title: Severe Rhabdomyolysis in an Elderly Patient With Diabetes and Vascular Disease: Interplay of Statin Therapy, Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) Inhibition, and Thiazide-Induced Hypokalemia
creator: Darpan Kothia, Bola Habeb, Felix Ermolenko
description: Rhabdomyolysis is a potentially life-threatening complication of drug therapy, particularly in elderly patients exposed to polypharmacy. Statins are a well-known cause, while thiazide-induced hypokalemia and volume depletion can further predispose to muscle injury. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors such as empagliflozin provide cardio-renal benefits but may potentiate statin toxicity and exacerbate dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, amplifying rhabdomyolysis risk.

title: A Novel Nanopore-Based Genotyping System for Norovirus GII: Validation and Application to Pediatric Gastroenteritis Cases in Moscow, Russia
creator: Ivan F. Stetsenko, Vasilina K. Lapshina, Polina A. Nikolaeva, Boris S. Gukov, Alexandr V. Chernitsov, Andrey R. Luparev, Ekaterina E. Davydova, Maria A. Gordukova, Elena V. Galeeva, Alina D. Matsvay, German A. Shipulin
description: Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with genogroup II (NoV-GII) being predominant. This study presents a novel genotyping system for norovirus GII, combining long-range PCR to amplify the complete ~3.2 kb RdRp–VP1 region with Nanopore sequencing and a dedicated bioinformatics pipeline. This approach provides comprehensive, high-resolution genomic data, representing a significant advancement over conventional methods.

title: Diagnostic Performance of a Silver-Amplified vs. a Non-Amplified Lateral Flow Kit for Adenoviral Conjunctivitis: A Multicenter Prospective Study
creator: Tsuguto Fujimoto, Nozomu Hanaoka, Kenichiro Takahashi, Hisatoshi Kaneko, Masaaki Kobayashi, Hisashi Nakagawa, Hiroshi Hatano, Tomoko Tsukahara-Kawamura, Hironori Migita, Kentaro Nakamura, Kiyoharu Kuramoto, Eiichi Uchio, Julia Davydova
description: Accurate diagnosis of adenoviral conjunctivitis is critical for timely treatment and infection control. However, conventional lateral flow kits often lack sufficient sensitivity, especially in mild cases. This multicenter prospective study evaluated the diagnostic performance of silver-amplified lateral flow kits (SA-LFKs) compared with non-silver-amplified kits (NSA-LFKs), using real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) as the reference standard.

title: Fast-Track to Protection? A Review of Encepur’s Express Dosing Schedule for Tick-Borne Encephalitis
creator: Kyra Zens, Ralph Torgler, Michael Horn, Carsten Schade Larsen
description: Cases of confirmed tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) have increased dramatically over the last 30 years, highlighting growing endemicity across Eurasia. Two preventative vaccines, Encepur® (Bavarian Nordic A/S, Hellerup, Denmark) and FSME-Immun® (Pfizer Ireland Pharmaceuticals, Cork, Ireland), are licensed in Europe. For both vaccines, primary immunisation consists of a three-dose regimen, administered over approximately one year using “Conventional” dosing schedules.

title: Genome-Based In Silico Analysis of the Structural and Functional Characteristics of the Type Three Secretion System (T3SS) and Core Effector Proteins in Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) Strains Isolated from Food-Producing Animals and Products of Animal Origin
creator: Refiloe Malesa, Rian Pierneef, Thendo Mafuna, Kudakwashe Magwedere, Emmanuel Seakamela, Itumeleng Matle
description: Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) is a significant diarrheagenic pathotype responsible for severe gastrointestinal infections, particularly in vulnerable populations. The aim of this study is to utilize genome-based in silico analysis to study the structural and functional characteristics of the Type III Secretion System (T3SS) and its core effector proteins in EPEC strains.

title: Treosulfan-Based Conditioning Regimens for Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation in Acute Myeloid Leukemia and Other Myeloid Malignancies
creator: Eleni Gavriilaki, Panagiotis Dolgyras, Ioannis Konstantinidis, Despina Mallouri, Grigorios Salvaras, Christos Demosthenous, Ioannis Batsis, Anna Vardi, Ioannis Papadopoulos, Sophia Tsokkou, Zoi Bousiou, Giorgos Karavalakis, Christos Varelas, Alkistis Panteliadou, Nikolaos Spyridis, Antonia Syrigou,
description: Background: Treosulfan combined with fludarabine (FluTreo) has emerged as a reduced-toxicity alternative to conventional myeloablative conditioning in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and related myeloid malignancies. Purpose: This study evaluates the safety, engraftment kinetics, and long-term outcomes of the FluTreo FT14 regimen in a real-world adult cohort.

title: Sodium Carboxymethyl Cellulose-Stabilised Multiple Emulsions with pH-Sensitive Behaviour, Enhanced Stability and Mucoadhesion for Oral Delivery of Chemopreventive Agents
creator: Agnieszka Markowska-Radomska, Konrad Kosicki, Ewa Dluska
description: Background/Objectives: The oral administration of chemopreventive agents for colorectal cancer (CRC) remains limited by their low solubility, instability, and limited intestinal absorption. This study develops sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC)-stabilised water-in-oil-in-water (W/O/W) multiple emulsions as pH-responsive carriers for co-delivery of resveratrol and selenium—two complementary chemopreventive compounds.

title: A Laser‐Induced Chrysiasis Treated With Pulsed Intense Light and Chemical Peels
creator: Rosemarie Mazzuco, Juliano Adolfo Grock, Airá Novello Villar, Sarah Lyane Venzon, Analupe Webber
description: BackgroundGold salts (chrysotherapy) were widely used for the treatment of moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis during the 1990s. Following administration, gold particles may deposit permanently in multiple tissues, including the skin. Exposure to ultraviolet radiation can induce a characteristic blue‐gray pigmentation known as chrysiasis.

title: Population-Based Genetic Assessment of Thrombophilia Polymorphisms: Allelic Frequencies and Population Linkage Dynamics
creator: Panagiota Tsiatsiou, Sofia Balaska, Zafeirios Tsinaris, Maria Archonti, Antonia Lanta, Vasiliki Tsaireli, Anna Takardaki, Areti Kourti, Angeliki Kassomenaki, Georgios Meletis, Dimitrios A Tsakiris, Lemonia Skoura, Mihaela Hostiuc
description: Background and Objectives: Thrombophilia is a prothrombotic disorder that increases the risk of blood clotting and can pose serious health problems. It is considered a condition of gene–gene or gene–environment interactions. Variation in the prevalence of thrombophilia mutations and their interaction among populations necessitates localized genetic assessments. However, population-based genetic data remains limited for developing effective preventive strategies.

title: Comparative Assessment of Point Shear Wave Elastography (pSWE) and Two-Dimensional Shear Wave Elastography (2D-SWE) in the Diagnostic Evaluation of Simple Liver Cysts and Liver Hemangiomas
creator: Emiliya Lyubomirova Nacheva-Georgieva, Daniel Ilianov Doykov, Bozhidar Krasimirov Hristov, Desislav Ivanov Stanchev, Iliya Stoyanov Todorov, Zhivko Georgiev Georgiev, Katya Angelova Doykova, Siyana Emilova Valova, Krasimir Iliev Kraev, Petar Angelov Uchikov
description: Background and Objectives: What led to the development of elastography was the emerging need for a method that could objectively and accurately assess the stiffness of internal structures. As a result, a distinction between normal from pathological tissues becomes possible.

title: A Pilot Clinical Study of a Biomimetic Suction Patch for Improving Wrinkles, Elasticity, Hydration, and Pigmentation via Enhanced Topical Delivery
creator: Seunghoon Choi, Hyung‐ki Park, Jaehwan Ahn, Dong‐Hyun Ko, Jin‐Hyun Kim, Byung Woo Hwang, Seongmin Noh, Wonkyu Hong, Keun Ho Lee, Da Wan Kim
description: BackgroundSuction‐based bioinspired patches have emerged as noninvasive platforms for enhancing topical delivery; however, clinical validation of their multidimensional skin benefits remains limited.AimsThis pilot study evaluated the clinical efficacy of a biomimetic suction‐type microstructured patch combined with a cosmetic ampule for improving wrinkles, elasticity, hydration, and pigmentation.Patients/MethodsTen healthy female subjects (aged 31–63 years) participated in a 4‐week split‐face study.

title: IFPHPOS0040 From Climate Risk to Clinical Action: An AI-Enabled Intervention for Health Care Professionals to Provide Climate Specific Health Advice in Community Settings
creator: Rochelle Velho, Peter Ward
description: BackgroundAir pollution is a major public health challenge. The Right to Breathe report (2025) calls for integration of environmental risk into routine clinical care. However, translation of environmental data into actionable, patient-centred interventions remains limited in primary care.MethodsA scoping review (2020–2026) evaluated seven widely used digital air quality tools (IQAir, Plume Labs, BreezoMeter, EPA AirNow, PurpleAir, airTEXT, AirTrack).

title: Environmental and Dispersal-Related Drivers of Color Morph Distribution in Triatoma infestans (Klug, 1834) (Hemiptera, Reduviidae)
creator: Erika V. Díaz, Federico G. Fiad, Gisel V. Gigena, Ana G. López, Romina V. Piccinali, Ana Laura Carbajal-de-la-Fuente, Claudia S. Rodríguez, Julieta Nattero
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryTriatoma infestans is a blood-feeding insect and the main vector responsible for transmitting the parasite that causes Chagas disease in southern South America. This species shows different color forms—some individuals are darker (melanic), while others are lighter (non-melanic). In this study, we examined the presence of these two forms in a rural region of Argentina, comparing how common they were at the beginning and end of the warm season.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Health
creator: Amily Guenier, Gethin Hopkin, Greg Williams, Joanne Elliott, Tina Purnat, Elena Petelos, Jedidah Mould, Elizabeth Dalgarno, Abin Thomas, Amy Wilcock, Laura Swain, Arpana Verma
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally changing public health, health surveillance and epidemiology. In last year’s International Festival of Public Health, a challenge for delegates was to consider if this is the “beginning of the end”? In a mere 10 months, we have seen an exponential rise in the use of AI across all disciplines.

title: IFPHOR0035 Health Insurance and Maternal Healthcare Utilisation in Nigeria: A Scoping Review of the National Health Insurance Scheme
creator: Oluwadamisi Tayo-Ladega
description: BackgroundNigeria continues to experience a high burden of maternal mortality despite ongoing health system reforms aimed at improving access to maternal healthcare. Health insurance is widely recognised as a critical mechanism for reducing financial barriers and advancing progress toward universal health coverage.

title: Overwintering Capacity of the Mediterranean Fruit Fly in the Dalmatia Region of Croatia
creator: Mario Bjeliš, Ivan Tavra, Frane Strikić, Luka Popović, Cleopatra A. Moraiti, Vasilis G. Rodovitis, Nikos T. Papadopoulos
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryTo elucidate the field biology of the Mediterranean fruit fly (medfly), Ceratitis capitata (Wiedemann) (Diptera: Tephritidae), with the aim of developing robust pest management strategies, overwintering trials were conducted in Split, central Dalmatia, Croatia, between 2019 and 2021. Experiments confirmed the capacity of medfly to overwinter in the area and revealed that both adult and pupae can survive in open-field and urban conditions in central Dalmatia in addition to the overwintering of larvae in fruit.

title: IFPHOR0084 Clearer Letters, Better Care: A Health Literacy Driven Quality Improvement Project
creator: Moradeke Orekoya, Annie Lowe
description: In Wigan, an estimated 43.12% of residents have low health literacy, contributing to health inequalities. The local NHS Trust identified written patient communication as a modifiable barrier to care. This was informed by a volunteer led quality improvement project (July–December 2025) that recorded 123 wrong site attendances, with 28% linked to unclear letter content.

title: Integrating Orientation Optimization and Thermal Distortion Prediction in LPBF: A Validated Framework for Sustainable Additive Manufacturing
creator: Nikoletta Sargioti, Elias P Koumoulos, Evangelia K Karaxi, Reza Teimouri
description: This study investigates the impact of build orientation on thermal distortion, residual stress behaviour, and process efficiency in LPBF. Four orientation strategies, optimized for surface area, support volume, print time, and overheating, were generated in Siemens NX and evaluated using Atlas 3D to predict build-stage and post-support removal distortion.

title: IFPHOR0062 Global Health Promotion and Communication training Curricula: Trends and Structures
creator: Allan Ssembuusi, David Musoke, Christine Nalwadda Kayemba, Aisha Nakiwala Sembatya, Marjorie Kyomuhendo, Ivan Lukanda, Agnes Nyabigambo, Rhoda Wanyenze
description: IntroductionHealth promotion and communication (HPC) are essential for behaviour change, community empowerment, and effective health information dissemination. However, HPC training opportunities are limited in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This study benchmarked global postgraduate HPC programmes to inform a postgraduate HPC curriculum development at Makerere University, Uganda.

title: Curvilinear Sub-Resolution Assist Feature Placement Through a Data-Driven U-Net Model
creator: Jiale Liu, Wenjing He, Wenhao Ding, Yuhang Wang, Yijiang Shen
description: In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, computational lithography, particularly sub-resolution assist features (SRAFs), is crucial for enhancing the process window. However, conventional SRAF placement methodologies are hampered by a critical trade-off between speed and pattern fidelity, and they largely fail to optimize the complex, curvilinear layouts essential for advanced nodes.

title: IFPHPOS0023 Multimorbidity Profiles and Mortality Inequalities Among Migrant-Origin Populations in Sweden: A Latent Class Analysis
creator: Courtney Franklin, Daniela Foresta
description: BackgroundMultimorbidity has an adverse multiplicative effect on all health outcomes, including an elevated risk of all-cause mortality. There is evidence of inequalities in multimorbidity patterns when comparing migrant populations to their native counterparts. Emerging research suggests that mortality depends not only on the number of conditions, but also on how conditions cluster within individuals.

title: Dust Mite-Specific IgE in Nasal Lavage Fluid During Natural Allergen Exposure and After Nasal Provocation Test in Subjects with Suspected Local Allergic Rhinitis
creator: Mohamad Mahdi Mortada, Alaa Sherri, Edyta Pietrowska, Marta Popławska, Maciej Chałubiński, Marcin Kurowski, Kinga Lis
description: Introduction: Apart from the typical AR phenotype and its standard clinical manifestations—rhinorrhea, sneezing, nasal itching, and congestion—the so-called local allergic rhinitis (LAR) can be observed in a subset of subjects presenting rhinitis symptoms, a negative skin prick test (SPT), and serum-specific immunoglobulin E (sIgE) for the relevant allergens and confirmed with a positive nasal provocation test (NPT), which is the

title: IFPHOR0096 Students as Changemakers: Fostering Interdisciplinary Engagement in Sustainable Healthcare
creator: Harshini Suresh, Ashley Thian, Lana Kaedbey
description: Understanding the relationship between planetary health and human health is pivotal for the long-term sustainability of our healthcare systems. An audit of the Planetary Health Report Card (2025) revealed low levels of student engagement in sustainability in healthcare, despite discourse within public health.A student-led, cross-faculty conference aimed to encourage interdisciplinary collaboration in sustainability.

title: IFPHOR0040 “Less Weight Should Be Given to Weight”: Weight Framing, Lived Experience, and Professional Perspectives in Local Healthcare
creator: Chloe Singleton
description: BackgroundWeight-focused policies, language, and practice are conceptualised as the ‘weight centred health paradigm’ (WCHP), equating weight with health and perpetuating stigma, blame and exclusion experienced by those beyond ‘healthy’ BMIs. Alternative approaches propose a ‘weight-inclusive health paradigm’ (WIHP), advocating salutogenic, compassionate healthcare.

title: IFPHPOS0045 Bridging the Gap Between National Guidance and Frontline Practice: A Study of Social Workers’ Implementation of NICE Guidelines on Self-Harm with Children in Care
creator: Gill Lever, Christopher J Armitage, Dawn Dowding, Dharman Jeyasingham
description: BackgroundSelf-harm among children in care is substantially higher than in the general population. The NICE self-harm guidelines (2022) aim to improve the quality and consistency of care across all services, including children’s social care. A rapid review identified a lack of evidence on how national self-harm guidance is implemented within children’s social care.

title: Predicting and Treating Pulmonary Fibrosis with Proteomic Biomarker Investigations
creator: Giulia Raineri, Anna Valeria Samarelli, Roberto Tonelli, Valentina Masciale, Beatrice Aramini, Tiziana Petrachi, Giulia Bruzzi, Filippo Gozzi, Ester Trasforini, Angela Esposito, Filippo Azzali, Massimo Dominici, Albino Eccher, Stefania Cerri, Enrico Clini, M Walid Qoronfleh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, rare, and fatal disease that is the consequence of aberrant remodeling and defective repair mechanisms within the lung, culminating in the loss of alveolar integrity. Although significant progress has been made in understanding the pathogenesis, it would be crucial to identify biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and prediction of therapy response to improve the management of this challenging and debilitating disease.

title: IFPHOR0046 parkrun and People Who Access Services – A Public Health Initiative Reducing Illness and Inequalities
creator: Katy Cleece, Michael Holt
description: BackgroundObesity is one of the largest public health challenges globally, costing the NHS £3.2 billion per year. Obesity and wellbeing are intrinsically linked, with each negatively impacting on the other. Physical activity reduces obesity related disease and illnesses and improves physical and mental health.

title: IFPHOR0054 A Roadmap for Post-Crisis Health System Recovery in Gaza Based on the WHO Health System Building Blocks Framework
creator: Othman Alagha, Neil Southern
description: BackgroundThis study addresses the critical gap between theoretical frameworks and actionable strategies for health system recovery in the Gaza following the 2023 crisis. The research aims to create a comprehensive and contextualized roadmap for reconstructing Gaza’s devastated health system using the WHO Health System Building Blocks framework.

title: IFPHOR0095 Data-Sharing Barriers in Zoonotic Disease Surveillance: Why Human and Animal Systems Still Operate in Silos
creator: Astra Ralph Dsouza, Srishtika Mohana Ganesh Murthy, Sahithya Ranganatha
description: BackgroundZoonotic threats require rapid detection across human, animal and environmental sectors, yet surveillance systems often remain fragmented. Delays in sharing information between public health and veterinary services can weaken early warning, slow response and increase the risk of spillover events escalating into larger outbreaks.

title: IFPHPOS0037 Maternal Decision-Making Autonomy’s Influence on Polio Vaccine Delivery Modality in Pakistan: A National Cross-Sectional Study using HIES 2024-25
creator: Ribal Ahmed, Aelita Pyagay, Safa Azzawi, Sunyoung Kim
description: BackgroundPakistan remains one of the last countries with endemic poliovirus, with persistent immunity gaps despite intensive eradication efforts. The influence of maternal decision-making autonomy on mode of polio vaccination (campaign interaction vs non-campaign interaction) is under-researched. We therefore examined the association of maternal decision-making autonomy and mode of polio vaccination for under-5s in Pakistan.

title: IFPHOR0036 Reducing Justice System Inequities in Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD): Evidence From Six Countries
creator: David Junior Gilbert, Natalie Novick Brown, Paul Connor, Gisli Gudjonsson, Jacqueline Pei, Anita Gibbs, Hayley Passmore, Christie Petrenko, Carmela Pestell, Grace Tan, Valerie McGinn, Joanna Chu, Kaitlyn McLachlan, Mansfield Mela, Patience Udonsi, Clare Allely, Raja Mukherjee, Penny A Cook
description: BackgroundIndividuals with Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) are up to nineteen times more likely to come into contact with the criminal justice system (CJS), reflecting a critical public health and safeguarding concern. Interrogative suggestibility and confabulation are theorised mechanisms heightening risk during investigative encounters, yet experimental evidence with young people remains limited.

title: IFPHPOS0056 Digital Panopticon: Artificial Intelligence in Public Health from the Perspective of Foucault’s Biopower to Deleuze’s Societies of Control
creator: Sadra Valiee, Fatemeh Homayounifar
description: IntroductionThe future of public health is increasingly inseparable from artificial intelligence (AI). Yet AI in public health is not solely a technical phenomenon. It is deeply implicated in the governance of bodies and populations, raising urgent questions about surveillance, power, and autonomy.

title: IFPHPOS0035 Public Health Learning Hubs in a Local Authority, A Forum for Multidisciplinary Learning and Problem-Solving
creator: Gethin P Hopkin, Muna Abdel Aziz
description: BackgroundSharing multidisciplinary perspectives to address challenges is integral to effective public health practice. Using Kline’s “Time to Think” principles and adapting a programme used elsewhere in public health registrar training and consultant professional development, we established multidisciplinary Public Health Learning Hubs in a local authority public health team.

title: IFPHOR0069 The Global Opioid Access Divide: A Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Ecological Analysis of Consumption Inequality, Health System Determinants, and Drug Composition Across 201 Countries, 2015–2023
creator: Abdul Rhaman Kafagi
description: BackgroundGlobal opioid analgesic access is profoundly inequitable, with 5.5 billion people living in countries with little or no access to controlled medicines for pain and palliative care. Comprehensive multi-country analyses identifying modifiable health system drivers of this divide remain limited.MethodsA retrospective cross-sectional and longitudinal ecological analysis of country-level opioid consumption was conducted across 201 countries from 2015–2023.

title: Combined Subcision and Low‐Volume Diluted Calcium Hydroxylapatite for Gluteal Cellulite: A Three‐Patient Case Series
creator: Andrea Acevedo, Luis Alberto Parra, Juan Sebastian Rodriguez Cabrales, Valentina Dicker, Lina Velasquez, Andrea Marcela Parra
description: al modalities seldom achieve durable correction, and high‐volume biostimulator protocols remain financially inaccessible to most patients in low‐resource settings. We describe a combined, low‐volume protocol pairing subcision with diluted calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA; Radiesse, Merz Pharmaceuticals GmbH, Frankfurt, Germany) for gluteal cellulite in three women. Three female patients (ages 30–37) with gluteal cellulite were treated by a single practitioner.

title: The Role of the CCR5 Receptor in Neuropathic Pain Modulation: Current Insights and Therapeutic Implications
creator: Mario García-Domínguez, Mats B Eriksson, Anders O Larsson
description: Neuropathic pain, a chronic condition arising from injury or dysfunction of the somatosensory nervous system, is characterized by persistent hypersensitivity and spontaneous pain. The chemokine receptor CCR5 (C-C motif chemokine receptor 5) has recently been identified as a critical mediator in neuroinflammation and neuropathic pain signaling pathways.

title: Association Between Injury Etiology and Scar Outcomes: A Retrospective Clinical Study
creator: Runzhi Huang, Leibing Zhang, Mingkun Ma, Dayuan Xu, Hongda Bi, Shizhao Ji
description: BackgroundWhile scar formation significantly impacts the quality of life post‐injury, the prognostic value of the initial injury etiology remains uncertain. This study aimed to elucidate the relationship between injury etiology and scar prognosis, and to develop a clinically applicable predictive tool and clinical treatment strategies.

title: The Effect of Academic Environment on Turnover Intention of High-Skilled Scientific and Technology Professionals: Empirical Evidence from China’s First-Class Universities
creator: Xiuliang Dai, Lijian Wang, Dan Chen, Xiaoyu Guo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The study constructs a theoretical framework for how the academic environment and job satisfaction affect the turnover intention of high-skilled science and technology talents (STPs), based on academic ecology theory and job satisfaction theory. Conducting a quantitative analysis based on survey data collected from 482 national-level STP recipients across 14 first-class universities, the study integrates descriptive statistics, ANOVA, OLS regression, and bias-corrected bootstrap mediation analysis to examine the relationships between these variables.

title: O-17 - 1 UNDERSTANDING AND PREVENTING HARMS CAUSED BY CLIMATE CHANGE RISKS IN PRISONS IN WALES
creator: Mr Adam Davies, Dr Benjamin Gray, Dr Aimée Challenger, Dr Stephanie Perrett, Mr Kristian James
description: BackgroundRisks to prison settings from climate change (CC) have been identified through UK and Wales risk assessment (CCRA) processes. Published evidence of health risks of CC to prisoners and staff is limited. Risks include heat related deaths, flooding, severe weather damaging buildings, power outages, and risks to food and water supply.

title: O-02 - TARGETED METAGENOMIC ANALYSIS OF CAUSES OF INFLUENZA-LIKE AND RESPIRATORY ILLNESS IN HEALTHCARE WORKERS IN THE UK, WINTER 2025/26: THE SIREN PREPARE AND DETECT STUDY
creator: Ms Sarah Foulkes, Ms Katie Bellis, Ms Marissa Knoll, Ms Katie Munro, Dr Irina Lut, Ms Quisha Bustamante, Mr Jameel Khawam, Mr Jesus Fresno, Ms Angela Dunne, Ms Sophie Russell, Ms Omoyeni Adebiyi, Dr Jasmin Islam, Dr Ana Atti, Dr Ewan Harrison, Dr Victoria Hall
description: BackgroundHealthcare workers (HCWs) have increased risk of respiratory infections, which contributes to pressures on healthcare systems and makes them a valuable population for surveillance.ObjectivesWe used targeted metagenomic sequencing, to understand the range of viruses associated with respiratory illness in HCWs in winter 2025/26.

title: Does Diabetes Matter? The Efficacy of PRP on the Quality of Life in Stress Urinary Incontinence
creator: Andreea Borislavschi, Răzvan-Cosmin Petca, Aida Petca
description: Background: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is quite common in women, impairing the quality of life. Diabetes mellitus may exacerbate pelvic floor dysfunction and alter treatment response. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is a regenerative option to treat SUI; however, data in women with diabetes are limited. This prospective, non-randomized comparative cohort study evaluated PRP outcomes in diabetic versus non-diabetic women with SUI.

title: O-26 - IMPROVING SUPPORT FOR SEX WORKERS IN WALSALL RESEARCH PROJECT. INSIGHTS FROM LIVED EXPERIENCE AND LOCAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND COMMISSIONERS
creator: Mr Nigel Smith, Ms Danielle Jayes
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSex workers in Walsall experience significant and intersecting health inequalities shaped by stigma, trauma, unstable housing, policing practices, fragmented services, and inconsistent access to mental health support.ObjectivesThis study was coproduced by UKHSA West Midlands, Walsall Council, and Changing Lives.

title: PS-08 - UKHSA FIELD SERVICES RAPID INVESTIGATION TEAM: ACTIVITY AND EARLY IMPACT
creator: Mrs Oluwakemi Olufon, Mr Neil Bray, Ms Carmellie Inzoungou-Massanga, Ms Florence Halford, Ms Eve Matthews, Ms Anita Shah, Mr Motolani Awokoya, Mr Saravana Kumar Kothandan, Ms Deepti Kumar
description: BackgroundThe Field Services Rapid Investigation Team (RIT), established in 2022, is the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA’s) national, multidisciplinary, deployable rapid response service. RIT adds to UKHSA’s response capability, working alongside regional Health Protection Teams and the global PHRST to respond to complex and enhanced incidents.

title: Corneal Epithelial Tissue Engineering Strategy Based on Cell Viability Optimization: A Review and Prospects
creator: Guoguo Tang, Miaomiao Chi, Yang Zhai, Rongmei Peng, Jing Hong
description: Corneal transplantation is often considered the last resort for severe corneal epithelial disorders, especially limbal stem cell deficiency (LSCD). Tissue engineering offers novel strategies to mitigate the shortage of corneal transplant donors. However, low cell viability and compromised functionality in tissue engineering represent a major challenge. In this review, we describe the key characteristics required for corneal epithelium bioscaffolds.

title: PS-26 - EVOLVING MPOX EPIDEMIOLOGY IN ENGLAND, 2023–2026
creator: Celine El Hakim, Miss Holly Fountain, Mrs Katy Sinka
description: BackgroundFollowing the 2022 mpox outbreak, case numbers in England remained low. However, an increase in November 2025 preceded a sharp increase in early 2026. Several factors contributed, evidence of an evolving epidemiological picture.ObjectiveDescribe epidemiological changes in mpox cases reported in England, focusing on transmission dynamics, demographics, and viral clades.

title: O-09 EVALUATING PERFORMANCE OF GROUP A STREPTOCOCCAL LATERAL FLOW DEVICES IN CARE HOME OUTBREAKS IN ENGLAND: A PILOT STUDY, AUTUMN 2025
creator: Ms Eve Matthews, Joshua Carter, Clare Sawyer, Carmellie Inzoungou-Massanga, Motolani Awokoya, Neil Bray, Oluwakemi Olufon, Rohini Manuel, Theresa Lamagni, Obaghe Edeghere, Deepti Kumar
description: BackgroundGroup A Streptococcus (GAS) outbreaks in care homes lead to significant morbidity among residents. In 2025, 36 iGAS care home outbreaks were reported in England, throat swabs for culture were collected in 56% of these. Lateral flow devices (LFDs) offer rapid GAS detection for prompt initiation of control measures. LFD sensitivity and specificity for detecting asymptomatic carriage is unknown.

title: PMP22-Related Neuropathies: A Systematic Review
creator: Carlo Alberto Cesaroni, Laura Caiazza, Giulia Pisanò, Martina Gnazzo, Giulia Sigona, Susanna Rizzi, Agnese Pantani, Daniele Frattini, Carlo Fusco
description: Background. PMP22-related neuropathies comprise a spectrum of predominantly demyelinating disorders, most commonly Charcot–Marie–Tooth type 1A (CMT1A; 17p12 duplication) and hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies (HNPP; 17p12 deletion), with rarer phenotypes due to PMP22 sequence variants (CMT1E, Dejerine–Sottas syndrome [DSS]). Methods. We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review (PROSPERO ID: 1139921) of PubMed and Scopus (January 2015–August 2025).

title: O-39 - EMERGENT VECTOR BORNE DISEASES DON’T RESPECT BOUNDARIES – A NEED FOR ONE HEALTH IN ACTION
creator: Dr Zoe Willems, Prof Dominic Mellor, Dr Kate Smith, Dr Sally Mavin, Dr Sophie El-Nahas, Sarah McLeod, Prof Jim McMenamin, Prof Catherine Moore, Dr Luis Morelo, Dr Rachel Cloke
description: BackgroundEmerging Vector Borne Diseases cannot be dealt with by any one institution or country alone. One Health advocates collaborative working to prevent, prepare for and respond to disease threats. ‘On paper’ this is the best approach, but how does that work in reality? Silos still exist, and not just those demarcated by geographical boundaries.

title: A Case Report: Identification of a Pathogenic Microdeletion at Chromosome 21q21.3q22.13 Using Whole-Exome Sequencing and CNV Analysis in a Moroccan Child with Global Developmental Delay
creator: Farah Jouali, Ghyzlane El Haddoumi, Imane Antra, Rachid Benhida, Afaf Ben Itto, Jamal Fekkak
description: Copy number variations (CNVs) affecting the chromosomal region 21q21.3–q22.13 are rare and have been increasingly associated with neurodevelopmental abnormalities and multisystemic manifestations. In this study, we aimed to characterize the clinical, genomic, and genotype–phenotype correlations of a Moroccan child carrying a de novo microdeletion in this region.

title: Study on Safe Filler Injection Techniques Using Cutting‐Edge Ultrasound Technology
creator: Won Lee, Benjamin Ascher, Kyu‐Ho Yi, Ji‐Soo Kim, Audrey Melin, Seong Hwan Kim
description: BackgroundRecently, the development of an ultrasound device connected to a finger probe has enabled real‐time ultrasound‐guided filler injection. We aimed to evaluate the feasibility, clinical applicability, and patient satisfaction associated with the use of a novel real‐time finger‐held Doppler ultrasound system as a guide for hyaluronic acid filler injection.

title: O-56 - INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS: NATIONAL INSIGHTS FROM ACROSS THE HEALTH PROTECTION SYSTEM IN ENGLAND
creator: Dr Enrique Castro-Sanchez, Ms Stephanie Davis, Ms Shwetha Wevita, Dr Joanna Harris, Dr Jude Robinson
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCommunity infection prevention and control (IPC) in England is delivered through a complex system involving UKHSA Health Protection Teams (HPTs), local authorities, NHS partners, and contracted providers, with variation across community and non-NHS settings.ObjectivesTo inform a national IPC education and capability-building strategy, we analysed findings from the Future of the Health Protection System (FHPS) Co-Design Group survey to identify challenges and opportunities for improvement.MethodsOpen-ended responses from 192 respondents across the English health protection system were collected between August and October 2024.

title: Shikonin-Loaded Nanoparticles Attenuate Particulate Matter-Induced Skin Injury by Inhibiting Oxidative Stress and Inflammation
creator: Feifei Huang, Qinghua Tang, Ke Wang, Lingmei Zhou, Ruiwei Liao, Zhuoya Wang, Yan Li, Lin Zhou, Ming Li
description: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) poses a major threat to skin health, yet effective prevention strategies remain limited. Shikonin, a naphthoquinone derived from Lithospermum erythrorhizon, exhibits potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. However, its therapeutic application is limited by low bioavailability.

title: PS-14 - 2023-2025 HEPATITIS A OUTBREAK ACROSS EU AND UK ASSOCIATED WITH FRESH BERRIES WITH POTENTIAL ONGOING SEASONAL RISK: A RETROSPECTIVE CASE-CASE STUDY ACROSS THE FOUR NATIONS
creator: Mr Sawyer Patterson, Jin-Min Yuan, David Leeman, Koye Balogun, Tatiana Garcia Vilaplana, Neville Verlander, Siew Lin Ngui, Andre Charlett, Andrew Nelson, Alison Smith-Palmer, Caitlin McCarthy, Samantha Shepherd, Rory Gundson, Danielle McMichael, Patrick McAleavey, Miranda Mindlin
description: BackgroundIn 2025, a cluster of genetically-linked non-travel hepatitis A cases was identified in the UK and EU, phylogenetically clustering with historic hepatitis A sequences from travellers returning from Morocco. Food histories were routinely collected from the non-travel hepatitis A cases. An incident management team (IMT) was established, convening the public health agencies of the five nations and Food Standards Agency.

title: P-93 - WASTEWATER BASED EPIDEMIOLOGY FOR ILLICIT DRUG SURVEILLANCE IN A SMALL ISLAND COMMUNITY: TRENDS, RISKS, AND HARM REDUCTION POTENTIAL
creator: Dr Rebecca Rowley, Ms Theresa Thornton, Dr Matt Tyrer
description: BackgroundSmall island communities experience unique challenges around illicit drug use. Geographic barriers create fluctuating supply, contributing to high levels of poly-drug use and increased overdose risk. Limited routine health data and restricted testing of seized substances further constrain understanding of population drug trends.

title: Intracranial Injury Caused by Transorbital Penetrating Trauma: An E-Scooter Brake Handle as an Unusual Culprit
creator: Paweł Szczurowski, Michał Gontarz, Jarosław Polak, Jakub Bargiel, Krzysztof Gąsiorowski, Kamil Nelke, Grażyna Wyszyńska-Pawelec, Caroline Schnakers
description: Transorbital penetrating intracranial injuries are a rare but life-threatening subset of penetrating head traumas. While isolated cases caused by bicycle brake handles have been reported, often with fatal outcomes, this is the first documented case of such an injury caused by an electric scooter (e-scooter) brake handle.

title: Aflatoxins in Mexican Maize Systems: From Genetic Resources to Agroecological Resilience and Co-Occurrence with Fumonisins
creator: Carlos Muñoz-Zavala, Obed Solís-Martínez, Jessica Berenice Valencia-Luna, Kai Sonder, Ana María Hernández-Anguiano, Natalia Palacios-Rojas
description: Aflatoxins (AFs) and fumonisins (FUMs) are among the most prevalent and toxic mycotoxins affecting maize production globally. In Mexico, their co-occurrence poses a significant public health concern, as maize is not only a dietary staple but also predominantly grown and consumed at the household level.

title: O-48 - ESTIMATING THE BURDEN OF SHIGA TOXIN-PRODUCING ESCHERICHIA COLI (STEC) IN SCOTLAND – A DATA LINKAGE STUDY (2015-2023)
creator: Ms Susan Brownlie, Dr Alison Smith-Palmer, Dr Lesley Allison, Dr Anne Holmes, Dr Jane Horne, Dr Jacqui McElhiney
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe incidence of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) in Scotland has been consistently high compared to other comparable countries, with the burden unevenly distributed across the population of Scotland.ObjectivesTo use data linkage to provide a detailed insight into the burden of infection of STEC in Scotland, including factors associated with severe clinical presentation, hospitalisation rates and duration, HUS and longer-term sequelae.

title: PS-15 - THE PRINCIPAL HEALTH PROTECTION PRACTITIONER (PHPP) NETWORK: STRATEGIC SYSTEM LEADERSHIP STRENGTHENING HEALTH PROTECTION PRACTICE AND DRIVING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACROSS UKHSA HEALTH PROTECTION IN REGIONS (HPIR)
creator: Ms Laura Pomeroy, Ms Cassie Gregory, Ms Anita Turley, Ms Suzanne Calvert, Ms Rachael Kain, Ms Penelope Edwards, Mr Mohammud Edoo, Ms Joanna Keal, Ms Sarah Dowle, Ms Elizabeth Knapper, Ms Kate McPhedran, Ms Jaime Morgan, Mr Robert Seremani, Ms Valerie Unsworth, Ms Luisa Walker
description: BackgroundThe Principal Health Protection Practitioner (PHPP) role varies across Regions in line with local business models, but retains consistent core functions. PHPPs are members of Regional Senior Leadership/Management Teams and provide professional leadership to Health Protection Practitioners (HPPs), the largest workforce group in Health Protection Teams.

title: PS-10 - MASS CASUALTY PLANS FOR A RESILIENT HEALTH AND SOCIAL CARE SYSTEM: WHAT RISKS AND IMPACTS DO PLANNERS CONSIDER
creator: Dr Padraig Lyons, Professor Kate Cochrane
description: BackgroundMass casualty incidents (MCIs) such as major accidents, fires, or other natural disasters present multifaceted challenges that can rapidly overwhelm health and social care systems. Existing service pressures within health and social care services raise concerns about the adaptability and sustainability of current mass casualty planning approaches, including how recovery is addressed.

title: O-45 - THE HSE DNE BLOOD BORNE VIRUS (BBV) TEST & TREAT PROGRAMME FOR REFUGEES AND APPLICANTS SEEKING PROTECTION (RASPS) USING RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TESTING (RDT)
creator: Dr Sarah Murray, Dr Elizabeth O'Donoghue, Dr Douglas Hamilton, Dr Ksenia Davenport
description: BackgroundIn recent years there has been a significant increase in people seeking International Protection in Ireland (1), mirroring the global migration trend (2). These populations often come from countries with higher prevalence rates of communicable diseases, and under-resourced healthcare systems. Additionally, they are a highly mobile population, often without access to a regular GP.

title: Electron Density and Effective Atomic Number as Quantitative Biomarkers for Differentiating Malignant Brain Tumors: An Exploratory Study with Machine Learning
creator: Tsubasa Nakano, Daisuke Hirahara, Tomohito Hasegawa, Kiyohisa Kamimura, Masanori Nakajo, Junki Kamizono, Koji Takumi, Masatoyo Nakajo, Fumitaka Ejima, Ryota Nakanosono, Ryoji Yamagishi, Fumiko Kanzaki, Hiroki Muraoka, Nayuta Higa, Hajime Yonezawa, Ikumi Kitazono, Jihun Kwon, Gregor Pahn, Eran Langza
description: Simple SummaryElectron density and effective atomic number derived from dual-energy CT have been used in various clinical applications, but their usefulness for brain tumor diagnosis remains unestablished. We investigated the potential utility of these novel CT parameters in differentiating brain metastases, glioblastomas, and primary central nervous system lymphomas.

title: O-40 - AN OVERVIEW OF THE UK HEALTH SECURITY AGENCY’S (UKHSA) HORIZON SCANNING PROCESS FOR ZOONOTIC INFLUENZAS (ZI)
creator: Miss Annabel Ridsdale, Dr Onyi Emefiene, Dr Liam Fitzpatrick, Dr Yingfen Hsia, Mr Varun Sathiyendra, Dr Sakib Rokadiya, Dr Angie Lackenby, Dr Richard Puleston, Dr Sophia Makki
description: BackgroundEmerging respiratory infections are a major threat to global health security. The UKHSA national Acute Respiratory Infections team undertake horizon scanning (HS) as a proactive, systematic approach to identify emerging national and international respiratory threats to human health. Zoonotic Influenza (ZI) signals are routinely reviewed, risk assessed and escalated to ensure timely public health actions.

title: Harnessing Metabolomics to Advance Nutrition-Based Therapeutics for Inflammation: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials
creator: Belén Carlino, Gerardo N Guerrero-Flores, Camila Niclis, Gina Segovia-Siapco, Martín L Mayta, Ivana Šarac, Marija Paunovic, Marija Takić
description: Background/Objectives: The association between plasma metabolites derived from dietary substrates and inflammatory processes remains underexplored, despite its potential relevance in the prevention of non-communicable diseases. This systematic review aimed to examine the relationship between blood metabolites and the modulation of inflammatory biomarkers.

title: PS-02 - OUTBREAK MANAGEMENT AND INCIDENT RESPONSE: PUBLIC HEALTH INVESTIGATION OF BOTULISM CASES ASSOCIATED WITH UNLICENSED COSMETIC BOTULINUM TOXIN USE
creator: Mrs Samantha Charlesworth, Mrs Sara Coy, Dr James McGowan
description: BackgroundBotulism is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition requiring rapid identification and coordinated public health action. In 2025, an unexpected increase in suspected botulism cases was identified in the East of England, prompting a regional and national health protection response.

title: Does Intraoperative Navigation Improve K-Wire Positioning in Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty?—A New Approach
creator: Timo Blaszczyk, Georg Gosheger, Jonathan Wohlmuth, Vincent Hofbauer, Eugenio Jannelli
description: Background/Objectives: In reverse shoulder arthroplasty (RSA), precise K-wire positioning of the glenoid component is critical to prevent complications such as glenoid loosening or instability as well as premature implant failure. Optimal component placement must adhere to individualized preoperative plans to account for patient-specific anatomical conditions.

title: Harnessing Probiotics to Combat Candidiasis: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Future Directions
creator: Emma Wright, Nisha Valand, Umakhanth Venkatraman Girija
description: Candida species are common commensals within the human microbiome but can transition opportunistically to pathogenic states when host–microbe homeostasis is disrupted. Their ability to adhere to mucosa and implanted medical devices, form thick biofilms, and invade epithelial tissues makes candidiasis particularly harmful in immunocompromised and elderly populations.

title: Automated measurement of cardiomyocyte monolayer contraction using the Exeter Multiscope
creator: Sharika Mohanan, David Horsell, Taylor Watters, Mohammadreza Ghasemi, Lewis Henderson, Caroline Müllenbroich, Gil Bub, Francis Burton, Godfrey Smith, Alexander D Corbett
description: Previously, we introduced a microscope design that enabled rapid, random-access well plate imaging [ eLife, 10, e56426 (2021) 10.7554/eLife.56426 ]. Here, we implement this design in a low-cost, compact, and portable prototype (the Exeter Multiscope) and apply it to the problem of capturing the contraction of cardiomyocyte monolayers, which have been plated into nine wells within a 96-well plate.

title: Documentation of Adverse Social Drivers of Health in US Emergency Departments
creator: Melanie F Molina, Rebecca E Cash, Janice A Espinola, Krislyn M Boggs, Carlos A Camargo, Margaret E Samuels-Kalow
description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to characterize emergency department (ED)-based policies related to documentation of adverse social drivers of health (aSDOH) among a national sample of US EDs.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional survey of ED leaders from a 5% stratified random sample of US EDs (n = 280) from January to October 2023.

title: Sex-Specific Morphological and Neuromuscular Profiles of U-15 Colombian Basketball Players
creator: Alex Ojeda-Aravena, María Alejandra Camacho-Villa, Fernando Millan-Domingo, Ronald Quintero-Bernal, Jeimy Andrea Merchán, Fabio Villafrades, Adrián De la Rosa, Stefania Toselli, Luciana Zaccagni, Natascia Rinaldo
description: Background: Basketball performance is highly dependent on morphological and neuromuscular traits, especially during adolescence, when rapid growth and maturation generate marked sex-based differences. However, limited data are available on Latin American players’ performance. This study aimed to compare the anthropometric characteristics, body composition, somatotype, and neuromuscular performance of male and female Colombian U-15 national basketball players.

title: O-11 - EXAMINING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN SENTINEL RESPIRATORY SURVEILLANCE AND ANTIBIOTIC PRESCRIBING IN SCOTLAND: ANALYSIS OF INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL LINKED DATA
creator: Dr Ronan McCabe, Dr Helen Gadegaard, Dr Kimberly Marsh, Dr Josie Evans
description: BackgroundGP practices registered to Scotland’s Community Acute Respiratory Infection (CARI) sentinel surveillance programme have reported that access to CARI’s 10 pathogen (predominantly viral) respiratory testing panel, with results available within 7-10 days, supports antimicrobial stewardship by helping ensure that patients with ARI receive the most clinically appropriate treatment.ObjectivesWe examined this association using individual-level linked data.

title: A Prospective Cohort Study Comparing Microscopy and Culture in the Diagnosis of Superficial Fungal Skin Infections
creator: Amelia Yuting Monteiro, Hui Mei Cheng, Larissa Lim, Jiun Yit Pan, Kun Liang, Hong Liang Tey, Antoni Torres
description: Superficial fungal skin infections are common but often misdiagnosed, which may result in inappropriate treatment and the worsening of symptoms. An accurate and timely diagnosis is essential to differentiate these infections from similar conditions such as secondary syphilis, annular psoriasis, and pityriasis rosea.

title: Right ventricular dysfunction in structural tricuspid interventions
creator: Jonathan Lee, Eirini Beneki, Nikolaos Katsanakis, Edoardo Zancanaro, Monica Mukherjee, Edgar Argulian, Julia Grapsa
description: With the growing global adoption of transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI) and the increasing number of available devices, a comprehensive understanding of right heart dysfunction has become essential. Right heart dysfunction is frequently observed both before and after TTVI and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes.

title: P-58 - TUBERCULOSIS CASES REPORTED TO THE PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCY IN NORTHERN IRELAND: A RETROSPECTIVE ANALYSIS OF NOTIFICATION SOURCES AND TIMELINESS OVER 1-YEAR PERIOD
creator: Dr Corey Magee, Dr Jillian Johnston
description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) is a leading global cause of preventable infectious deaths. Timely notification of TB cases is essential to facilitate prompt public health action and prevent onward transmission. This study reviewed TB notifications reported to the Public Health Agency (PHA) in Northern Ireland (NI) over a 1-year period to describe notification sources and timeliness.

title: Adjuvante Systemtherapie beim Melanom in der Praxis: Multizentrische Erhebung an 51 DeCOG‐Hautkrebszentren
creator: Markus Reitmajer, Elisabeth Livingstone, Lucie Heinzerling, Kai‐Martin Thoms, Frank Meiss, Markus V Heppt, Anja Gesierich, Konstantin Drexler, Friedegund Meier, Max Schlaak, Andrea Forschner, Lisa Zimmer
description: ZusammenfassungHintergrundAdjuvante Immuncheckpoint‐Inhibitoren (ICI) und zielgerichtete Therapien (targeted therapy, TT) haben das Therapiemanagement für Patienten mit Melanom grundlegend verändert. Die aktuelle deutsche S3‐Leitlinie unterscheidet jedoch nicht zwischen Patienten mit und ohne adjuvante Therapie in ihren Empfehlungen zu Bildgebungsintervallen und der Nachsorge nach Beendigung der adjuvanten Therapie. Dies führt zu uneinheitlichen Vorgehensweisen zwischen den Hautkrebszentren.

title: Study protocol: A randomized controlled trial of a community-based intervention on clinical parameters, health literacy, medication adherence, and quality of life among individuals with coexisting diabetes and hypertension
creator: Krishna Kumari Samantaray, Sasmita Das, Krushna Chandra Sahoo, N Siva
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). • Ms Krishna Kumari Samantaray: • Dr Sasmita Das and Dr Krushna Chandra Sahoo: • Dr N. Siva: Keywords: Community-based intervention, Diabetes, Hypertension, Medication adherence, Health Literacy, Quality of Life Specifications table Subject areaNursing and MedicineMore specific subject areaCommunity-based care for chronic diseases (Diabetes and Hypertension)Name of protocolCommunity-Based intervention (CBI) for Individuals with Coexisting Diabetes and HypertensionReagents/tools / Instruments- Sociodemographic proforma and Clinical Profile Form- Digital Sphygmomanometer (BP measurement)- Standardized Glucometer (Random Blood Sugar Test)- Modified Diabetes and Hypertension Health Literacy Scale-

title: Berufskrankheit „Hautkrebs durch UV‐Strahlung“ – eindeutige Fakten, heterogene Konsequenzen
creator: Werner Aberer, Rainer Hofmann‐Wellenhof, Norbert Sepp, Barbara Ebner, Swen‐Malte John
description: medizinische Herausforderung dar, insbesondere bei Tätigkeiten im Freien. Trotz alarmierender Erkrankungsraten und klarer wissenschaftlicher Evidenz zur Ätiologie werden aber das SCC und seine Vorstufen nicht in allen Staaten als Berufskrankheit anerkannt. Die gesetzgeberischen Maßnahmen divergieren stark – von völliger Ignoranz bis zur Etablierung umfassender Präventions‐ und Entschädigungsprogramme. 1 Dieses Ungleichgewicht beruht oftmals auf mangelndem Problembewusstsein und niedrigen Melderaten.

title: Outcomes of Forehead Flap Reconstruction in 3,368 Nicotine-Dependent vs Non-Dependent Patients: A Retrospective Cohort with Propensity Score-Matched Analysis
creator: Yousef Tanas, Philong Nguyen, Joshua Wang, Keyvon Rashidi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the TriNetX global health research network. Patients undergoing forehead reconstruction with preservation of vascular pedicle (e.g., axial pattern flap, paramedian forehead flap) between January 2000 and February 2023 were categorized into two cohorts: those with nicotine dependence documented within 6 months before surgery (n = 1,704) and those without nicotine use (n = 5,004). Both arms had a follow-up of 1 year.

title: Fabric–elasticity relationships of femoral head trabecular bone are similar in Type 2 diabetes and non-diabetic individuals
creator: Mathieu Simon, Sasidhar Uppuganti, Jeffry S Nyman, Philippe Zysset
description: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a chronic disease leading to an elevated glucose level in the blood and increased fracture risk. Because T2D individuals tend to have normal to higher areal bone mineral density (aBMD) than healthy individuals, their fracture risk is often underestimated.

title: No. 11 Blade‐Based Surgical Techniques for Steatocystoma Multiplex: A Systematic Review
creator: Jia Qi Adam Bai, Sherilyn Wen, Aleksandra Frątczak, Chaocheng Liu
description: l approaches using a No. 11 blade to create a small incision followed by expression and removal of the cyst wall have increasingly been reported as a promising therapy with favorable cosmetic outcomes. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of No. 11 blade‐based surgical techniques for the treatment of SM.

title: KRT23 promotes proliferation invasion and metastasis of gastric cancer through epithelial-mesenchymal transition mediated by the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway
creator: Yi Xie, Fanghui Zhou, Xuelian Li, Pailan Peng
description: BackgroundGastric cancer (GC) is a highly prevalent and lethal malignancy worldwide. Notwithstanding advances in treatment, suboptimal patient outcomes highlight the urgent need for novel therapeutic targets to improve survival. This study aimed to explore the influence of keratin 23 (KRT23) on the proliferation, migration, and invasion of GC cells, as well as its underlying molecular mechanism.

title: Phytoremediation-agrivoltaic systems for PTEs decontamination: a case study from an industrial site in Augusta, Italy
creator: Michele Di Agosto, Claudio Armaro, Samuele Di Novo, Francesco Salmeri, Nico Randazzo, Francesco Sergi
description: Over the past century, industrial activities have caused widespread soil contamination by potentially toxic elements (PTEs), making effective remediation increasingly urgent. Phytoremediation offers a sustainable strategy using selected plant species to remove, stabilize, or sequester pollutants. This study proposes an integrated agrivoltaic-phytoremediation framework for remediating PTE-contaminated soils.

title: Association between cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome, lifestyle, and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: a prospective cohort study
creator: Mingming Wang, Yanan Qiao, Ruilang Lin, Yongfu Yu, Min Zhao, Marie Standl, Costan G Magnussen, Bo Xi
description: SummaryBackgroundCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is reported to be associated with increased all-cause and CVD-specific mortality. However, the association between CKM and cancer-specific mortality, as well as the modifying or joint effects of healthy lifestyle on mortality remain unclear.MethodsIn this prospective cohort study, we enrolled participants aged 37–73 years from the UK Biobank.

title: Sleep Disturbance as a Mediator Between Self-Reported Nighttime Noise Annoyance and Depression, Anxiety, and Suicide: A Mediation Analysis
creator: Dian-Jeng Li, Cheng-Fang Yen, Cheng-Chia Yang, Hung-En Liao, Yi-Lung Chen
description: Objective:To examine whether sleep disturbance mediates associations between self-reported nighttime noise annoyance and depression, anxiety, and suicide risk in Taiwanese adults.Methods:We analyzed cross-sectional online survey data from 776 Taiwanese adults collected between December 2024 and May 2025. Self-reported nighttime noise annoyance from road traffic, railways, aircraft, and residential building vibrations was assessed on a 5-point verbal scale.
