Epsilon‐near‐zero (ENZ) materials can dramatically enhance local optical fields, enabling nonlinear interactions at relatively low intensities. Yet, near their plasma frequency, isotropic ENZ media remain highly absorptive, limiting nonlinear operations that require good transparency. Longitudinal epsilon‐near‐zero (LENZ) metamaterials, characterized by a vanishing permittivity along the optical axis, provide a promising route to field enhancement while mitigating absorption losses and impedance mismatch.

title: Interfacial Role of Dopant d‐States on Hot Carrier Generation in Bimetallic Nanoparticles
creator: Rania Zaier, Katarzyna Kluczyk‐Korch, Tomasz J Antosiewicz
description: Metallic nanoparticles are of great interest due to a collective localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), which decays through Landau damping and results in a nonthermal distribution of electrons and holes, so‐called hot carriers, the generation and harnessing of which are significant for photocatalysis, photovoltaics, and sensing.

title: Optical Phased Arrays on Photonic Integrated Circuit Platforms: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Applications
creator: Jingwei Li, Yuyuan Han, Aoxiang Chen, Pengpeng Li, Xinglin Zhu, Guanbao Zhao, Luohan Peng, Huaibin Zheng
description: On‐chip optical phased arrays (OPAs) have emerged as a core technology in photonic integrated circuits (PICs), enabling compact, solid‐state, and digitally reconfigurable beam steering with high scalability. By eliminating mechanical motion and leveraging semiconductor fabrication, OPAs provide a versatile platform for large‐aperture and high‐speed optical wavefront control in applications including LiDAR, free‐space optical communication, imaging, and holographic displays.

title: An Active Beam‐Reconfigurable Retrodirective Array
creator: Wen Yue Wei, Yan Shi, Li Jing Yang, Jun Wei Wu, Qiang Feng, Long Li
description: Retrodirective arrays can scatter an arbitrarily incident wave back along its incident direction, demonstrating significant potential for wireless communications. However, traditional retrodirective arrays can only reflect incident waves back along a fixed direction. This inherent constraint restricts their application primarily to point‐to‐point communications. To overcome this constraint, this paper focuses on the study of a beam‐reconfigurable retrodirective array.

title: Global variability in colorectal cancer screening guidelines: panel composition and recommendations
creator: Koki Nakajima, Hiroaki Saito, Yoshitaka Nishikawa
description: ObjectiveColorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Although many countries have developed CRC screening guidelines, how CRC screening guidelines are developed across countries remains unclear. This study examined guideline-development funding, stakeholders, and their conflicts of interest (COI), and compared CRC screening recommendations across Group of Seven (G7) countries.

title: Steroid Injection in Patients With Benign Vocal Fold Lesions: A Meta‐Analysis and Meta‐Regression
creator: Yousef M. Al‐Shammari, Bisher Albesher, Sarah M. Murad, Dhari Altaher, Nourah H. AlGhurair, Ahmad S. Alawadhi, Hasan Alshemari
description: ObjectivesThis study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of steroid injections in patients with benign vocal fold lesions.Data SourcesPubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from January 2000 through December 2025 using predefined terms for benign vocal fold pathology and steroid injection.Review MethodsWe conducted a PRISMA‐guided systematic review and meta‐analysis of studies evaluating steroid injections for benign vocal fold lesions.

title: 炎症小体的翻译后修饰调控机制
creator: 晨阳 何, 平龙 徐, 盛铎 刘
description:
炎症小体是天然免疫中感知病原体和损伤信号、驱动促炎性细胞因子成熟和细胞焦亡的核心平台，其异常活化参与炎症、自身免疫、代谢及神经系统疾病等多种病理过程。近年来，研究逐渐揭示了覆盖炎症小体启动、组装、活化和降解全过程的动态修饰网络：泛素化和去泛素化主要调节炎症小体组分的稳定性、复合体组装和降解；磷酸化和去磷酸化通过激酶-磷酸酶调控NLRP3构象转换、NLRP3与NIMA相关激酶7结合及ASC斑点形成，并调节NLRC4和Pyrin炎症小体活化；乙酰化和去乙酰化、SUMO化和去SUMO化则以位点或亚型特异方式影响炎症小体组装、蛋白质降解及焦亡执行。这些修饰网络共同决定IL-1β和IL-18的成熟、释放及消皮素D介导的焦亡强度。本文综述了炎症小体关键组分的主要修饰类型及调控机制研究进展，讨论了靶向修饰网络的治疗策略和转化难点，以期为炎症相关疾病的机制研究和精准干预提供参考。

炎症是机体抵御病原体入侵及细胞损伤的重要机制，其依赖于免疫细胞中促炎和抗炎基因表达的精密调控。当基因突变或调控失衡时，持续过度的炎症反应会造成炎症部位血管生成、纤维化及组织破坏，诱发炎症相关疾病，影响患者生活质量。虽然生物制剂和小分子靶向药物增加了治疗方案选择，但仍存在免疫原性低、安全性隐患和费用昂贵等问题。以炎症性肠病为例，患者持续缓解率显著低于50%，约30%为原发性无应答，疗效随病程延长和既往治疗失败递减，且基线生物标志物对疗效预测价值有限，难以指导用药［1］。因此，亟需从炎症调控的上游寻找新的治疗突破口。近年来研究发现，蛋白质翻译后修饰可通过泛素化、磷酸化、乙酰化、SUMO化等多层面修饰精准调控炎症小体信号通路，影响多种炎症相关疾病的发生和进展［2-5］。

炎症小体是主要定位于细胞质的多蛋白复合物，由受体蛋白（如NLRP3、NLRC4、AIM2等）、衔接蛋白ASC和效应蛋白caspase-1前体组装而成，是天然免疫系统识别病原体和应激信号的重要平台［6］。受体蛋白感知细胞外不同的病原相关分子模式或损伤相关分子模式，进而招募ASC并激活caspase-1，促进IL-1β前体和IL-18前体剪切为成熟的IL-1β和IL-18，诱导细胞焦亡并启动炎症反应［7］。与上述经典通路比较，非经典炎症小体通路则由caspase-4/5（人源）或caspase-11（鼠源）直接识别细胞内脂多糖并切割GSDMD诱导焦亡，焦亡伴随的钾离子外流可促进NLRP3炎症小体二级激活，放大caspase-1依赖的炎症反应［8］。本文通过综述炎症小体病理性失调导致炎症相关疾病及其翻译后修饰机制研究进展，旨在为炎症相关疾病的治疗策略优化提供理论依据和潜在靶点。

炎症小体病理性失调导致炎症相关疾病

自身炎症性疾病

炎症小体功能获得性突变是自身炎症性疾病的经典致病机制。NLRP1的致病性突变主要累及皮肤和关节，表现为多发性自愈性掌跖癌、家族性慢性苔藓样角化病等多种皮肤相关疾病（附表1）［9-10］。NLRP3炎症小体基因突变与周期性发热综合征相关，突变发生在NLRP3的热蛋白结构域、NACHT和富含亮氨酸重复序列结构域（附表1）［11-18］。其中，Q703K是常见的NLRP3基因突变位点，会引起NLRP3炎症小体异常活化并诱导IL-1β过度释放，进而导致冷吡啉相关周期性综合征等疾病，临床表现为反复发热、皮疹、关节及眼部炎症等［17-18］。NLRC4炎症小体功能获得性突变多发生在肠道和骨髓中，诱发家族性寒冷自身炎症综合征、巨噬细胞活化综合征及婴儿期肠炎等自身炎症性疾病（附表1）［19-27］。Pyrin炎症小体是一种由MEFV基因编码的受体蛋白，突变时可增强炎症小体活化及IL-1β、IL-18分泌，引发家族性地中海热、Pyrin相关自身炎症伴中性粒细胞性皮肤病，当此类突变和家族性地中海热已知致病性突变发生于同一位点时具有累加效应，致使该病在某些家族中呈现显性遗传特征（附表1）［28-30］。

自身免疫病

自身免疫病是机体免疫系统对自身抗原失去耐受导致的持续性免疫反应。炎症小体的基因多态性与疾病易感性相关，其异常活化促进自身免疫病的发生发展。如附表1所示，在炎症性肠病中，NLRP3基因V44I、Q705K及R779C突变显著增加疾病易感性，导致患者肠黏膜组织出现红斑、糜烂及溃疡性病变［31-33］。类风湿关节炎与NLRP3基因rs4612666、rs10754558位点多态性相关［34］，且NLRP3炎症小体主要在滑膜浸润的单核细胞或巨噬细胞中被激活，使用选择性抑制剂MCC950可有效阻断其活化，减轻关节炎症反应及骨破坏程度［35］。NLRC4基因W655S突变可增强ASC寡聚化及IL-1β成熟分泌，促进系统性红斑狼疮的发生［36］。此外，炎症小体通过遗传易感和细胞应答双重机制参与系统性红斑狼疮的发病过程：在遗传层面，NLRP3炎症小体的功能获得性变异（rs10754558）显著增加狼疮性肾炎的风险；在细胞层面，患者单核细胞呈现预激活状态，NLRP1和AIM2等炎症小体组分持续高表达使IL-1β的产生显著增加［37］。

代谢性疾病

NLRP3炎症小体在肥胖、2型糖尿病和非酒精性脂肪性肝病等代谢性疾病的发生发展中发挥桥梁作用。Liu等［38］利用肥胖和健康人群的原代巨噬细胞证实肥胖会导致NLRP3炎症小体过度激活。动物模型研究表明长期高脂饮食会激活NLRP3炎症小体，引起胰岛纤维化和心肌纤维化，并加速椎间盘退变［39-41］。2型糖尿病作为肥胖的重要并发症，NLRP3基因多态性（如rs10925027、rs10754558等）与其发病密切相关，显著影响2型糖尿病及心血管并发症的遗传易感性［42-43］。研究报道，NLRP3和caspase-1抑制剂可有效降低2型糖尿病患者的促炎性细胞因子水平［44］。非酒精性脂肪性肝病是与肥胖及其代谢并发症密切相关的肝脏疾病，NLRP3炎症小体在壳多糖酶3样蛋白1调控下促进肝脏炎症和纤维化［45］。值得关注的是，RNA编辑酶双链RNA特异性腺苷脱氨酶1作为内源性负调控因子可有效抑制NLRP3炎症小体活化，具有潜在疾病治疗价值［46］。

神经系统疾病

NLRP3炎症小体在多种神经系统疾病的神经炎症放大和神经元损伤过程中扮演重要角色。在阿尔茨海默病患者皮质中，硫氧还蛋白相互作用蛋白显著上调，可与β淀粉样蛋白斑块和磷酸化τ蛋白共定位，并通过激活NLRP3炎症小体加剧神经炎症，显示出作为干预靶点的潜力［47］。阿尔茨海默病相关神经炎症还具有显著的细胞类型特异性：小胶质细胞主要依赖经典的NLRP3/caspase-1信号通路，星形胶质细胞可能通过caspase-8介导炎症反应，而锥体神经元则可能通过caspase-4发生焦亡［48］。在帕金森病中，α突触核蛋白聚集体通过激活NLRP3炎症小体驱动神经炎症，而NLRP3基因rs7525979多态性则与帕金森病风险降低相关［49-50］。瑞巴派特（Rebamipide）和黄芩苷均可通过抑制α突触核蛋白介导的NLRP3炎症小体活化减轻神经炎症并保护多巴胺能神经元［51-52］。在肌萎缩侧索硬化中，C9orf72毒性二肽激活小胶质细胞NLRP3炎症小体，加剧神经炎症和神经元损伤，而miR-223作为内源性抑制因子与疾病进展成负相关［53-54］。此外，NLRP3炎症小体活化程度还会影响创伤性脑损伤患者的预后，且肥胖等因素可加重其介导的神经炎症［55-56］。机制上，转录因子CEBPD在损伤神经元中上调，通过激活NLRP3炎症小体及下游GSDMD介导的细胞焦亡加重继发性损伤，抑制CEBPD则具有神经保护作用［57］。

炎症小体翻译后修饰调控机制

泛素化和去泛素化

泛素化是调控炎症小体活性的关键机制，由E1激活酶、E2结合酶和E3连接酶依次催化，通过共价连接K48或K63型泛素链精准调控炎症小体活性，前者介导蛋白酶体降解，后者调控信号复合体组装。去泛素化酶则通过移除泛素链，在炎症小体组装阶段发挥重要作用。见附表2。

在炎症小体组装阶段，卵巢肿瘤去泛素化酶6A可直接结合NLRP3的NACHT结构域，并在K430和K689位点选择性切割K48链，有利于NLRP3炎症小体的稳定性和组装，增加IL-1β分泌并放大炎症反应（图1）［58］；Lys-63特异性去泛素化酶BRCC3和含有Josephin结构域的去泛素化酶JOSD2可使NLRP3-R779C突变体去泛素化，促进炎症小体寡聚化和活化，增加婴儿患早发性炎症性肠病的风险［33］；泛素羧基端水解酶L5通过去除NLRP3的K63链促进炎症小体组装和活化，加剧丙型肝炎病毒感染中的肝脏炎症反应并推动疾病进展［59］。值得注意的是，在USP家族中，去泛素化酶对炎症小体组装的调控呈双向性。正向调控方面，USP7和USP47通过直接促进ASC寡聚化及斑点形成增强NLRP3炎症小体活化［60］；而USP3则通过移除ASC的K174位点上K48链，抑制其蛋白酶体降解并上调ASC水平，为ASC寡聚化及斑点形成提供充足底物［61］。相反，USP25则通过对K63链特异性去泛素化，抑制NLRP3与ASC的相互作用及ASC寡聚化，从而负向调控NLRP3炎症小体活化［62］。此外，一些泛素连接酶也可通过修饰ASC正向调控组装过程：血红素氧化铁调节蛋白2泛素连接酶1可通过线性泛素化修饰ASC促进炎症小体组装［63］；线粒体抗病毒信号蛋白质通过肿瘤坏死因子受体相关因子3亦可对ASC的K174位点上K63链进行泛素化，驱动ASC斑点形成及炎症小体活化［64］。在炎症小体降解阶段，肿瘤坏死因子受体表达上调并竞争性结合MARCH7以抑制NLRP3的K48链泛素化，同时MARCH7促进去乙酰化酶SIRT2降解以提高NLRP3乙酰化水平，最终增强NLRP3炎症小体活化、巨噬细胞焦亡及炎症反应［65］。

泛素化常与磷酸化、乙酰化等其他翻译后修饰协同作用。例如，磷酸甘油酸激酶1经酪蛋白激酶2磷酸化后被激活，进而直接磷酸化NLRP3的S448/S449位点，并招募USP14特异性切除NLRP3的K63链以解除其抑制状态，从而驱动炎症小体组装和活化［66］。然而，泛素化及其交叉修饰在特定病理状态下亦可发挥保护作用，其调控网络还可与表观遗传、表观转录组修饰发生交互作用。如E3泛素蛋白连接酶Pellino同源物1不仅可直接在ASC的K55位点连接K63泛素链，促进ASC与NLRP3相互作用及ASC寡聚化，增强IL-1β分泌［67］，其功能还可受上游RNA m⁶A修饰的间接调控，通过促进Y-box结合蛋白1泛素化抑制NLRP3炎症小体活化，延缓动脉粥样硬化［68］。目前针对泛素化系统的主要干预策略包括调控E3连接酶（如BC-1215）［69］、使用去泛素化酶抑制剂（如Eeyarestatin Ⅰ、b-AP15和WP1130等）［70］和PROTAC技术［71］。Keuler等［71］已成功构建首个靶向NLRP3炎症小体的PROTAC降解剂V2，后者在基础研究和药物研发中具有双重价值。

磷酸化和去磷酸化

磷酸化是一种快速且高度动态的翻译后修饰形式，能够精确调节炎症小体核心组分（如NLRP3和ASC）的构象状态、亚细胞定位及寡聚化进程，从而影响炎症小体的信号启动和组装。如附表2所示，多种激酶和磷酸酶通过磷酸化NLRP3、ASC及Pyrin的酪氨酸或丝氨酸位点动态调控其活性。

在NLRP3炎症小体中，磷酸化调控具有“激酶-磷酸酶-底物”多层次网络特征。启动阶段，TBK1/IKKε磷酸化NLRP3氨基端保守丝氨酸位点（人源Ser5/小鼠Ser3）维持其非活化构象；当病原信号传入时，蛋白磷酸酶2A通过去磷酸化NLRP3以解除TBK1/IKKε的抑制作用［72］。组装阶段，激酶c-Abl和ERK5可通过磷酸化ASC的酪氨酸位点Y146促进ASC斑点形成及NLRP3-ASC共定位（图1）［73-74］；极样激酶1则通过磷酸化NEK7增强NEK7与NLRP3相互作用，驱动炎症小体寡聚化，而抑制剂GSK461364可靶向极样激酶1进而阻断NEK7磷酸化，因此该抑制剂可作为新药候选物［75］。在NLRC4炎症小体中，磷酸化起决定性激活作用。当细胞感染鼠伤寒沙门菌时，蛋白激酶Cδ被快速招募至NLRC4复合物，磷酸化其Ser533位点，诱导构象重排和寡聚化，进而激活caspase-1并触发焦亡［3］。与NLRP3不同，NLRC4的磷酸化位点单一且功能明确，这可能有利于其快速应答细胞病原体感染。在Pyrin炎症小体中，RhoA GTP酶通过激活蛋白激酶N1/N2以磷酸化Pyrin的多个丝氨酸位点并招募14-3-3蛋白，从而阻止Pyrin异常组装并维持其静息状态［76］。当艰难梭菌或鼠疫耶尔森菌分泌的毒素抑制RhoA活性时，触发Pyrin炎症小体去磷酸化和组装以感知病原入侵［77］。这一机制与磷酸化NLRP3的TBK1/IKKε调控类似，均通过激酶-磷酸酶平衡维持免疫稳态。

乙酰化和去乙酰化

乙酰化可促进炎症小体组装和稳定，去乙酰化则可在转录水平（启动阶段）和蛋白质水平（组装和降解阶段）多层次调控炎症小体活性。在炎症小体组装阶段，赖氨酸乙酰转移酶5可介导NLRP3的K24位点乙酰化进而促进NLRP3寡聚化和组装［4］。在前列腺癌中，circAR-3通过招募赖氨酸乙酰转移酶2B增强NLRP3乙酰化，加速癌细胞增殖和炎症反应［78］。Wang等［79］研究显示，在脂多糖刺激的巨噬细胞中，磷酸甘油酸脱氢酶通过消耗烟酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸抑制SIRT1和SIRT3活性，维持组蛋白H3K9/H3K27和炎症小体核心组分NLRP3/ASC的K21/22/24位点的乙酰化水平，促进Toll样受体4转录、NLRP3组装和IL-1β成熟，而该酶缺失可缓解炎症反应（图1）。

目前，SIRT家族和HDAC家族的去乙酰化酶是炎症相关疾病的潜在治疗靶点（附表2）。在SIRT家族中，SIRT2主要定位于细胞质，在巨噬细胞中高表达，通过去乙酰化微管蛋白及多种信号分子参与炎症调控［80］。在衰老相关慢性炎症和胰岛素抵抗中，SIRT2通过去乙酰化NLRP3的K21/K22位点抑制炎症小体组装和脂肪组织炎症，从而逆转慢性炎症状态［81］。SIRT2下调会导致NLRP3炎症小体异常活化，诱发caspase-1依赖性细胞焦亡，减少造血干细胞数并削弱其重建能力［82］。SIRT3主要定位于线粒体，在心脏、肝脏、肾脏等高代谢组织中高表达，通过直接去乙酰化NLRC4的K71/K272位点促进其组装，增强宿主抗感染能力［83］。核定位的SIRT6则通过去乙酰化NLRP3启动子区域组蛋白H3K9引起染色质凝聚，在转录水平抑制NLRP3炎症小体表达，减轻肾小管损伤并延缓糖尿病肾病进展［84］。因此，SIRT2、SIRT3和SIRT6因亚细胞定位、组织分布和底物特异性差异，在炎症小体调控中展现出功能的多样性和互补性，可实现对炎症小体活性的精准调控。

HDAC家族中，HDAC10在免疫细胞中广泛表达，通过直接去乙酰化NLRP3的K496位点，将其修饰状态从乙酰化转为泛素化，进而通过蛋白酶体途径降解NLRP3并缓解急性炎症损伤［85］。HDAC2主要定位于细胞核，通过去除组蛋白H3K27的乙酰化修饰抑制NLRP3基因转录，而Santacruzamate A联合5-氟尿嘧啶或瑞戈非尼可通过抑制HDAC2以增强NLRP3介导的细胞焦亡，发挥抗肿瘤效应［86］。HDAC3在肝脏、肺脏以及免疫细胞中高表达，HDAC3抑制剂BRD3308则可减少NLRP3炎症小体活化和焦亡反应，有效缓解脓毒症诱导的急性肺损伤［87］。

SUMO化和去SUMO化

SUMO化是调控炎症小体活化和细胞焦亡的一种重要且可逆的翻译后修饰，由SUMO连接酶和去SUMO化酶共同维持其动态平衡。SUMO化修饰可通过影响蛋白质的稳定性或互作界面调控炎症小体的组装和活化，而去SUMO化酶则通过移除这些修饰发挥相反的调节作用。如附表2所示，E3连接酶含三联模体蛋白28可促进NLRP3发生SUMO1/2/3修饰，进而抑制其泛素化及蛋白酶体降解，增强蛋白质稳定性并促进炎症小体组装［88］。在SUMO化和去SUMO化的动态转化层面，泛素缀合酶9介导NLRP3的K204位点SUMO化修饰可促进ASC募集和斑点形成，增强炎症小体活性及IL-1β分泌；去SUMO化酶SENP3可移除相关SUMO化修饰，抑制炎症小体组装并减弱炎症反应［89］。类似地，线粒体锚定蛋白连接酶介导NLRP3的K689位点SUMO化修饰可抑制NLRP3组装；而通过SENP6和SENP7介导的去SUMO化可促进炎症小体组装及IL-1β释放［5］。此外，含锌指和BTB结构域蛋白16也可与ASC、泛素缀合酶9、SUMO1相互作用并影响ASC在组装中的功能，提示ASC特定位点（K21/K109）可能为SUMO化关键区域［90］。因此，动态调控SUMO化和去SUMO化可影响炎症小体活性的强度和持续时间。

SENP家族成员通过对不同底物的去SUMO化修饰，在炎症小体组装及活化过程中发挥多维调控作用。在经典通路中，SENP3既可介导NLRP3去SUMO化修饰，还可去除GSDMD的K177位点SUMO化修饰，导致GSDMD蛋白不稳定并抑制焦亡进程，限制炎症损伤的扩散［91］。在非经典通路中，SENP1可在巨噬细胞中通过去SUMO化修饰直接促进caspase-11活化，进而加剧炎症反应［92］。在更复杂的调控网络层面，脑出血模型中SENP5通过去SUMO化修饰促进甲基转移酶样蛋白3降解，下调溶血磷脂酸受体1 mRNA的m6A甲基化水平，进而促进NLRP3炎症小体活化及神经炎症；而外泌体介导的miR-30b-5p递送则通过靶向沉默SENP5恢复甲基转移酶样蛋白3水平及其对溶血磷脂酸受体1 mRNA的m⁶A修饰，抑制炎症小体相关蛋白异常上调，从而减轻炎症反应并改善神经功能损伤［93］。综上，SENP家族通过对NLRP3、GSDMD、caspase-11和甲基转移酶样蛋白3等不同底物的去SUMO化修饰，在经典通路、非经典通路、焦亡执行和表观转录调控等多个层面实现对炎症小体活化的精准调控，凸显了SUMO化和去SUMO化动态平衡在维持免疫稳态中的核心地位。

结 语

炎症小体作为机体炎症应答的核心调控因子，其活性和功能的动态调节是维持免疫稳态及应对病理刺激的核心机制。炎症小体的翻译后修饰具有多维度特性：同一蛋白酶对NLRP3的调控效应因疾病而异；修饰位点及关键酶的种类决定炎症小体的功能表现和命运走向；同一蛋白酶既可直接调控炎症小体的活性，也可通过级联反应间接调控其活性。因此，解读相关研究时须综合考虑细胞类型、病理背景及实验条件等多种因素，避免得出片面结论。炎症小体的翻译后修饰异常与自身炎症性疾病、自身免疫病、代谢性疾病和神经系统疾病等密切相关，其异常修饰模式不仅推动疾病进展，也为诊断和治疗提供了新的生物标志物和干预靶点。多种靶向炎症小体翻译后修饰的小分子抑制剂（如GSK461364［75］和BRD3308［87］）已在动物模型中展现出良好疗效，表明通过精准调控炎症小体活性改善疾病预后具有可行性。

针对炎症小体翻译后修饰干预策略的临床转化仍面临一系列瓶颈。首先，靶点选择性。炎症小体蛋白质翻译后修饰涉及复杂的酶网络，参与多条信号通路并广泛作用于不同底物，传统干预策略难以实现对特定信号通路的精准调控。其次，脱靶效应和系统毒性。小分子抑制剂和PROTAC在体内均可能影响非预期底物或相关信号通路，从而引发免疫失衡或其他不良反应。第三，组织特异性递送。炎症小体在不同组织和细胞中的功能异质性显著，现有递送系统难以实现病理部位精准靶向递送，限制其治疗窗口。最后，长期干预的安全性问题亦不容忽视。炎症小体在宿主抗感染及免疫稳态维持中具有重要作用，持续抑制其活性可能削弱机体防御能力，增加感染或免疫相关并发症的风险。

综上，本文系统梳理了四种蛋白质翻译后修饰在炎症小体启动、组装、活化、降解各阶段的调控机制，并探讨了修饰间的相互作用网络和细胞类型特异性。目前虽已鉴定出多个炎症小体相关突变及蛋白质翻译后修饰位点，但其临床相关性及调控异质性仍需深入验证。未来研究可从以下方向突破：首先，联合单细胞蛋白质组学和邻近标记技术绘制不同组织驻留细胞在稳态和疾病状态下的蛋白质翻译后修饰-炎症小体动态图谱，揭示其调控网络的组织特异性。其次，借鉴PROTAC、光遗传学及微环境激活前药等策略，开发时空可控的修饰酶靶向干预工具，实现特定细胞或疾病阶段的精准调控。第三，建立“遗传变异-蛋白质翻译后修饰-炎症小体功能”关联分析框架，并利用诱导多能干细胞分化模型和碱基编辑技术解析疾病相关突变对蛋白质翻译后修饰网络的扰动规律，为靶向干预提供新靶点。第四，整合多组学与系统生物学方法，比较不同组织和疾病模型中调控网络的共性和特性，为炎症相关疾病的精准防治提供新策略。

title: What is groundwater?
creator: Mark O Cuthbert
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Groundwater may be the most important substance on Earth that most people have never heard of, yet it has quietly influenced the evolution of human culture since its earliest beginnings. title: 《中华人民共和国精神卫生法》实施10年后非自愿入院及其法律标准符合性的变化
creator: Sifu Luo, Ge Wang, Weilong Guo, Xiaoping Wang, 毅 游
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的《中华人民共和国精神卫生法》(以下简称“精神卫生法”)于2013年实施，将非自愿入院限定于特定情形，以保护精神障碍患者的权益。本研究旨在评估该法实施10年后，精神障碍患者非自愿入院率及其法律标准符合性的变化。方法采用重复横断面研究设计，分别于2012年与2023年，连续纳入中南大学湘雅二医院精神科病房1~2个月的新入院患者，收集其社会人口学资料及临床特征，采用修订版外显攻击行为量表(Modified Overt Aggression Scale，MOAS)、社会功能缺陷筛选量表(Social Disability Screening Schedule，SDSS)、自知力与治疗态度问卷(Insight and Treatment Attitudes Questionnaire，ITAQ)、简明精神病评定量表(Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale，BPRS)及半定式知情同意能力检查评估问卷(Semi-Structured Inventory for Competence Assessment，SSICA)对患者的攻击行为、社会功能、自知力、精神症状及知情同意能力进行量化评估。依据精神卫生法相关条款，结合入院诊断及量表评分判定非自愿入院的法律标准符合情况。结果共纳入618例患者。2012年与2023年总体非自愿入院率分别为34.7%和30.1%(P=0.220)，封闭病房非自愿入院率分别为53.1%和47.4%(P=0.264)，调整人口学及临床特征后，年份与封闭病房非自愿入院仍无显著关联(P=0.375)。2012年与2023年封闭病房非自愿入院者中不符合法律标准的比例分别为32.9%和44.4%(P=0.104)，但调整人口学特征后，2023年不符合法律标准的可能性高于2012年(P=0.032)。在封闭病房非自愿入院患者中，符合标准者的BPRS敌对猜疑因子评分高于不符合标准者(P<0.001)，调整年份后仍存在关联(P=0.005)。2组间社会功能、自知力及知情同意能力的差异均无统计学意义(均P˃0.05)。结论与精神卫生法实施前(2012年)相比，实施后10年(2023年)的非自愿入院率未见明显变化，不符合法律标准的非自愿入院患者仍占一定比例，提示现行法律标准与临床实践之间仍存在差距，需进一步加强衔接。Keywords: 精神卫生法, 精神障碍, 非自愿入院, 重复横断面研究, 法律标准 非自愿入院是缺乏自知力的精神障碍患者临床管理的重要措施，但因其涉及对个人自由的限制，且治疗满意度较低，长期以来存在争议[1]。世界上许多国家均通过立法对非自愿入院加以规范[2]，而非自愿入院率在不同国家和地区的差异显著，且难以完全由立法框架或严重精神障碍发病率不同加以解释[3]。 中国在2013年正式实施《中华人民共和国精神卫生法》(以下简称“精神卫生法”)，确立了以自愿住院为原则、保护精神障碍患者合法权利的立法精神。该法第三十条规定，在诊断结论、病情评估表明就诊者为严重精神障碍患者，且已经发生伤害自身的行为或有伤害自身的危险，或已经发生危害他人安全的行为或有危害他人安全的危险时，应当对其实施住院治疗。即仅在严重精神障碍患者满足上述危险性标准时，方可对其实施非自愿入院。在立法前，中国精神障碍患者以非自愿入院为主，2002年一项覆盖17个城市、包含2 333名患者的多中心研究[4]显示，自愿入院率不足20%。在2013年精神卫生法实施后，部分研究提示非自愿入院率在短期内有所下降。例如，杭州一项研究[5]显示，立法后第4个月，封闭病房的非自愿入院率由立法前的91.47%下降至77.86%。然而，精神卫生法实施后不同地区非自愿入院率的长期变化并不一致。上海的一项纵向研究[6]显示，立法后第1个月，非自愿入院率从立法前的79.8%降至69.7%，此后逐渐回升，调查结束时(立法后4年)达到87.8%的最高点。2017年一项覆盖29个省会城市(含直辖市)、32家精神专科医院的全国性横断面调查[7]则进一步显示，仅45.3%的非自愿入院患者符合精神卫生法所规定的危险性标准，各医院间符合率的波动范围为7.9%~88.5%。 自精神卫生法实施至今，围绕非自愿入院已有大量讨论，主要集中于法律标准与实施过程[8]。就标准本身而言，危险性标准在实践中界定较为模糊，风险评估多依赖家属陈述及医生经验判断[9]。一项基于中国裁判文书网的司法实践分析[10]进一步揭示，非自愿入院相关诉讼中精神障碍患者在起诉、举证及胜诉等环节均面临困难。而以危险性为核心标准，可能导致部分无明显危险性但确有治疗需要的患者无法及时获得干预[11]。目前实证研究多集中于对非自愿入院率的中短期观察，对精神卫生法实施后较长时间跨度内非自愿入院率及其法律标准符合情况的研究证据仍较为缺乏。 综上，本研究基于同一医疗机构立法前(2012年)及实施后10年(2023年)的2次横断面调查数据，采用重复横断面设计，比较精神卫生法实施前及实施后10年间精神障碍患者非自愿入院率及其与法律标准符合性的变化，以期为理解非自愿入院实践及法律标准执行情况提供参考。 对象与方法 伦理声明 本研究已获得中南大学湘雅二医院国家临床医学研究中心伦理委员会的批准{审批号：(2021)国伦审〔科〕第(035)号}。所有患者或其家属均知晓研究内容和目的，并签署书面知情同意书。对于因精神症状、认知状态或知情同意能力受损而不能充分理解研究内容或不能独立签署知情同意书的患者，由其家属代为签署书面知情同意书。 对象 本研究在中南大学湘雅二医院精神科开展。该科室是此三甲综合医院的重点临床专科之一，有6个病区，共设242张床位。以该院精神科2012年7月26日至9月10日及2023年3月1日至4月30日2个时段的新入院患者为研究对象，连续纳入，可基本反映相应时期该院新入院患者的特征。使用G*Power 3.1进行χ 2检验事先样本量估算，参考既往研究[5-6]的结果，并结合本研究的探索性质，设为保守的中小效应量w=0.2。在显著性水平α=0.05，检验效能1-β=0.8的条件下，计算得出每组至少需99例。实际纳入样本量均满足估算要求：2012年共纳入259例，其中开放病房99例，封闭男病房79例、封闭女病房81例(封闭病房合计160例)；2023年共纳入359例，其中开放病房131例、封闭男病房111例、封闭女病房117例(封闭病房合计228例)。 方法 研究工具 1)基本资料调查：包括患者性别、年龄、婚姻状况、文化程度、居住地、本次住院前是否经过门诊治疗、门诊治疗依从性、入院诊断。 2)修订版外显攻击行为量表(Modified Overt Aggression Scale，MOAS)[12]：将攻击行为分为言语攻击、对财产的攻击、自身攻击和体力攻击他人4个维度，由调查者根据家属描述的患者近1个月最严重的攻击行为进行评分(0~4分)，得分越高表示攻击行为越严重。 3)社会功能缺陷筛选量表(Social Disability Screening Schedule，SDSS)[13]：共10个条目，由调查者根据家属描述的患者本次发病以来的行为表现进行评定，总分越高提示社会功能缺陷越严重。总分≥2视为存在社会功能缺陷。 4)自知力与治疗态度问卷(Insight and Treatment Attitudes Questionnaire，ITAQ)[14]：共11个条目，每个条目0~2分。由调查者根据精神检查情况评定患者的自知力水平，总分越高表明患者自知力越充分。 5)简明精神病评定量表(Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale，BPRS)[15]：适用于不同诊断的精神障碍患者的症状严重程度评估。采用18项版本，每项按1~7分评分，总分及各因子分越高提示症状越严重。 6)半定式知情同意能力检查评估问卷(Semi-Structured Inventory for Competence Assessment，SSICA)[16]：共20个条目，包括对病情、治疗及住院的理解与认识等内容，总分0~31，得分越高表示知情同意能力越强。总分≤15视为无知情同意能力。 研究流程 在2012年和2023年，分别由2名经过相同培训的精神科医师在患者入院48 h内完成全部评估。在患者或其家属了解研究内容和目的并签署知情同意书后，研究者对患者及其家属进行访谈，收集患者的基本资料和入院方式，使用上述量表对患者的攻击行为、社会功能、自知力、精神症状及知情同意能力进行量化评估，并查阅患者的入院病历获取临床相关资料。 概念定义及判定标准 根据精神卫生法第三十条及第八十三条，本研究将非自愿入院法律标准分为严重精神障碍标准与危险性标准两部分，并结合入院诊断及量表评分进行判定。严重精神障碍定义为：符合国际疾病分类(International Classification of Diseases，ICD)-10任一精神或行为障碍诊断，且入院时SDSS总分≥2、ITAQ总分≤17。危险性标准依据MOAS评估结果判定：条目1(言语攻击)≥3分，或条目2(对财产攻击)≥1分，或条目3(自身攻击)≥1分，或条目4(体力攻击)≥1分，判定为存在伤害自身或他人的行为或危险。同时符合上述2项标准者，本研究判定为符合非自愿入院的法律标准。 根据患者对住院的态度，将入院方式划分为自愿与非自愿。当研究者询问患者“本次住院是您自愿的吗？”时，表示自愿或不反对住院者归为自愿入院；表示被强行送入院或非知情入院，或因精神病性症状无法理解问题、不能表达真实意愿者，归为非自愿入院。 统计学处理 采用SPSS 28.0软件进行统计分析。计数资料以频数(构成比或率)表示，组间比较采用χ 2检验。非正态分布的计量资料以中位数(第1四分位数，第3四分位数)表示，组间比较采用Mann-Whitney U检验，并报告Z值。为控制样本构成差异对主要结果的影响，采用二元Logistic回归进行调整分析，结果以OR值及95% CI表示。P<0.05为差异有统计学意义。 结 果 社会人口学和临床特征比较 2012年与2023年共纳入618例患者。相比2012年，2023年的住院患者的年龄、婚姻状况、文化程度及居住地构成的差异均有统计学意义(均P<0.05)，性别分布无统计学差异(P˃0.05，表1)。2023年的未成年患者(<18岁)比例更高，未婚/离异/丧偶者比例上升，本科及以上学历者比例增加，居住地为城市者比例提高(均P<0.05)。 表1研究对象的社会人口学和临床特征Table 1 title: 环境相对湿度、衰弱与中国中老年人新发卒中风险：一项前瞻性队列研究
creator: 杨波 周, 明铭 张, 浩 丁, 捷 郑, 玉兴 杨, 岩 崔
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的卒中是中国致死致残的主要病因之一，疾病负担沉重。人口老龄化加剧了中老年群体卒中的防控压力。环境相对湿度(relative humidity，RH)虽被视为影响健康的关键因素，但现有研究对其与卒中关联的结论不一，尤其缺乏中国人群的前瞻性证据。本研究旨在探讨环境RH与中国中老年人新发卒中风险的关联，并评估衰弱在其中的中介作用及性别差异。方法基于中国健康与养老追踪调查(China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study，CHARLS)2011、2013、2015和2018年调查的数据构建动态入组队列，最终纳入19 582例研究对象，时间为自其首次满足入组条件的访谈日期起至首次报告新发卒中、失访或2020年末次随访。采用ERA5再分析资料获取个体居住地逐小时的RH，计算入组前1年平均RH，并按三分位数分为低、中等、高湿度组(以低湿度组为参照)。以随访期间研究对象首次自我报告并经临床医生诊断的卒中作为新发卒中的判定依据。采用Cox比例风险模型估计HR及95% CI，逐步调整社会人口学特征、健康行为及入组前1年平均气温等混杂因素，并进行性别分层分析；采用反事实框架中介分析评估衰弱指数(frailty index，FI)的中介效应，采用非参数自助法(bootstrap)并重复抽样5 000次计算FI的中介效应比例及其不确定性。结果中位随访时间为7年，随访期间新发卒中1 235例(6.31%)。Cox模型分析结果显示，与低湿度组相比，中等湿度组和高湿度组的新发卒中风险均升高；在全调整模型中，中等湿度组(HR=1.119，95% CI 1.033~1.213)和高湿度组(HR=1.279，95% CI 1.227~1.331)的新发卒中风险均升高(均P<0.01)，且随模型调整程度增加，效应量逐步减弱。性别分层分析显示，该关联在男性中更为明显：全调整模型中男性的中等湿度组HR=1.145(95% CI 1.031~1.272)、高湿度组HR=1.352(95% CI 1.268~1.442)；女性的高湿度组风险亦升高(HR=1.186，95% CI 1.092~1.288)，但女性的中等湿度组关联减弱(HR=1.082，95% CI 0.954~1.227)。中介分析结果显示，环境RH对新发卒中风险的总效应具有统计学意义(P<0.01)，湿度与衰弱水平相关(β=0.22，P<0.01)，衰弱在湿度与新发卒中风险关联中的中介效应比例为22.0%。结论环境RH升高与中国中老年人新发卒中风险增加相关，且该关联可部分通过衰弱通路传递；该关联存在性别差异，在男性中更为显著。这提示在卒中一级预防与老年健康管理中，应关注高湿环境暴露，并加强对衰弱人群及男性等潜在高风险亚组的风险识别与健康指导。

卒中是中国居民致死致残的重要原因之一，其具有高发病率、高复发率和高致残率等特点，对个人生活质量与社会医疗负担造成长期影响。随着中国人口老龄化进程加快，中老年人群卒中防控需求日益迫切[1-2]。既往研究[3]已证实多种传统危险因素(如高血压、糖尿病、吸烟、肥胖及体力活动不足)与卒中发生密切相关，但仅依赖个体层面的行为与代谢因素仍难以充分解释卒中发病风险的人群差异及其在不同季节与地区的波动。因此，识别可干预的环境暴露及其作用途径，对于完善卒中一级预防策略具有重要公共卫生意义[4]。

环境相对湿度(relative humidity，RH)作为气候系统中反映大气水分条件的重要指标，近年来在健康效应研究中受到关注。一方面，湿度可通过影响人体热交换与体温调节，改变心血管系统负荷；另一方面，湿度水平与室内潮湿、霉菌滋生及呼吸道炎症等问题相关，可能进一步影响血管内皮功能、炎症反应及血液流变学状态，从而增加脑血管事件风险[5]。然而，现有关于湿度与卒中关系的证据仍不一致。研究[6]一般基于短期时间序列或病例交叉设计，关注日尺度气象波动与住院/死亡结局，其结果在不同地区与研究框架下呈现较大异质性；同时，较少有研究从个体层面刻画较长时间窗口的湿度暴露，限制了对慢性环境暴露与卒中发生之间关联的理解，尤其缺乏在中国人群中的前瞻性证据[7]。

衰弱是反映中老年人群生理储备下降与多系统功能受损的综合征，已被证明与多种不良健康结局密切相关，并可能是环境暴露与心脑血管事件之间关联的关键易感因素[8]。环境湿度可能通过热应激、慢性炎症、睡眠与呼吸系统负担等途径加速功能衰退和缺陷累积，使衰弱程度加重；而衰弱状态下的自主神经调节能力、血压稳定性及应激耐受能力下降，又可能增加卒中发生的风险[9]。尽管如此，关于RH与卒中的关联是否可被衰弱所中介，以及衰弱在其中的贡献程度的量化证据仍相对匮乏，特别是在基于全国代表性队列的前瞻性研究中尚缺乏系统评估[10]。

基于此，本研究依托中国健康与养老追踪调查(China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study，CHARLS)2011、2013、2015和2018年调查波次的数据构建动态入组的前瞻性队列，评估入组前1年环境RH水平与新发卒中风险的关联，并在控制社会人口学特征、健康行为及关键气象共暴露等混杂因素的基础上，进一步探讨衰弱指数(frailty index，FI)在上述关联中的中介作用。同时，考虑到卒中发生及对环境应激的反应可能存在性别差异(如生理调节能力、基础危险因素谱及行为暴露模式不同)，本研究将开展性别分层分析以评估RH与卒中关联的效应异质性，从而识别潜在的高风险亚组[11]。本研究旨在为中国中老年人群卒中风险评估提供环境维度的证据支持，并为在高湿环境下开展针对性的健康风险提示，实施性别差异化的风险沟通与衰弱筛查，以及强化易感人群保护提供科学依据。

对象与方法

对象

本研究数据来源于CHARLS。CHARLS由北京大学国家发展研究院组织实施，采用多阶段分层整群抽样方法，在全国范围内对45岁及以上中老年人及其配偶开展长期随访调查，收集人口学特征、社会经济状况、健康行为、慢性病与功能状态等信息，具有良好的全国代表性[12]。本研究基于CHARLS 2011、2013、2015和2018年调查波次构建动态入组的前瞻性队列，研究对象可在上述任一波次作为入组基线进入随访，并随访至2020年以评估新发卒中结局。

纳入标准：1)基线时完成卒中相关问卷信息并可判定卒中基线状态；2)至少参加一次随访调查且具备随访信息以判断卒中结局；3)基线核心协变量信息完整(包括人口学与社会经济特征、主要健康行为指标及其他预先设定的混杂因素)。排除标准：1)基线自报既往经医生诊断的卒中者(为确保结局为新发卒中)；2)随访信息缺失、无法确定结局发生时间或缺失随访时长者；3)关键暴露变量(环境RH)无法匹配或缺失者；4)主要协变量缺失且无法进行完整案例分析者。根据上述标准构建研究队列后，研究对象自其首次满足入组条件的调查波次访谈日期起进入随访。随访终点设定为首次报告新发卒中、失访或随访截止(以最后一次可获得的随访波次为准)，以最先发生者作为结局终点。队列人年从基线访谈日期累计至终点日期。本研究动态入组队列的样本来源及纳入、排除流程见图1。本研究使用CHARLS的公开、去标识化数据。CHARLS各轮调查均经北京大学生物医学伦理委员会批准，家户问卷调查实地工作方案的伦理批准号为IRB00001052-11015。所有受访者均在调查前签署书面知情同意书。本研究未实施额外人体干预、样本采集或接触可识别个人信息。

title: Arginine methylation modification in the malignant progression of benign and malignant liver diseases
creator: Jie-Zuo Huang, Bei-Ning Qiao, Dang-Chi Li, Qiu-Rong Wei, Zi-Jian Zhang
description: The role of protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs) in benign and malignant liver diseases has garnered considerable attention. PRMTs play a key function in regulating protein methylation modification in diseases such as alcoholic fatty liver disease, metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease, viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.

title: Management of Oehlers type IIIb dens invaginatus in a maxillary lateral incisor: A case report
creator: Saeed Asgary
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Oehlers’ classification, DI is categorized into three types, with Type IIIb representing the most severe form, in which the invagination extends through the root and exits at the apical foramen, often without direct communication with the main pulp canal.1 Such cases pose considerable endodontic challenges due to their intricate internal anatomy and the difficulty of achieving complete debridement and hermetic sealing.

Most patients begin to experience bleeding 5 to 7 days after the onset of the illness, usually while hospitalized.

title: 健脾解毒优化方对结直肠癌患者化疗毒副作用及肠道菌群的影响：一项前瞻性对照研究
creator: 重杰 王, 金辉 刘, 林子 陈, 海霞 晏, 端阳 郭, 四方 张
description: 目的结直肠癌(colorectal carcinoma，CRC)患者在接受化疗过程中常出现胃肠道反应、体重下降和骨髓抑制等不良反应，影响治疗的连续性和患者的功能状态。肠道菌群失衡与CRC进展、化疗相关不良反应及患者对化疗的反应有关。本研究旨在观察健脾解毒优化方(Jianpi Jiedu optimized formula，JPJDYHF)辅助化疗治疗Ⅲ~Ⅳ期CRC患者的临床效果、安全性及其对肠道菌群结构的影响。方法前瞻性纳入121例原发性Ⅲ~Ⅳ期CRC患者，按患者意愿分为联合组(JPJDYHF联合化疗)与对照组(单纯化疗)。对照组接受中国临床肿瘤学会(Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology，CSCO)指南推荐的一线化疗方案，联合组在此基础上分阶段口服JPJDYHF1号方和2号方。剔除脱落病例后，对完成6个化疗周期的113例患者，以年龄、性别、TNM分期、化疗方案等9项基线变量构建倾向评分匹配(propensity score matching，PSM)模型，采用1:1最邻近匹配(卡钳值0.25)筛选出60例患者(每组30例)进行统计分析。记录首周期至第2周期的化疗通过情况；于各化疗周期结束时评估客观缓解率(objective response rate，ORR)、疾病控制率(disease control rate，DCR)、Karnofsky功能状态(Karnofsky Performance Status，KPS)评分、中医证候积分及化疗相关不良反应(胃肠道反应、体重减轻、骨髓抑制)；检测化疗前后血清癌胚抗原(carcinoembryonic antigen，CEA)与糖类抗原19-9(carbohydrate antigen 19-9，CA19-9)水平及肝肾功能。于6个化疗周期结束后，采集粪便样本，提取总DNA，针对16S核糖体RNA(16S ribosomal RNA，16S rRNA)基因V3~V4区进行高通量测序，评估Alpha与Beta多样性，采用线性判别分析效应量(linear discriminant analysis effect size，LEfSe)筛选差异菌群，并采用基于未观测状态重建的群落系统发育调查2(Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States 2，PICRUSt2)和同源蛋白簇(Clusters of Orthologous Groups，COG)数据库进行功能预测。结果经PSM后，2组基线特征均衡。临床疗效方面，联合组化疗通过情况优于对照组，ORR(46.67% vs 16.67%)和DCR(90.00% vs 73.33%)均更高(均P<0.05)。联合组的中医证候疗效总有效率达73.3%，高于对照组的30.0%(P<0.05)。第3周期和第6周期时，联合组的KPS评分均高于对照组(均P<0.05)。安全性与不良反应方面，第6周期结束时联合组的胃肠道反应严重程度、体重下降程度及骨髓抑制发生情况均较对照组改善(均P<0.05)，且2组肝肾功能指标变化的差异均无统计学意义(均P˃0.05)。血清学指标方面，第5、6周期结束时联合组的CEA水平低于对照组，且下降率更高(均P<0.05)，但CA19-9水平和下降率的差异均无统计学意义(均P˃0.05)。肠道菌群分析显示，2组Alpha多样性无差异(P˃0.05)，而Beta多样性存在显著分离(P<0.05)。LEfSe分析表明，联合组拟杆菌门(Bacteroidota)、梭杆菌门(Fusobacteriota)及弯曲杆菌门(Campylobacterota)的相对丰度下降；属水平上，拟杆菌属(Bacteroides)、副拟杆菌属(Parabacteroides)和促癌相关梭杆菌属(Fusobacterium)的相对丰度下降，而产短链脂肪酸的布劳特氏菌属(Blautia)、瘤胃球菌科-UCG-014(Ruminococcaceae-UCG-014)的相对丰度升高(均P<0.

title: Perspective: Genicular artery embolization for knee osteoarthritis - When the hype doesn’t match the evidence
creator: Tijmen A van Zadelhoff, Rianne A van der Heijden, Sita MA Bierma-Zeinstra, P Koen Bos, Edwin HG Oei
description: This paper summarizes the current evidence on genicular artery embolization (GAE) for the treatment of knee osteoarthritis (OA). The goal of this minimally invasive treatment is to reduce synovitis by embolizing peri‑genicular neovascularization and subsequently alleviate pain. Multiple uncontrolled case series have generally demonstrated a promising efficacy of GAE with substantial, lasting pain reduction and improved function.

title: Association of Gallstone and Polymorphisms of ABCB11 Gene among the Adult Patients in Iran: A Case Control Study
creator: Sedigheh Yektamoghaddam, Mohammad Mahdi Forghanifard, Vajiheh Zrrinpour, Mojtaba Fathi
description: BackgroundBackground: Gallstone disease (GSD) is a prevalent gastrointestinal condition influenced by genetic, environmental, and dietary factors. The ATP-binding cassette subfamily B member 11 (ABCB11) gene, encoding the bile salt export pump (BSEP), plays a critical role in bile acid transport. title: Indocyanine green angiography in uveitis
creator: Luca De Simone, Anna Byszewska, Abdulrahman F. Albloushi, Riccardo Genovese, Ioannis Papasavvas, Carl P. Jr Herbort
description: Indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) represents an indispensable imaging modality for the precise evaluation and management of posterior uveitis by allowing to explore the choroidal compartment. ICGA leverages near-infrared fluorescence and extensive protein binding to provide an unhindered, dynamic assessment of the choriocapillaris and choroidal stroma. This review explores the principles, standard protocols, and clinical applications of ICGA in posterior uveitis.

creator: Subodh Dave, Jon van Niekerk, Philip Pirie, Jo O’Reilly

These factors can leave clinicians feeling disempowered and demoralised.

title: Integrating three-dimensional (3D)-printed teaching models to improve the learning effectiveness of oral pathology: A teaching practice research project
creator: Feng-Chou Cheng, Chun-Pin Chiang, Yi-Ping Wang, Wei-Cheng Lin, Jer-An Guo, Julia Yu-Fong Chang

This teaching practice research project aimed to evaluate whether integrating three-dimensional (3D)-printed teaching models into oral pathology instruction could enhance students’ learning effectiveness, particularly in understanding lesion texture and clinical palpation.

creator: Felistas Mazhude, Robert S. Kramer, Anne Hicks, Qingchu Jin, Melanie Tory, Jaime B. Rabb, Mahsan Nourani, Douglas B. Sawyer, Raimond L. Winslow
description: Problem:Postoperative complications after cardiac surgery significantly impact both the short-term and long-term survival of patients. Cardiovascular diseases are a major health concern, accounting for 12% of health expenditures in the United States. A substantial number of patients with cardiovascular disease undergo invasive procedures, including cardiac surgery, and the incidence of postoperative complications is notable.

title: The effectiveness of cyproheptadine as a treatment option for cats with eosinophilic airway inflammation
creator: Jillian Seeman, Rachael Kreisler, Jeffrey Norris
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PICO questionIn cats with eosinophilic airway inflammation does cyproheptadine compared with no treatment result in a reduction in severity of clinical signs?Clinical bottom lineCategory of researchTreatment.Number and type of study designs reviewedFour studies were evaluated: the first was a randomised, blinded, placebo-controlled, crossover study, the second was a randomised crossover study, the third was a non-randomised, controlled study, and the fourth a non-randomised, controlled study.Strength of evidenceModerate.Outcomes reportedIn two of the four studies it was found that cyproheptadine was not useful in

title: Expanded classification for immediate molar implant placement: Integrating root socket strategies beyond septal bone typing
creator: Chiun-Lin Steven Liu, Shih-Cheng Wen, Ching-Jung Chang Chien, Je-Kang Du
description: Background/purposeThis conceptual development study with exploratory clinical analysis aimed to create and preliminarily evaluate a six-category classification system for immediate implant placement (IIP) in molar extraction sites. IIP in molar regions remains challenging due to complex socket morphology and variable septal bone availability. Existing septal-based classifications (e.g., Smith-Tarnow) may exclude viable cases with favorable root socket anatomy.

title: Refugee healthcare resilience and burdens: a 10-year mixed-methods analysis of system shocks in Canada
creator: Eric Norrie, Linda Holdbrook, Rabina Grewal, Rachel Talavlikar, Mohammad Yasir Essar, Tyler Williamson, Annalee Coakley, Kerry McBrien, Gabriel E Fabreau
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryBackgroundSystem shocks, including policy changes, refugee surges, and pandemics, strain healthcare systems. These shocks compound refugee health vulnerabilities, limiting care but may also trigger adaptive responses that build resilience. Understanding local responses is essential for resilient care models.MethodsThis sequential explanatory mixed-methods retrospective study (2011–2020) examined how a refugee health centre in Alberta, Canada, responded to four shocks: Interim Federal Health Program (IFHP) Cuts (2012), Syrian Surge (2015), Yazidi Resettlement (2017), and COVID-19 (2020).

title: Clostridioides difficile infection risk and contemporary antibiotic use: Evidence from a large real-world dataset highlighting the need for a comprehensive antibiotic stewardship in dentistry
creator: Stella O. Oyewole, Adepitan A. Owosho
description: Background/purposeIn dental care, antibiotics are frequently used for infection control. While certain antibiotics are historically linked to the increased risk of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). Existing risk classifications may not reflect current prescribing practices or patient outcomes. This study seeks to investigate antibiotic exposure patterns in patients prior to CDI symptom emergence and diagnosis to better understand true risk associations.

title: Medial Patellofemoral Complex Reconstruction Using the Rectus Femoris Tendon
creator: Anshu Shekhar, Sachin Tapasvi, Camilo Helito
description: The medial proximal static stabilizers of the patella are the medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and the medial quadriceps tendon femoral ligament. These are collectively referred to as the “medial patellofemoral complex” (MPFC). MPFL reconstruction is the workhorse of patellar stabilization surgery for recurrent lateral instability. We describe a technique for reconstructing the MPFC using the ipsilateral rectus tendon.

title: Global horizontal irradiance data for 12 stations in Mauritius, Rodrigues and Agaléga
creator: Yogesh Beeharry, Ravish Gokool, Yatindra Kumar Ramgolam, Aatish Chiniah
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This data article presents the Global Horizontal Irradiance data acquired at a temporal resolution of one-hour intervals from 12 sites around the island of Mauritius, Rodrigues and Agaléga. These data were collected over different durations for different sites.

title: Heterogeneity sonata: Orchestrating distal metastasis under stress
creator: Baiyang Liu, Yongbin Chen
description: e supporting biosynthesis and proliferation, and its rapid consumption by malignant cells renders low-glucose conditions a pervasive metabolic stress in the tumor microenvironment.2 This stress not only limits cellular energy supply but also engages programs such as autophagy, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and reorganization of vesicular trafficking.

title: Outcomes and risk factors of pulpotomy in mature permanent teeth with complicated crown fractures: A 12–60-month prospective clinical study
creator: Qiang Li, Yin-Fei Pu, Jia-Jia Zheng, Wei Sun, Xiao Shao
description: Background/purposeTraumatic dental injuries (TDIs), especially complicated crown fractures (CCFs), challenge pulp preservation in mature teeth. This study evaluated outcomes and risk factors in mature permanent teeth treated with pulpotomy using iRoot BP Plus.Materials and methodsThis prospective single-arm clinical trial included 47 mature permanent anterior teeth with CCFs and pulp exposures within 24 h post-trauma.

title: Learning curve of EUS-guided gastroenterostomy for the management of malignant gastric outlet obstruction: Data from a bicentric retrospective study
creator: Angelica Toppeta, Marie Philippart, Jean-Philippe Ratone, Antoine Assaf, Mariola Marx, Élodie Romailler, Meddy Dalex, Marc Giovannini, Solène Hoibian, Yanis Dahel, Francesco Martini, Sébastien Godat, Fabrice Caillol
description: Background and Objectives:EUS-guided gastroenterostomy (EUS-GE) is a promising alternative for managing malignant gastric outlet obstruction (GOO). This study aimed to analyze the learning curve (LC) for EUS-GE.Methods:This retrospective European bicentric study included 96 patients with malignant GOO who underwent EUS-GE (April 2021 to August 2024) using the wireless EUS-guided gastroenterostomy simplified technique (WEST) or modified WEST.

title: LSD1 inhibition sensitizes anti-PD1 blockade immunotherapy by inhibiting the long-range attack of tumor-derived extracellular vesicles
creator: Yu Zhao, Danyang Zhang, Lin Meng, Siming Shan, Chao Zhang, Zhenzhong Deng, Chao Han, Lingyi Kong
description: Programmed cell death protein-1/programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD1/PD-L1) blockade has shown promise in cancer therapy but remains limited by low response rates. Recent efforts have explored strategies to enhance immunotherapy efficacy. Histone lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) inhibition can enhance tumor immune responses by downregulating PD-L1 expression.

title: Late implant loss and complications of one-step implant therapy in severely atrophic posterior maxilla
creator: Shing-Zeng Dung, Jui Wang, Yung-Ting Hsu, Tzu-Hsuan Weng, Shale M. Ninneman, Yu-Kang Tu
description: Background/purposeSuccessful long-term outcomes of one-step implant placement in the atrophic maxilla have rarely been reported. This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the long-term efficacy of the one-step lateral sinus floor elevation and simultaneous implant placement (LSFESI) in severely atrophic posterior maxilla, and to identify the risk factors for marginal bone loss (MBL) and late implant failure (LIF).

title: Rapidly progressive subdural empyema secondary to acute pansinusitis complicated by superior sagittal sinus thrombosis in a young adult: a multidisciplinary case report
creator: Roxana Nartea, Monica Hodor, Simona Vetu, Ilinca Pirciog
description: Subdural empyema is a rare but life-threatening intracranial infection, most commonly arising as a complication of paranasal sinusitis. Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary treatment are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. A 23-year-old previously healthy male developed a rapidly progressive subdural empyema associated with superior sagittal sinus thrombosis and severe sepsis. Clinical deterioration occurred within 24 hours of symptom onset.

title: Association between periodontitis and anemia: Results from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
creator: Cheng Lin, Xing Xing, Ye Han, Jianxia Hou, He Zhu
description: Background/purposeRecently, the association between periodontitis and anemia has raised the attention, however there is still a lack of convincing evidence on the association between periodontitis and anemia. This study aimed to examine the association between periodontitis and anemia by analyzing a large population-based nationally representative sample in American.

title: Eosinophilic pleural effusion in an individual in a high tuberculosis-burden country
creator: Amitesh Krishna Srinivasan, Akshay Kawedia, Nipun Malhotra, Saurabh Mittal, Anant Mohan, Karan Madan, Vijay Hadda, Pawan Tiwari, Tejas Suri, Irfan Shekh
description: Shareable abstractAn interactive case report discussing a case of eosinophilic pleural effusion https://bit.ly/4eTX8QP A 29-year-old previously healthy Indian man, without any comorbid illnesses, presented with a 2-month history of a left-sided chest pain that worsened with deep inhalation. He also had dry cough and a low grade intermittent fever. He denied having breathlessness, haemoptysis, joint pains or skin rashes.

title: From human dental pulp stem cells to functional cholinergic neurons: An optimized neurogenic differentiation protocol for new approach methodologies
creator: Pritsana Sawutdeechaikul, Thanaporn Pimpakan, Toan Van Phan, Vinicius Rosa, Joao Nuno Ferreira
description: Background/purposeDrug discovery is now supported by new approach methodologies (NAMs), creating a growing need for in vitro non-animal models that mimic human physiology and, most importantly, function. Secretory function in exocrine organs like salivary glands relies mostly on cholinergic innervation.

title: Preoperative predictors of adverse pathological outcomes following radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer in a tertiary referral center
creator: Matei Maximilian Buzoianu, Iulia Andras, Lorin Giurgiu, Paul Medan, Stefana Medan, Andrei Popa, Emanuel Cata, Emanuela Ionutas, Marius Apetrei, Ioan Coman, Nicolae Crisan
description: Accurate preoperative identification of non-organ-confined disease in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer could guide patient selection for bladder-sparing strategies. We evaluated the association between available preoperative clinical variables linked to worse oncologic outcomes and pathologic upstaging (≥T3) at radical cystectomy in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

title: Microwave versus conventional sintering on mechanical properties of 3Y-TZP - A systematic review
creator: Padmapriya Puppala, Gaurang Mistry, Vidhi Desai, Rajeev Singh, Mayuri Bachhav, Sanpreet Singh Sachdev
description: This systematic review evaluates the mechanical properties of yttria-stabilized zirconia (3Y-TZP) processed by microwave sintering compared to conventional sintering methods. Zirconia, known for its excellent strength and esthetics, has seen advancements in sintering techniques to enhance its properties. Conventional sintering, while effective, is time-consuming and less energy-efficient.

title: Performance of large language models on image-based oral pathology questions from the Japanese National Dental Examination
creator: Hikaru Watanabe, Osamu Uehara, Tetsuro Morikawa, Takayuki Kojima, Takayuki Suga, Akira Toyofuku, Satoshi Takada, Yoshihiro Abiko
description: Background: /purposeLarge language models (LLMs), such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT) and Gemini, have demonstrated promising capabilities for medical question-answering tasks. However, the diagnostic performance of LLMs in image-based oral pathologies remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to evaluate these capabilities using histopathological images obtained from the Japanese National Dental Examination.

title: Molecules of lung cancer – fusion alterations in nonsmall cell lung cancer: biology and diagnostic considerations
creator: Marie Talty, David O'Reilly, Jasmine Dunne, Jarushka Naidoo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fusion alterations have transformed outcomes for a subset of patients with nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as part of the evolution of precision oncology. While the role of molecular pathology in the diagnosis and treatment of NSCLC has rapidly evolved, it remains the responsibility of the pulmonologist to coordinate the diagnostic evaluation of patients with lung cancer, including clinical assessment, obtaining a histological diagnosis and coordination of staging procedures.

title: Shining a spotlight on females in ADHD science
creator: Stephen P. Becker
description: As JCPP Advances marks its fifth anniversary, this editorial highlights the need for continued and expanded research on females with attention‐deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Despite growing recognition of sex differences in ADHD presentation, diagnosis, and outcomes, females remain underrepresented in both research and clinical contexts.

title: Alteration in adenosine monophosphate deaminase activity and ferric reducing capacity in diabetic renal failure patients
creator: Lubna Sameer Hammad, Jwan abdulmohsin Zainulabdeen
description: Background: Renal failure is the final stage of chronic kidney disease (a common complication of diabetic mellitus) usually occurs due to delayed treatment or poor disease control with Glomerular filtration Rate falling below 15 mL/min leading to severe deterioration of renal function. Meanwhile Adenosine Monophosphate Deaminase (AMPD) participate in purine metabolism; affecting energy balance.

title: Human oral microbiota dysbiosis may be a novel non-invasive indicator of erectile dysfunction
creator: Yu Qiao, Fei Mao, Bing-Ru Jiang, Shu-Yan Lv, Heng-Bing Wang, Guang-Bo Fu
description: Background/purposeDysbiosis of the oral microbiota has been associated with various human diseases, however, the relationship between the oral microbiota and erectile dysfunction (ED) remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the connection between the oral microbiota and ED, ultimately identifying a novel non-invasive indicator for ED.

title: Synergising latent profile analysis and network analysis to elucidate the relationships among emotion dysregulation, post-traumatic stress disorder, dissociation, psychosis, and affective symptoms in individuals with trauma and severe mental illness
creator: Jianlin Liu, Celeste Minn Tan, Adela-Maria Isvoranu, Sacha Epskamp, Yoke Boon Tan, Rachel Hsiao Shen Tan, Sherilyn Shi Hui Chang, Vanessa Ai Ling Seet, Phern Chern Tor, Yu Wei Lee, Charmaine Tang, Nisha Chandwani, Swapna Verma, Mythily Subramaniam
description: BackgroundTrauma exposure and emotion dysregulation are transdiagnostic risk factors for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and severe mental disorders (e.g., depression, and schizophrenia spectrum disorders). The present study elucidated the latent profiles and interrelationships between emotion dysregulation and psychopathology (PTSD, dissociation, psychosis, and affective symptoms) in a trauma-exposed severe mental illness population.

title: A Scoping Review of Large Language Models in Personal Sleep Wellness
creator: Hamid Mansoor
description: As sleep health becomes increasingly central to personal well-being, individuals are turning to digital tools for education, tracking, and behavior change support. Large language models like ChatGPT and Gemini have recently emerged as promising components of these tools, capable of generating personalized, conversational, and context-aware sleep guidance.

title: Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Phosphodiesterase-5 Inhibitors: A Systematic Review
creator: Peyton Pinkus, Soroush Farsi, William D. Strickland, Lauren Tong, John L. Dornhoffer, Robert A. Saadi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionSudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) can significantly impact quality of life. Recent studies propose a link between the use of phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (PDE-5is) and SSNHL emergence.ObjectiveTo clarify the relationship between PDE-5i use and the risk of SSNHL development.Data SynthesisFollowing the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statement, two independent reviewers searched the PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases for articles up to December 2023 on hearing loss in PDE-5i users.

title: Comparison of Nasal Mucus Metabolites in Chronic Rhinosinusitis With and Without Polyps and Healthy Controls
creator: Michael F. Armstrong, Kathleen R. Bartemes, Danielle E. Hunter, Marisa D. Griesel, Stephen G. Voss, Garret W. Choby, Carlos D. Pinheiro Neto, John B. Hagan, Rohit D. Divekar, Erin K. O'Brien
description: ObjectiveTo identify differences in nasal mucus metabolites from patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) and chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps (CRSsNP) and healthy controls.Study DesignCross‐sectional.SettingSingle institution tertiary care facility.MethodsPatients were assigned to groups based on the appearance of normal mucosa (control [n = 5]), diseased mucosa ([CRSsNP] [n = 6]), or polypoid mucosa ([CRSwNP] [n = 4]), respectively.

title: 신임 뇌신경영상 섹션 편집장 소개글
creator: 성헌 김
description: 구소 임상교수로 재직 중이다. 백 교수는 뇌신경영상, 두경부영상 및 갑상선영상 분야에서 폭넓은 진료와 연구 경험을 축적해 왔으며, 특히 최신 MRI 기법, 합성 MRI, 초고속 뇌 MRI, 뇌종양 및 전이성 병변의 영상 평가, 뇌혈관질환 및 두경부 질환 영상 분야에서 활발한 연구를 수행해 왔다. 또한 인공지능 및 딥러닝을 활용한 영상 분석과 임상 적용 가능성에 대해서도 지속적인 연구를 이어가고 있다.

title: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Study of Hypopigmented Patches in Trichrome Non-Segmental Vitiligo
creator: Mona Ibrahim Abdel Hafiz, Ghada Abdel Badea Omar, Nafissa Mohamed El-Badawy, Radwa Osama Mohamed Kamel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionVitiligo is a multifactorial autoimmune disease. A comprehensive understanding of the pathogenesis within the trichrome area, particularly of the role of CD8+ and CD4+ T lymphocytes, is crucial to developing effective therapeutic strategies.ObjectivesWe aimed to characterize the distinct histopathological and immunohistochemical features of trichrome non-segmental vitiligo, with a specific focus on CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocyte populations within different pigmentary zones of a single lesion to elucidate the pathogenesis of this vitiligo subtype.MethodsThirty patients with trichrome non-segmental vitiligo were enrolled.

title: Measuring environmental (in)justices: Insights from a systematic literature review on methodological approaches
creator: Jacqueline Loos, Charlotte Gohr, Noelia Zafra-Calvo, Gonzalo Cortés-Capano, Anna Lena Tonninger, Henrik von Wehrden
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryEnvironmental (in)justice research uses various conceptual frameworks and methodological approaches, leading to fragmentation across contexts and disciplines. Our systematic review provides a methodological overview of how environmental (in)justice has been studied in 421 English-language scientific articles. Most studies approach environmental (in)justice from a quantitative and interdisciplinary perspective, primarily using purposive sampling, secondary data, and GIS/remote sensing tools with an emphasis on distributive justice.

title: Serum amyloid a as a high-resolution indicator of mucosal healing in ulcerative colitis
creator: Kotaro Akita, Yoshihiro Yokoyama, Yuta Shimomori, Tomoe Kazama, Masanori Nojima, Hiroshi Nakase
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEndoscopy is the standard for assessing mucosal activity in ulcerative colitis (UC), but reliable biomarkers are needed. This study evaluated serum amyloid A (SAA) as a potential biomarker by comparing it with established markers in UC.MethodsWe retrospectively evaluated 182 patients with UC who underwent blood and stool testing within 14 days of colonoscopy at a tertiary care hospital between April 2017 and January 2025. Patients were classified into 4 groups according to the Mayo Endoscopic Subscore (MES).

title: Artificial Intelligence Chest X-Ray Opportunistic Screening Model for Coronary Artery Calcium Deposition: A Multi-Objective Model With Multimodal Data Fusion
creator: Jiwoong Jeong, Chieh-Ju Chao, Reza Arsanjani, Chadi Ayoub, Steven J Lester, Milagros Pereyra, Ebram F Said, Michael Roarke, Cecilia Tagle-Cornell, Laura M Koepke, Yi-Lin Tsai, Chen Jung-Hsuan, Chun-Chin Chang, Juan M Farina, Hari Trivedi, Bhavik N Patel, Imon Banerjee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo create an opportunistic screening model to predict coronary calcium burden and associated cardiovascular risk using only commonly available frontal chest x-rays (CXR) and patient demographics.Patients and MethodsWe proposed a novel multitask learning framework and trained a model using 2121 patients with paired gated computed tomography scans and CXR images internally (Mayo Clinic) from January 1, 2012, to December 31, 2022, with coronary artery calcification (CAC) scores (0, 1-99, and 100+) as ground truths.

title: Mental Health Challenges of Iranian Nurses in War: Letter to the Editor
creator: Amir Hossein Goudarzian, Tahereh Yaghoubi
description: ological consequences for nurses, including depression and anxiety disorders (2, 3). The 12-day war between Iran and Israel, although short in duration, had significant psychological effects on people, especially nurses. Moreover, considering the risk of the war restarting, this important group in the country faces many threats.

title: Evaluation of Stress, IL-18, and IL-22 Levels and Their Interrelationships in Patients with Seborrheic Dermatitis
creator: Lütfi Işık, Müzeyyen Gönül, Selda Pelin Kartal, Funda Güçel
description: IntroductionSeborrheic dermatitis (SD) is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis with multifactorial pathogenesis. Cytokines such as IL-18 and IL-22 are implicated in inflammatory and stress-related pathways, but their roles in SD remain unclear.ObjectivesTo investigate serum IL-18 and IL-22 levels in SD patients, evaluate their relationship with disease severity and perceived stress, and explore their potential relevance to SD pathophysiology.

title: Advanced recovery of bioactive polyphenols: integrated optimization of drying and green extraction for avocado seed by-products
creator: Jorge G Figueroa, Isabel Borrás-Linares, Jesús Lozano-Sánchez, Rosa Quirantes-Piné, Antonio Segura-Carretero
description: Response surface methodology using a central composite design was applied to optimize the accelerated solvent extraction (ASE) of phenolic compounds from avocado seed and seed coat by-products. The optimal extraction conditions for both matrices were achieved at 200 °C using as extractant solvent a mixture of ethanol:water (50,50, v/v).

title: Ventral pallidum efferent pathways via mediodorsal thalamus and lateral habenula mediate default mode network regulation
creator: Epistimi-Anna Makedona, Mu-En Kuo, Michael Harvey, Gregor Rainer
description: SummaryTransitions between internal and external focus are fundamental to cognition. These shifts depend on the modulation of the default mode network (DMN), of which the ventral pallidum (VP) is a key subcortical node. Here, we examine which VP efferent pathways mediate these transitions, using projection and cell type specific optogenetic silencing.

title: Arthralgia in Patients with Chronic Plaque Psoriasis: Practical Insights for Dermatologists
creator: Paolo Gisondi, Francesco Bellinato, Enzo Errichetti, Luca Idolazzi, Alen Zabotti
description: IntroductionArthralgia is a frequent but often overlooked symptom in patients with psoriasis (PsO) and may represent an early manifestation of psoriatic arthritis (PsA).ObjectiveTo provide a practical overview aiming to support dermatologists in the identification and management of arthralgia in PsO.

title: Selective modification of glycoprotein substrates by GnT-V in mouse kidney
creator: Reina F Osuka, Masamichi Nagae, Miyako Nakano, Shunsuke Tanigawa, Kazuya Ono, Yudai Tsuji, Yoshimasa Ito, Kazuo Takahashi, Ryuichi Nishinakamura, Yasuhiko Kizuka
description: SummaryN-Glycans are modified by various glycosyltransferases in a protein-selective manner and critically control protein functions. Here, we investigated the mechanisms for the protein substrate selectivity of N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase-V (GnT-V or MGAT5) in the mouse kidney. Through lectin-assisted proteomics, two metalloproteases on the apical surface of tubules, alanyl aminopeptidase (ANPEP) and meprin α (MEP1A), were identified as the major GnT-V substrates.

title: Time Well Spent? Time Use for Health Information Management Across Home Care Roles: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study in Finland
creator: Inka Sylgren, Esa Jämsen, Paulus Torkki
description: Introduction:The growing number of older adults with multiple long-term conditions increases the need for better vertical integration of providers, especially in home care. Ensuring information continuity and care coordination is essential but remains time-consuming for home care professionals (HCPs).Methodology:This study aimed to quantify HCPs’ time on health information management (HIM) and examine factors associated with this time use.

title: The Prevalence of Entamoeba gingivalis and Trichomonas tenax in Relation to Periodontal Disease among Patients Attending Dental Clinics in Urmia, Iran: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Yahya Azadeh, Shahram Khademvatan, Zahra Goharfar, Shokoufeh Shahrabi-Farahani, Rasool Jafari
description: Background:We aimed to determine the prevalence of Entamoeba gingivalis and Trichomonas tenax in relation to periodontitis in Urmia, Northwestern Iran, in 2022.Methods:Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) samples were collected from 133 patients and analyzed using microscopic and molecular techniques to identify parasites. Data were analyzed using SPSS software and Chi-square and Fisher’s exact test.Results:42.1% of patients were infected with E.

title: Silybum marianum and Trigonella foenum-graecum Exhibit Moderate In Vitro Antimalarial Properties against Plasmodium knowlesi
creator: Norsyafiqah Binti Ahmad Safri, Fei Wen Cheong, Nur Zulaikha Zulkefli, Abolghasem Siyadatpanah, Roghayeh Norouzi, Yee Ling Lau
description: Background:Malaria remains a major global health burden, with increasing challenges posed by drug-resistant Plasmodium species. Another emerging threat is Plasmodium knowlesi, a zoonotic parasite responsible for rising human infections in Southeast Asia, particularly Malaysia. This study investigates the in vitro antimalarial activity of Silybum marianum (milk thistle) and Trigonella foenum-graecum (fenugreek) seed extracts against P.

title: DJ-1-Binding Compound Improves Peripheral Nerve Injury in the Spinal Dorsal Horn by Restraining STAT3-Mediated Neurotoxic Reactive Astrocytes
creator: Shengtao Wang, Jieyong Cai, Qingsong Zhou, Ming Zhao, Wei Zhou
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Astrocytes are significantly activated after peripheral nerve injury (PNI) and affect the nerve repair by mediating neuroinflammation. DJ-1 is highly expressed in astrocytes, and its binding compounds exert significant neuroprotective effects by regulating antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses. This study is designed to investigate the therapeutic effects of DJ-1-binding compound P-DJ-1A in a rat PNI model induced by spared nerve injury (SNI) surgery.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Urine Test Strip and Morbidity Indicators of Urogenital Schistosomiasis in Kwara State, Nigeria
creator: Olufunke Adenike Opeyemi, Iyabo Adepeju Simon-Oke, Titus Adeniyi Olusi
description: Background:The efficient management of schistosomiasis depends on the rapid and accurate diagnosis of infection. Rapid diagnostic tests are essential for identifying morbidity markers of urogenital schistosomiasis.Methods:A total of 1,341 urine samples collected from school-age pupils in Kwara State were screened for Schistosoma haematobium eggs using the syringe filtration method.

title: Utility of a Simulation-Based Mastery Learning Curriculum for Teaching Labor and Delivery Procedures
creator: Gabrielle K Smith, Shivani Arza, Christopher S Ennen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Introduction: Mastering obstetric procedural skills is difficult. These skills require a tactile understanding of pelvic anatomy, must be performed in real time, and learners’ performance cannot be visualized by coaches, making it difficult to obtain feedback. Simulation-based mastery learning (SBML), a competency-based approach in which learners acquire skills to predefined standards in an environment free of risks, is a potential solution to this dilemma.

title: Idiopathic Spinal Cord Infarction: A Case Report of an Unusual Diagnostic Dilemma and Therapeutic Challenge
creator: Safae Dehbi, Manal Arfaoui, Bouchra Armel, Hamza El Hamzaoui, Mustapha Alilou
description: We report a 23-year-old male patient with acute respiratory distress and progressive quadriparesis following a football match, without preceding trauma. Initial imaging and cerebrospinal fluid studies were unremarkable. Spinal MRI revealed an infarction in the anterior spinal artery territory (C2-D1). Extensive etiological workup was negative. Despite treatment with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin, neurological recovery was limited.

title: Molecular Detection and Subtype Characterization of Blastocystis spp. in Symptomatic Children Using PCR and Sequencing
creator: Samaneh Boulaghi, Amirali Reihani, BiBi Razieh Hosseini Farash, Yousef Sharifi, Omid Ahmadi, Alireza Samadi, Ghodratollah Salehi Sangani, Mohsen Najjari, Fariba Berenji, Mehdi Zarean
description: Background:Blastocystis spp. is a globally distributed intestinal protozoan that infects humans and various animals. This protozoan is a common pathogen among humans and animals and can be transmitted from animal species to humans. Therefore, the present study aimed to identify and characterize Blastocystis sub-types in children with gastrointestinal symptoms using PCR and sequencing.

title: Return to Sport After Excision of Os Trigonum of Talus in Athletes
creator: Alexis Watson, Gokul Kalyanasundaram, Alexander J. Wahl, Wen Chao
description: Background:Os trigonum syndrome is a common cause of posterior ankle pain in athletes performing repetitive hyper‑plantarflexion of the ankle. An accessory bone posterior to the talus, the os trigonum, may remain unfused or form a Stieda process, leading to pain from overuse, trauma, or impingement. Failure of conservative management often requires surgical excision.

title: Frontal Sinus Endoscopy in Combined Approach Frontal Sinusotomy for Post-COVID-19 Mucormycosis
creator: Sangeetha T Sachithanandam
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionSinonasal mucormycosis is a fulminant, life-threatening, invasive fungal infection that emerged as an epidemic during the second wave of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic in developing countries such as India. The objective of this study is to evaluate the role of frontal sinus endoscopy, to assess the disease extent in invasive frontal sinus mucormycosis, and to study the effectiveness of a combined approach involving endoscopic and external frontal sinusotomy among post-COVID-19 invasive sinonasal mucormycosis involving frontal sinuses.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included

title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling identifies YY1 as a key regulator of fibroblast plasticity in hypertrophic scar formation
creator: Qian Yu, Zonglin Huang, Lei Cai, Yanze Lv, Lianzhao Wang, Huanhuan Wu, Qiang Dai, Zikai Qiu, Zhigang Yang, Xin Fu, Ran Xiao
description: BackgroundHypertrophic scars (HTSs) are characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition and impaired scar remodelling. Fibroblasts are central to HTS pathogenesis, yet clinical strategies remain limited by an incomplete understanding of fibroblast heterogeneity and transcriptional regulation. This study aimed to identify a key fibroblast subpopulation and its regulatory transcription factors to address this translational gap.

title: True Intra-Articular Lipoma of the Knee: A Case Report
creator: Hugo Vaz dos Santos, Raquel Costa, André Castanheira, Luís Barbosa, Luís Machado
description: Although lipomas are the most common benign soft tissue tumor, very few cases of true intra-articular lipomas have been described. They are usually small in size and located at the knee. The differential diagnosis of an intra-articular lipomatous mass is made between lipoma arborescens and synovial lipoma.

title: Molecular Characterization of Human Papilloma Virus in Carcinoma Cervix along with Screening of Risk Factors and their Regional Comparison
creator: Arti Agrawal, Astha, Parul Garg, Gargi Tyagi, Pooja Agrawal, Urvashi Verma, Ruchika Garg, Ayushi Gupta, Surabhi Gupta
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction: Background:The threat of cervical carcinoma is still a major public health challenge in low- and middle-income countries, including India. In this context, disparate findings about HPV genotypes are reported from different regions of India.

title: Libraries as Spaces for Inclusive Communities: A Literature Review
creator: Salma Paola Rodríguez Poveda, Ana Dolores Vargas Sánchez, Diego Efrén Rodríguez Cárdenas, Cesar Augusto Niño Hernández, Christine Mady, Oluwayemi IbukunOluwa Odularu, Weerayut Weerayut Seekhunlio, Weerayut Weerayut Seekhunlio, Ana Dolores Vargas Sánchez, Ida Fajar Priyanto
description: Recognizing and appreciating the diversity of people around the world is a necessary step in achieving equality for all. The opening of equitable chances for society as a whole is one of the ways in which libraries contribute to the reduction of the exclusion gap. Despite their expanding relevance, institutions like libraries demonstrate inconsistent patterns of integration and research.

title: Endometrial Hemangiomatous Polyp Presenting as Postmenopausal Bleeding and Mimicking Uterine Malignancy: A Rare Diagnostic Challenge
creator: Akriri Jindal, Ankita Soni, Gargi Kapatia, Manjit Kaur Rana
description: Vascular lesions of the uterus are rare, yet remain a potential differential diagnosis for the etiologies of postmenopausal bleeding. Hemangiomas of the uterus are benign neoplasms that can occur in any age group, with a predilection for reproductive age females. It is a benign vascular tumor and should be kept as a differential diagnosis for uterine endometrial mass lesions.

title: Retinal Pigment Epithelial Detachment Following Topical Travoprost Therapy
creator: Meghana Narapareddy, Narayanan Balakrishnan, Mohamed Anjum Iqbal
description: Prostaglandin analogs, including travoprost, are widely used to lower intraocular pressure in primary open-angle glaucoma. While generally safe, rare posterior segment changes have been reported. Retinal pigment epithelial detachment (RPED) associated with travoprost is uncommon and poorly documented. We report three patients who developed serous RPED shortly after initiating topical travoprost, none of whom had preexisting macular disease.

title: Assessment of the Risk of Venous Thromboembolism in Overcrowded Shelters: A Geospatial and Statistical Analysis of the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake
creator: Hisao Nakai, Ryo Horiike, Tomoya Itatani, Mayu Tokuoka, Ayuka Maeda, Haruka Iida, Yoshie Aoki, Daisuke Toda, Masato Oe
description: Background: In recent years, Japan has frequently experienced natural disasters, including major earthquakes and extreme weather events linked to climate change, forcing many people into sheltered lives. These overcrowded environments are known to increase the risk of life-threatening venous thromboembolism (VTE). The 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake (NPE) similarly compelled numerous residents into prolonged shelter living.

title: Comparative analyses of Alzheimer's disease blood biomarkers and cognitive domains
creator: Deirdre M O'Shea, James E Galvin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). INTRODUCTIONWhether Alzheimer's disease (AD) blood biomarker–cognition associations differ across cognitive domains, analytic context, and biomarker modeling strategy in population‐based cohorts is unclear.METHODSIn 1170 older adults from the Health and Retirement Study Harmonized Cognitive Assessment Protocol (HRS‐HCAP), we examined cross‐sectional (2016) and prospective (2016 to 2022) associations of blood phosphorylated tau at threonine 181 (p‐tau181), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light (NfL), and amyloid beta 42/40 ratio (Aβ42/40) with memory, executive function, language, visuospatial ability, and global cognition using individual‐biomarker, principal component

title: Corneal Endothelial Pathology and Thickening in Early Diabetes Mellitus
creator: Konstantin Gushansky, Anry Pitchkhadze
description: PurposeTo compare endothelial cell properties and central corneal thickness (CCT) between nondiabetic individuals and patients with early type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) with good glycemic control.MethodsThis retrospective case-control study included patients diagnosed with T2DM within the past 10 years and nondiabetic individuals.

title: Unusual Presentation of Giant Cell Arteritis With Localised Temporal Artery Aneurysm
creator: Syed A Ahmad, Niazi Khairi, Meeran Hussain, Mark Lloyd
description: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is a granulomatous vasculitis of medium and large-sized arteries occurring in older adults. Skip lesions are well described, but to our knowledge, localised aneurysm formation in the context of normocalcaemic, non-progressive GCA has not been reported.

title: Endoscopic Endonasal Optic Nerve Decompression for Traumatic Optic Neuropathy: A Systematic Review
creator: Babak Ganjeifar, Seyed Reza Ahmadi Koupaei, Ali Moradi
description: IntroductionTraumatic optic neuropathy (TON) is an acute injury to the optic nerve caused by direct or indirect trauma, often resulting in vision loss. Endoscopic transsphenoidal optic nerve decompression (EOND) is a minimally invasive technique designed to relieve pressure on the optic nerve. This systematic review evaluates the efficacy, safety, and visual outcomes of EOND in patients with TON.

title: On the Brink of the Abyss: Managing More Than 25 Liters of Blood Loss During a Cesarean Section
creator: Strahil N Kotsev, Nadine B Nour, Muhammad Sharif Allah Dad, Zainab Saeed
description: We present a case of placenta percreta in which the patient experienced an intraoperative blood loss exceeding 25 liters. To our knowledge, this represents the highest volume of hemorrhage reported during cesarean section (CS) in which the patient survived. Injuries of the iliac vessels, urinary bladder, and ureter had to be dealt with intraoperatively.

title: Response to comments on ‘Staff experiences of percutaneous tracheostomy in intensive care: challenges, complications and potential solutions’
creator: M. Moran, A. Goryanyy, B. McGrath, A. Haron, G. Cooper, A. Weightman, C. Jay, C. Shelton
description: sed in our interviews, and in line with their findings, participants recognised its value in identifying blood vessels, selecting the optimal puncture site and informing decisions between percutaneous and surgical tracheostomy [2]. Participants in our study noted that ICU clinicians are proficient with ultrasound (for vascular access and point‐of‐care imaging) [2]. However, its application in PDT presents some challenges.

title: Evaluation of c-Myc in odontogenic cysts and tumours—An immunohistochemical study
creator: Soujanya Pinisetti, Nallagangula L. Vinaya, Praveena Adusumilli, Suresh Babburi, Aparna Venigalla, Ajay Benarjee
description: Objective:To assess immunohistochemically the presence of c-Myc both qualitatively and quantitatively in odontogenic cysts and tumours and to correlate the results with biological behaviour of these lesions.Materials and Methods:Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded blocks of odontogenic cysts and tumours were retrieved from institutional archives.

title: Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Maxillofacial Surgery and Evidence-Based Practice: A Systematic Review
creator: Gayatri Moharana, Rajat Mohanty, Spandita Das
description: Antibiotic prophylaxis is defined as the intentional administration of antibiotics with the goal of preventing infection prior to the occurrence of contamination by surgical incision. So, it can either be given before the procedure or after the surgery to prevent infection.

title: Medium-term biological variation of sodium, potassium and chloride in whole blood in cohorts of healthy individuals and hemodialysis patients
creator: Berta Sufrate-Vergara, Isabel Moreno-Parro, Pilar Fernández-Calle, Aasne K. Aarsand, Sverre Sandberg, Anna Carobene, Roberto Mora Corcovado, Daniel Prieto Arribas, Antonio Buño Soto, Paloma Oliver, Blanca Beumer Prieto, José Manuel Hidalgo, Ana Cristina Mendoza, Sara Julia Molina, Nuria Alert, Ana M
description: ObjectivesBiological variation (BV) refers to the fluctuation of the concentration of a measurand around its homeostatic set-point. While BV has been extensively studied in healthy populations, robust data for patients with chronic diseases, particularly using whole blood measurements, remain scarce.

title: New insights in submucous fibrosis: Nicotine dependence and nutritional assessment
creator: Rishabh Sachdeva, Aadithya B. Urs, Priya Kumar, Bhawna Mahajan
description: Background:Submucous fibrosis (SMF) is an oral potentially malignant disorder with a high risk of malignant transformation, primarily associated with areca nut use and tobacco consumption.Aim:This study aimed to evaluate the correlation of nicotine dependence and nutritional status with disease severity in patients with SMF.Settings and Design:This observational study was conducted among 70 SMF patients subdivided on clinical and histological classification.

title: Prevention and Post-extubation Screening of Perioperative Traumatic Dental Injury in Pediatric Anesthesia
creator: Iqra Ahmad, Christof N Gault, Zeyad Kamar, Sharif Mohamed
description: Adenotonsillectomy is a routine pediatric procedure often requiring general anesthesia and endotracheal intubation. While generally safe, traumatic dental injuries (TDIs) represent a significant and often under-recognized complication, particularly in children with mobile primary teeth and anatomical risk factors. Although preoperative dental evaluations are commonly performed, current anesthetic protocols rarely include post-extubation dental screening.

title: Cryptosporidium-Induced Myocarditis: A Unique Case Study
creator: Fatima Eltayeb, Emily Rawlinson, Raymol Keelan
description: Myocarditis is the inflammation of the myocardium. While viral infections commonly cause it, we present a unique case of Cryptosporidium-induced myocarditis in an immunocompetent individual. A 33-year-old man presenting with acute chest pain and loose stools was found to have troponin levels of over 1,000 ng/L.

title: Intraocular pressure and optic disc cupping in school-aged children: An epidemiological study in Taiwan
creator: Hsiao-Lien Chang, Yen-Ching Lin, Yun Hsia, Jehn-Yu Huang, Bo-I Kuo, Tsing-Hong Wang, Chao-Wen Lin, Yao-Lin Liu, Tzu-Hsun Tsai, I-Jong Wang, Chien-Chia Su
description: PURPOSE:The purpose of the study was to investigate intraocular pressure (IOP), cup-to-disc ratio (CDR), and ocular biometrics in school-aged children in Taiwan and to evaluate the factors associated with IOP and CDR.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This nationwide school-based study prospectively enrolled children aged 6–18 years.

title: Species-specific marker development for accurate identification of three red algae (Grateloupia asiatica, Pachymeniopsis lanceolata and Polyopes affinis) based on complete organelle genomes
creator: Yong Jin Lee, Yeon Mi Kim, Cheol Min Kim, Sung-Je Choi, Cheol Seong Jang
description: Red alga species in the phylum Rhodophyta are ecologically and economically important, which are widely used as food and medicinal products because they are rich in bioactive compounds. Unfortunately, researchers often meet challenges in identifying red algal species and understanding the evolutionary relationship among them. Shooting away these limitations necessitates detailed genomic studies, including those of cellular organelles.

title: Noise Reduction Protocol and its Impact on Sleep Quality and Delirium Among ICU Patients in A Tertiary Care Hospital in New Delhi
creator: Himanshi Lakra, Ruchi Gupta, Raminder Kalra, Arshdeep S Chadha, Sumit Ray
description: IntroductionNoise in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) is a major environmental concern affecting patient outcomes. ICUs frequently record excessive noise from alarms, equipment, staff activity, and procedures—often surpassing the WHO limits of 35 dB by day and 30 dB at night. Sustained exposure disrupts sleep and is closely linked to ICU delirium.

title: Evaluating the Effects of Pesticides Residues on Seminal Fluid Antioxidants Status and Semen Parameters among Males with Infertility at a Tertiary Hospital in Nigeria
creator: Waliu O. Oladosu, Saheed O. Jimoh, Oseni Ismaila, Adewale M. Alayo, Ganiyu A. Gbagirimojo, Oyewo Rasaki Adewale, Adekunle B. Okesina
description: Aims:To evaluate the impacts of seminal concentrations of selected pesticide residues on SFA parameters and seminal antioxidants in men with abnormal sperm parameters.Settings and Design:An analytical cross-sectional study of consenting infertile male patients, with at least one abnormal seminal fluid analysis (SFA) parameter, at a tertiary Health Centre.

title: Synergistic Effects of Thread Lifting, Autologous Fat Grafting, and Multi-Modal Laser Therapy in Facial Rejuvenation
creator: Naci Celik
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundFacial aging is a multifactorial process involving tissue descent, volume depletion, and dermal degeneration. Minimally invasive modalities like thread lifting, autologous fat grafting, and laser treatments address different aging components. However, their synergistic impact remains underexplored.ObjectivesThe aim of the author of this study is to assess the clinical efficacy and histologic rationale of combining permanent thread lifting, autologous fat grafting, and nonablative laser therapy for comprehensive facial rejuvenation.MethodsIn this retrospective study, a total of 65 female patients (aged 31-60, Fitzpatrick skin types

title: Impact of Admission Blood Glucose on 48-Hour Mortality and Complications in Non-Diabetic Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction
creator: Priyam Vallabhbhai Bhil, Gunjan Chanchlani
description: IntroductionStress hyperglycemia is a common physiological response during acute myocardial infarction (AMI), even among non-diabetic patients. Elevated admission blood glucose has been associated with early mortality, ventricular arrhythmias, and major adverse cardiac events (MACE). However, data from small, resource-limited intensive care settings remain limited.

title: Relationships between Musculoskeletal Disorders, Sleep Impairment, and Cardiorespiratory Fitness among Adolescents Aged 15-19 Years in Douala, Cameroon: A Cross-sectional Study
creator: Jerson Mekoulou Ndongo, William Mbang Bian, Abraham Sylvin Mefiré Rengou, Hassane Malam Moussa Ahmet, Elysée Claude Bika Lele, Emmanuel Guilou Njimongna Njoya, Samuel Honoré Mandengue, Bienvenu Bongue, Peguy Brice Assomo Ndemba, Clarisse Noel Ayina Ayina
description: Background:Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are a leading cause of disability worldwide. While poor sleep quality (PSQ) is considered an important risk factor for pain, high cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) is a somewhat controversial protective factor. The present study investigated the association between MSDs, PSQ, and CRF in adolescents.

title: Cochlear endoplasmic reticulum stress causes connexin 26 degradation is involved in age-related hearing loss
creator: Xue Bai, Bing Liao, Wen-Hui Hu, Mei-Qun Wang, Yu Sun, Xu-Bo Chen, Kai Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryAge-related hearing loss (ARHL) represents a progressive auditory disorder. Growing evidence indicates that degradation of connexin 26 (Cx26) in cochlear may constitute one of the pathogenic mechanisms in ARHL. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying age-related Cx26 degradation remain unclear. We systematically analyzed Cx26 expression patterns in C57BL/6J mice across different age groups and confirmed an age-dependent downregulation of Cx26 in the mouse cochlea.

title: Hs-Troponin I, as a Predictive Marker of Cardiovascular Instability in Sepsis and Septic Shock–A Prospective Observational Study
creator: Jyothsna Yadav Chintala, DVNL Prathyusha, Ganshyam Jagathkar
description: IntroductionSepsis and septic shock are leading causes of mortality in intensive care units (ICUs), often complicated by myocardial dysfunction. High-sensitivity troponin I (hs-TnI) has emerged as a sensitive biomarker for myocardial injury, but its role in predicting cardiovascular instability and mortality in sepsis requires further investigation.

title: A cluster of co-occurring cases of leptospirosis and brucellosis in a pastoral community of dairy farmers, India, 2023–2024: an epidemiological investigation
creator: Farida Khatoon, Srividya K Vedachalam, Sushma Choudhary, Subodh Kumar Joshi, Pankaj Kumar Jain, Yogesh Bahurupi, Fareeduzzafar,, Meenu Singh, Pankaj Kumar Singh
description: ObjectiveA cluster of leptospirosis and brucellosis cases in a semi-nomadic, pastoral community was reported in October 2023 from Village A, Uttarakhand State, India. This cluster was investigated to describe the epidemiology and potential exposures.MethodsSuspected cases were residents with sudden-onset fever or myalgia occurring from 1 August 2023 to 7 January 2024; confirmed cases were suspected cases with laboratory confirmation.

title: Predictive Ability of Breath Holding Time for Expansion of Hematoma in Patients with Intracerebral Haemorrhagic Stroke Undergoing Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction – A Prospective Observational Study
creator: Geetanshu Gupta
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionA common and serious complication of Intra-Cerebral Hemorrhage(ICH) within the first 24 hours is hematoma expansion, a major driver of poor outcomes. Although intensive Blood Pressure(BP) reduction can help, it presents important challenges. Bedside assessment of cerebrovasomotor response using the Breath-Holding Index (BHI) via Transcranial Doppler(TCD) offers a promising, noninvasive method to identify patients at highest risk and those most likely to benefit from aggressive therapy.

title: A conformal self-healing organogel with synergistic supramolecular crosslinking
creator: Yiyang Gao, Qihao Jiang, Jing Chen, Yanming Liu
description: SummaryThrough molecular design, this study developed a conformal self-healing organogel (CSHO) via molecular design. Utilizing acryloylmorpholine (ACMO) and hydroxyethyl acrylamide (HEAA) as monomers, tributyl citrate (TBC) as the solvent, and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) as an electrolyte salt, the organogel was polymerized by UV curing.

title: Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs): Risk Assessment in Collegiate Female Athletes
creator: Kelsea Nunes, Kelly Pritchett, Robert Pritchett, Katy Williams
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Alterations in energy intake (EI) and exercise energy expenditure (EEE) may increase low energy availability (LEA) risk in Division II female collegiate athletes. Chronic LEA can transition to problematic LEA, leading to Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs). The purpose of this study was to assess the current severity and prevalence of REDs using the REDs Clinical Assessment Tool 2 (CAT2) and the Female Athlete Triad Cumulative Risk Assessment tool (FAT CRA) in Division II collegiate female ball sport athletes.

title: Concomitant arthroscopy during valgus‐producing high tibial osteotomy does not demonstrate consistent additional clinical benefit despite improved cartilage findings: A systematic review of comparative studies
creator: Dave Osinachukwu Duru, Ebenezeer Mussie, Taimoor A. Sehgol, Yuta Nakanishi, Ryan M. Degen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026).
